product_title: Ritche 22mm Black Stainless Steel Bracelet Watch Band Strap Pebble Time/Pebble Classic
review_headline: - It keeps my wrist cool. Cons
review_body:
The quality of this product reflects the price. I got this to replace the rubber/silicone band that came with my original Pebble.

Pros:
- It gets the job done.
- The clasp holds very well despite my constant tendency to play with it. I've never had it fall off accidentally.
- Without too much inspection, it looks fair quality.
- Personal, but it goes very well with my black Pebble.
- It keeps my wrist cool.

Cons:
- It's noisy, more so than other metal bands I've worn from other watches.
- Specifically for Pebble users, the vibration of your watch will cause an obnoxious noise from the links shaking.
- There were quite a few scuffs on one side of the chain. It is clear the paint is thin and the manufacturer's attention to detail is lacking.
- The pins for size readjustment gave me a lot of trouble getting out.

I give 4 stars merely because of the quality for the price, and the scuffs on the side that could have been handled better.

product_title: Stuhrling Original Men's 718.04 Aquadiver Manta Ray Swiss Quartz Date Professional Diver Black Watch
review_headline: Good dive watch for the price and a quartz movement
review_body:
I bought this watch looking for a solid diving watch with a rubber strap and decent movement, so I could wear it in the pool or ocean. I found exactly that with this watch. While not the greatest watch company around, Stuhrling does have Swiss heritage, although they are now manufactured in New York after the brand was reestablished in 1999.

The watch comes in a huge rectangular shaped bright orange box, with all the Stuhrling paper work and warranty information. The presentation of the box seems to be a bit much for a watch of this quality, but it gives it an added touch. The watch itself has great weight; not to heavy, but solid enough to ensure the wearer that it's going to stay on one's wrist. The Bezel rotates uni-directionally for diving purposes and is made of solid coated steel. The orange paint on the bezel is a nice tough which is accented by the orange outlined minute hand. The hour markers and hands of the watch are all very luminous, making the time easy to read at night. The strap of the watch is my only complaint with this watch. The description says that the strap is a "men's standard" and I am aware that this can be any length between 7.25 - 7.70, but this strap was closer to a men's long length. Now, to be fair I have wrists that are 6.5 in around, so it was no surprise that the strap was long, but it was so long that I couldn't even buckle the strap on the last hole, I had to punch my own hole. As a result of this I decided to buy a new strap (which can be found here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00SSW0Q7Y?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00). The new strap gave the watch a new look and was much more durable than the original.
The movement of the watch is touted as a "Swiss Quartz" movement, with the decent Ronda 515 quartz movement at the heart. As to its accuracy, the watch has gained about 7-8 seconds since I bought the watch (over a month ago) so it's not too bad. The crown is screw down (standard for dive watches) and as far as I can tell, has worked perfectly as I have taken the watch swimming twice and worn it twice at the water park. Overall, I would recommend this watch to anyone looking for a decent dive watch that is relatively reasonably priced. For a better option with an automatic movement and killer price, look into the Jiusko Deep Sea series.ndard for dive watches) and as far as I can tell, has worked perfectly as I have taken the watch swimming twice and worn it twice at the water park. Overall, I would recommend this watch to anyone looking for a decent dive watch that is relatively reasonably priced. For a better option with an automatic movement and killer price, look into the Jiusko Deep Sea series.

product_title: BOS Men's Automatic Mechanical Multi-function Stainless Steel Black Dial Wrist Watch 9001G
review_body: This really is a cool looking watch.  It has a nice weight to it and "feels" well made.  There is some question as to quality control, however.  I had to send it back twice before I got one that I was satisfied with.  It's an automatic watch, but the auto-wind rotor on the first one didn't really work.  It was too loose.  Although you could see it turning a gear, it wasn't actually winding the spring.  I literally spun it in my hand for two minutes and still nothing.  The rotor on the replacement that I QUICKLY received was also too loose, but worked a little better.  However, the bezel had an area on it that looked as if it was rubbed with sandpaper.  Kind of hard to overlook considering the glossy/shiny look of the watch and ceramic bezel.  I also returned that one.  The third one looks and functions great.  HOWEVER, the stem/crown isn't entirely straight.  It's pretty noticeable when manually winding or setting the time because the crown wobbles.  It's a minor annoyance (at least for me) and doesn't detract from the look/function of the watch, so I've decided to keep this one.  It keeps great time and really does look and feel awesome for the price.  I don't think I would take the chance ordering this from an international seller or from any seller that doesn't have free return shipping...unless you're planning on actually using the 3rd party Amazon watch warranty that automatically gets added.  For the price and the ease of return/replacing with amazon prime, I think this watch is cool enough give it a shot.  I have a collection of about 35 watches, so I may never really be able to speak to how well it holds up to consistent use...but so far so good...

product_title: Bertucci Men's 12022 A-2T Original Classics Durable Titanium Field Watch
review_body:
I first purchased the A1-S because it was the first watch I had purchased in years and I was thinking that watches nowadays are just too big. My wrist is about 6.75" I loved the watch, but after a while thought a little bigger would be perfect. I was right. I find the 40mm diameter to look just right on my wrist.
I love the fixed lug/spring bars on this watch that make it seem more durable and more adventure minded. The black nylon strap is thick and not overly flexible. I like the way it feels on the wrist, besides which, it takes about 10 seconds to change to another nato band, and as a result gives you tremendous style flexibility. I also prefer the 3 ring Zulu or RAF style of the band much more than the five ring bands that are often found with field watches. It gives you more flexibility in positioning the watch relative to the band.
I've had the watch for several months now. I've worn it swimming, in the shower, at work. It still looks new. The mineral glass is flawless. The only extremely small beef I have with the watch is that the second hand doesn't precisely line up with the tick marks. A minor point, and one I can easily overlook considering the price.
I feel like Bertucci is my daily workhorse watch. My next Bertucci will be the Automatic A3-T.

product_title: Citizen Eco-Drive Men's Promaster Analog-Digital Watch With Black Silicone Band (Model: JZ1065-13E)
review_body:
It's big, it's thick, it's heavy, it's attractive, it reeks of quality, it's an Eco-Drive, I love it! - With reservations.
I have never owned a digital display watch, I figured a dual display would be a great way to wade into the world of digital time pieces.
I quickly found that the analog time display renders the digital display pretty much useless while the minute hand is traveling from 10 minutes to 20 minutes, or when the hour hand is traveling from 2 to 4, which translates to the digital display being obstructed around 4 out of every 12 hours. Dual display is a great concept, but with the analog display obstructing the digital display 1/3 of the time, the practicality of the dual display concept diminishes.
Don't even consider using the chronograph, timer, checking the date or finding the digital time when the analog time is 2:20 (see picture #1).
When unobstructed, the digital display is extremely readable and useful (see picture #2). A back light would be a great addition to the display.
The perpetual calendar is wonderful, eliminating those maddening short month adjustments, now if we can just get rid of those pesky DST adjustments. :-)
The three buttons that control the digital display functions are large and easy to manipulate, which also makes them easy to be accidentally manipulated.

The analog display is outstanding, with large white hands and white block hour indicators on the black background. The hands and hour indicators are illuminated, and my experience has been that with a good dose of light, the illumination remains distinguishable into 5 - 6 hours of darkness.
The bright red second hand is totally out of place, making it easy to spot and follow - I love it!

The watch band is a true plus, some sort of a rubbery compound, offering a little stretch, along with softness, and durability that you don't get with a leather band. The band doesn't absorb moisture/sweat, thus you don't get the rot/stench associated with leather bands, resulting in the JZ1065 being my summer watch. An old soft toothbrush and water will remove any gunk from the band and the watch, returning the JZ1065 to a like new status.

I can't rate the alarm because I can't hear it. My "Golden Years Ears" no longer pick up the frequency of the alarm, but my early teen grandsons can hear the alarm in a different room, so the alarm apparently performs quite well.

Bottom line: The JZ1065 is the most expensive watch I have ever or will ever purchase, and even with the periodic obstruction of the digital display, I would purchase it again. It is my third Eco-Drive, and just as with my previous two (BM8242 & AO9023), it is classy, reeks quality, keeps perfect time, looks good, feels good and doesn't ask for its battery to be changed - just show it the light!

product_title: Casio Men's PAW2000-1CR "Pathfinder" Digital Watch with Black Band
review_body:
PRG-200 it's the same model than PAW-200 but without hour signal reception.

PROS:
- To be a Protrek is very stylish, thin (11 mm), and light weight. Admits any 22 mm strap so it's very customizable.
- It's solar powered.
- Has many functions and all of them are reasonably accurate.

CONS:
1) Usability of some functions.
-Compass: Direction can vary up to 15 degrees if not placed perfectly horizontal.
- Alarms: Very low tone that only sounds for 10 seconds. No snooze function. You cannot rely on it to wake up in the morning.
- EL light: Very tricky to read the compass at night as compass reading frezzes when light is on.
2) Complex settings:
- Need the manual to set some city parameters or to reset barometer to factory default values. It's very usefull to download a PDF copy into your smartphone.

I WISH...:
- Louder alarm tone and snooze function.
- Two city settings (origin and destination) and an easy way to change between them.
- EL light to switch on while pressing any button in the dark (solar cell works as a sensor).
- Several timers not only one, like the same way the watch has 5 alarms.

Conclusion:
Good watch for the price I paid (90 euros second hand) but I would be very dissapointed if I would expend 200 for a new one.
If I only could be able to...:
-Set a louder snooze alarm: This is a so basic function that should be mandatory. You can miss a flight if rely only on this watch. And one of the main reasons I use a watch -while travelling- is to backup my smartphone wake alarm.
- Set two city (origin and destination) and easy change between then: Just arrive at the airport and change the city, settings (time, DST, longitude/attitude) will change automatically.
..this watch could be the perfect traveller watch.

product_title: Stuhrling Original Delphi Automatic Watch - Grey Skeleton Dial Wrist Watch for Men - Stainless Steel Brown Leather Analog Watch 730.02
review_headline: ... found this information from their web site to be useful (I just self-wound the crown after discovering that the
review_body:
I found this information from their web site to be useful (I just self-wound the crown after discovering that the watch had stopped overnight and reading the negative reviews -- hopefully it will help?). I have rated it Four stars subject to change as I just purchased it:

"When worn daily, the movement of your wrist causes the mainspring to wind progressively, eliminating the need for additional winding. However, to start your automatic, it is recommended that you manually wind it by rotating the crown clockwise a number of turns while it is in its normal operating position (screw-down crowns will need to be unscrewed first). This will place some initial power on the mainspring to begin wearing your watch. You should wind it until you feel some resistance, while being careful not to “over-wind” the mainspring. If you hold the watch to your ear while you are winding your watch, you will hear a ratcheting noise; that is the sound of the mainspring being wound.

While wearing a mechanical automatic timepiece daily will keep the mainspring wound, the movement of the oscillating piece with the Stührling logo on it (the rotor) seen through the crystal on the back does not generate enough force to wind the mainspring beyond a certain point. If it did, then surely the mainspring could become over-wound and lock up. However, the slightest movement of the rotor will keep the mainspring wound and keep your timepiece running."

product_title: Casio Men's PRW-3000-1CR Protrek Triple Sensor Multi-Function Watch
review_headline: The best, most functional watch I've ever owned. Yet still attractive!? Amazing.
review_body:
Why on earth did I wait so long to upgrade to this incredible watch? I can't add much that the other, extremely detailed reviews do such a good job with. I just want to throw down my 5-stars and say that I'm extremely pleased. The watch body is much smaller than I expected, which makes it look classy and not obnoxious like the older ABC watches, or the bulky, ridiculous "SHOCK" watches. Despite the well-proportioned body, the numbers are plenty big and clear (especially the main/middle line) and very easy to read at a glance. I'm comfortable wearing this watch every single day, for every activity - from the office and business travel, to outdoor rock climbing and construction site work. The atomic clock radio works great here in Los Angeles, so the watch always has perfect time, and the compass works VASTLY better than my $700 smart phone. I only take this watch off when I sleep, and even then, only when I'm sleeping at home. For backpacking and travel, it stays on my wrist 24/7 for days at a time.

The black metal ring around the outside is getting a bit scratched up. Which for me, just gives the watch some character - it's seen a bit of real life.

product_title: Seiko Men's Silvertone Solar Chronograph Diver Watch
review_body:
[I inadvertently also posted my review on the page for a quite similar watch--same watch but with steel bracelet--realized I should have probably posted it here because it is the one I bought with the rubber band. Hopefully Amazon doesn't mind me reposting here.]

The main reason I bought this watch is that it is solar and therefore doesn't need battery replacement. I have learned in the past not to buy regular quartz diver's watches, because more times than not the waterproof case integrity is permanently damaged when the battery has to be replaced (even by a jeweler that claims it is qualified to replace the batteries in dive watches). So I'm not keen on buying a dive watch that you might have to throw away in two years when the battery wears out, and my go-to dive watch has been an automatic Seiko Diver (which is at least 25 years old but still works perfectly, although the dial and hands are getting a bit faded).

But I said, why not give this solar diver a shot, and I have not been disappointed.

Excellent watch, especially for the price. One thing that is a bugaboo for me is when the hands of a watch don't line up precisely with the appropriate markers. (E.g., when the minute hand is on 12, the hours hand should be precisely on the hour.) That is a big indicator to me whether the watch has been assembled with care. With this Seiko every hand is spot on where it should be, from the small seconds hand to the chronograph measurement hands to the 24 hour indicator. Especially at this price point, that is exceptional. It's not easy to get all those hands to line up precisely, especially with the small dials, but this watch does it.

Another indication of quality is that lume is used on the small seconds hand (constant running) on the left-hand side of the dial. One of the things that is required for a watch to be officially qualified to be a diver's watch is that the second hand must be lumed. In other words, for safety reasons you must be able to tell in low light conditions that your watch is operating. Many so-called "dive watches" don't even have their large seconds hand lumed (which technically disqualifies them from being a dive watch), but his Seiko has both the small seconds and the large seconds lumed. Overall, the lume quality is excellent.

I also like the "sweep" hand effect of the large measuring seconds hand, that is unusual for a quartz chronograph, most just have the typical one-second jump.

The only thing I was a little disappointed in was that the chronograph only measures to one hour and then stops and goes back to zero. However, I have to say I can understand this since it is a solar watch; if the chronograph function runs continuously I could see that it could wear down your power reserve much more quickly and cause recharging issues.

My feeling is this watch is a top value for the money, and I would buy it again without reservation. product_title: 22mm SUPER Engineer Type II 316L Stainless Steel Straight End Watch Bracelet
review_body:
This is ONE SOLID BAND! I paired it with my SS Apple Watch and it looks terrific. I was originally going to get a cheap metal band from HOCO or OITMM for $30 but decided to upgrade to Taikonaut, and I'm glad I did! Those cheap bands look silly next to a $600 watch, and I was a little worried about the latch coming loose at some point. I'd rather pay $70 and have a quality band that matches a quality watch. The quality is top notch, you're not going to get much better than this. I think it's a value.

The links are held together with screwed-in pins, which works so much better than those cheap push-pins. I love the squared edges of the links and thickness of this model, it really makes the lugs visually pop with contrast. The Apple Watch itself is kinda bulbous, so a thicker band made sense to me, it matches better. It's more uniform opposed to a thin metal band. The sides and details of the band are polished, which matches nicely with the polished finish of the watch. The links are brushed, but still very reflective and look great. All in all, a top-quality product!

product_title: Citizen Goldtone and White Men's Eco-Drive Watch
review_body: Shipping/packaging was well done, typical Citizen watch box kept the product insulated from dings during shipment.  Watch keeps good time the fit and finish was exactly as described and all band joints including the crown a made with Citizen's precision tolerance.  Watch presents a very full "watch face" as opposed to some of the more cluttered watches (ie aviation), hourly markers are easy to see as well as all hands including the second sweep.  Only complaint, not really a complaint but moreover a sort of surprise upon laying my hands on this watch, is the calendar date window is a little small but I wear glasses so for you 20/20 folks it shouldn't be a problem.  Gold tone is not too reflective or subdued, it's just right and doesn't present the deep yellow tinge indicative of 24k or Thai gold, this is on the order of 10k gold tone in terms of color.  Stainless back, Eco Drive, blah, blah, blah simply a great watch that does what a watch is supposed to do and that is to keep accurate time, this one happens to also look good and goes well either in dress, office work, or any other urban enviro-wear.  Great price through Amazon!

product_title: Hadley Roma LB6950 12-16mm Watch Band Sq Black Enamel Expansion Watchband
review_body: I own a Citizen Eco-Drive, which is a great watch and I love not having to worry about battery changes. However, the leather strap on this watch eventually wears out, especially because the model I have is not water-proof and needs to be removed every time I shower. I was on my second strap (which cost between $30 and $40) and decided it was time for me to look for an alternative. At first it was a struggle to find a metal band because a silver strap just looked odd as the watch is black with the only silver decal being the hands and a button. Google alerted me to Hadley Roma, and having used expansion bands on watches before, I was excited to try this.  I took the chance of ordering, and I LOVE IT! The most ideal would have been a 15mm band, but what silver you do see where the band attaches to the watch does not detract too much. The band is light and comfortable.  I did need to remove some links, but that was easy enough to do after watching a YouTube tutorial. Thank you Hadley Roma, my band may now actually outlive my watch!

review_body: The watch was great. I did expect it to be a little bit bigger than it is. It is a little bit bigger around than a quarter (I was only surprised because I didn't bother to check the dimensions in the description). The watch looks exactly like it does in the picture; all of the design looks exactly like I expected. However, it came without a working battery. In the process of trying to get the battery out to replace it, I accidentally broke off a plastic piece that was on top of the battery. The second hand worked after I replaced it, but the hour and minute hands did not. I don't know if it had something to do with the broken piece or not, although as far as I can tell the piece was just to keep the battery firmly in place. Anyway, the watch is only six bucks, and considering that the design looks great and the second hand works at least, it fits the price and is better than the twenty bucks I almost paid for a similar watch at a store. product_title: GuTe Military Style LED analog Wristwatch Japan Quartz Big Dial Fashion Watch Steel Long Strap
review_headline: It's Cheap!  But there are caveats...
review_body:
If you're looking at this watch, you need to know a few things.

First, this watch is BIG. I have medium-large wrists and it looked like I'm a little kid borrowing my dad's watch. It's long, super thick, and really heavy. Now, for some people this is a plus but it's much bigger than it looks in all the pictures. Plus, I'm American so I have a problem converting from MM. But no jokes, this thing weighs a ton.

I bought this because I wanted a stopwatch feature, but wasn't sure I'd use it so I wanted something cheap. In the description it says that this is perfect for runners because of the stopwatch. It has no stopwatch. I read the printed directions, then went to town on this watch's buttons like I was in the World Finals for Simon. No dice, not anything remotely like a stopwatch. In fact, I couldn't even figure out how to change the date. As I don't like to live my life perpetually two and a half months behind, that made the digital features near on hopeless.

I'd also like to say that the band was pretty cheap. At this price, it's to be expected. But still, it would pinch and pull hairs and be otherwise uncomfortable. Not only that, but apparently I got the "Sassysquatch" band sizing. I tried removing links but neither my SIM tray ejector (nothing like having the right tools handy) or screwdrivers when I got home could convince the slags of what appeared to be fused metal to budge. I almost wrapped it twice around my wrist to make it more secure.

So, after taking a few days to fight with this heavy and confusing monster, I returned it. If you're wanting to buy one, just be aware.

product_title: Carrie Hughes Ladies Retro Steampunk Glass Ball Transparent Skeleton Mechanical Pocket Watch with Chain CH199
review_headline: First Rate Steampunk Skeleton Pocket Watch
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:e27f886335d71c24e6ae9fcffa9be865]]Steampunk skeleton mechanism pocket watches are very popular at the moment and they are available in a wide range of sizes, designs, shapes, chain types and let's not forget price.

Sent for review it comes in a well padded bronze - brown gift box and is generally well presented. This watch is quite unique in some ways as its ball shaped whereas most are flatter. It was certainly welcoming to see something a bit different.

Weighing in at 41g with dimensions of 3.0 x 2.8cm this would be classed as fairly small (large coin size in length and width and slightly smaller in thickness). The weight is just about right, not too heavy, not too lightweight. The chain is 82cm in length.

It looks and feels good quality and the material in question is steel (case), alloy (chain) with a bronze coloured coating to give it that vintage - antique look. The watch itself sits on a support frame and you can spin the ball shape around to manipulate it as and when required.

The dials are Roman numerals with small numbers on top and although the face is relatively small the magnification feature inside the ball enlarges / magnifies the viewing screen so that you can see it much clearer.

You don't need batteries for this as its operated mechanically via the hand winding dial on top. Once in motion you can see the mechanical skeleton in action very easily, especially at the back and it keeps the time accurately. Underneath there is a small bell which gives it a more of a balanced look.

The best way to show any product of course is via HD video review so I have also done a HD video with voice over recorded in normal room conditions with no studio lights or video editing.

Verdict: First Rate Steampunk Skeleton Pocket Watch.

product_title: 2014 New Oulm Men's Two Time Zone Business Quartz Wrist Watch Coffee Color
review_body: I'm a small time watch collector, usually purchase invictas and androids at the $100-$250 range,  they're my favs. Occasionally buy cheapies like this for the instant grad at a low cost. This is my second oulm, both performing well. This watch appears much richer than the cost. I'm into copper n rose gold, and this watch is somewhere in that warm family. Whole watch is lightweight, and I do believe all stainless, case, case back as well as band all stainless. Brown finish on case and band, is done well enough as to not look cheap. Don't know if they used IP process to adhere the color, prob not. But finish looks good and doesn't feel like it would scratch off easily. Watch crystal is some form of hard glass, no plastic. Watch case seems like 50mm, band is 24mm.  There are no micro adjustments on the band, so after you fit it, might not be the perfect fit, as was in my case. Ended up removing as band and replaced w/ an old 24mm heavy leather brown band from android and the watch looks great. Lots of words fer a cheap watch, just trying to help folks. In the end, it's a unique looking decent fashion watch, with much more class than the novelties you find at Walmart.

product_title: Casio Men's GLX5600-1 G-Shock G-Lide Surfing Watch
review_body:
No qualms with the watch performance, the size is good for me and functionality fits my needs well.

Unfortunately, the battery has lacked and Casio customer service hasn't been very helpful. Watch was originally purchased December of 2011, and battery died in November 2013, less than 2 years. This is not a huge surprise as I'm sure many of their watches sit in storage for a while before being sold, but still it's a lot less than the 7 years advertised. I rarely use the night light and don't use any functions other than time and tide on the "home screen", so pretty much just push buttons to change time for daylight savings twice a year. I waited almost a year to send it in for battery replacement because it had to be shipped across the country and I had another watch in the mean time. I needed the replacement and re-pressurization to be done professionally because I frequently wear the watch swimming and surfing. Finally sent it in October 2014. The new battery died in about 6 months! I spent a while on the phone with customer service today trying to get them to offer me any option besides "send it in for technician to determine if the battery needs to be replaced." I spent $26 to get the battery replaced last time, and there's a very high likelihood that's all it needs this time. It would cost me $13 in shipping just to get the watch there and back to find this out. I posed this hypothetical situation to the customer service rep and asked her if she thought it was a good system for me to have to replace the battery more than once a year for the rest of the watch life and got.... nothing in return. Waiting for a return call from her supervisor, but assuming they're not willing to replace the watch I can't justify sending it in for replacement again, which in total will now have cost me more than half the value of the watch just to keep it running for 2.5 years, way less than the 7 years advertised.

Can't recommend this watch given my experience, and especially knowing that many of my friends who have had tide watches from other companies (Nixon, Rip Curl, etc.) have had multiple replacements free of charge with no questions asked when anything went wrong.

product_title: Citizen Men's AT4000-53L "Amazon Exclusive" Eco-Drive Stainless Steel Watch with Triple-Link Bracelet
review_body:
I love watches but never spent more than $100 on one. Even in this age of smartphones giving you the time I love watches as a wonderful accessory and decided it was time to spend a decent amount of money on a good one. After weeks of looking at various Citizen watches I settled on this one: I love wearing blue jeans so the blue dial compliments that and I love that the color is an Amazon exclusive (which means the watch will be somewhat unique). The heft of the watch is great to me- feels sturdy and substantial. It is beautiful, radio controlled time/date and has been a pleasant ownership experience so far. If I had to cite a negative is that the manual that comes with the watch (and all supporting online content from the Citizen website) while very detailed and helpful still omit an EXTREMELY important fact about this watch: if it is not charged you cannot move the hands of the watch with the pull out crown. I read the manual several times and looked at the website- that fact is not spelled out. I was initially frustrated by this thinking the watch was defective but then decided to leave it facing a sunny window for a few days- VIOLA! Zfter that I followed the very detailed instructions on how to set the watch up (it is a bit complicated but then I knew this when I researched it). I love that it will not need a battery and the 5 year warranty makes me feel I have purchased a premium product, The hands are nicely illuminated in the dark.

I love this watch! I'll buy another Citizen EcoDrive in the future from Amazon (I went the e*ay route the 1st time and glad e*ay helped me get my money back from an unscrupulous seller who had a huge positive rating from buyers... cheap prices don't mean you get a quality working product).

product_title: Timex  Intelligent Quartz 3-GMT Watch
review_headline: A Solid Workhorse of a Watch!
review_body: With almost 40 watches in my current collection, I'm a discerning watch enthusiast (which is different than being a 'watch snob').  I like workhorse watches;  watches that look good and perform great.  Prior to this watch, I hadn't owned a Timex in 30 yeas, but when I saw this one, I felt the yearning to pull the trigger, and I'm glad I did. What cannot be said about a $90 Timex when most of their products are in the $25 - 40 range?  Well, when shopping for a Timex, you can expect to get nothing but the best for that kind of money.  And this watch delivers.  The glossy black finish is good. The printed numbers are very clear. The movement is accurate (+ 2 seconds by my testing) and the band is very supple.  I will comment that the band is a few shades lighter than in the pictures and the watch is substantially thick, but not so much that it would interfere with putting on a jacket.  The deep blue light of the Indiglo works when you press the crown, and is sufficient to easily see the time in a dark movie theater.  The hour and minute hands are substantial, and easy to see under most lighting conditions.  However, the second hand seems nearly invisible against the 'blackish' background.  I haven't used the time zone feature so I cannot evaluate that now.  All-in-all, you can expect a lot of watch when you pay $90 for a Timex as they don't inflate their prices.  Timex is known for making simple 'workhorse' watches that are great for daily wear, and this one is no exception.

product_title: kate spade new york Women's 1YRU0445 Metro Grand Crystal-Accented Watch with Black Leather Band
review_headline: Surprisingly tasteful but rides on its designer name
review_body:
Well, obviously I'm not wearing this watch, but my better half is. It's perfect for her – she dresses casually for work, but is helping brides pick out thousands of dollars of flowers for their upcoming weddings, so this strikes the right balance between fashion jewelry and a 'proper' watch. Also, she loves Kate Spade's bags.

From the picture, we half expected it to be a big, chunky, bling monstrosity, but that's not the case. the watch is pretty shallow, so the big face doesn't seem that large, and the crystal;s add a little sparkle but don't overpower. The leather band was stiff at first, but softened over a week's wear.

As for the designer name, well, the '12' on the clock face is the Kate Spade 'spade' logo, and the name is also on there. That's it. Very understated for what appears to be bling central in the product photo.

Functionality? It tells the time. There's no date, or AM/PM indicator, just the hour, minute, and second hands.

It definitely strikes a good balance between casual and formal, and so could well be the one watch you need to own, if you want a nice watch but you're not the sort who wants a different one for every outfit. The price might seem high if you're not a watch wearer, but the $200 to $400 area is where the best items are if you want more than a $30 throwaway piece, but are not willing to hit that 'real jewelry' level of $1,000.

As with any designer name good, the materials account for about half of the worth and the name the other half. If, like my wife, you're a fan of the KS name, this may be worth the extra coin to you.

review_headline: The shop refused to charge my wife for the repair but asked her to consider them to steer them to better products and service in
review_body: I bought this as a gift for my wife a little over two years ago.  It malfunctioned 2 weeks after the warranty expired.  We sent it to Tissot and were told it would take $240 to repair.  They claimed it was damaged and needed major work.  My wife wore the watch only occasionally and was certain it was never mistreated.  No budge from Tissot - still $240 or nothing.  We had them send it back and my wife took it to a local watch repair shop.  First, they observed no signs of impact or other damage - just normal light scratches from wear.  Then, they said they would take a look at it while my wife worked.  10 minutes later, out came the watch, working perfectly - it was a loose screw! The shop refused to charge my wife for the repair but asked her to consider them to steer them to better products and service in the future.  Tissot takes advantage of its customers and for that, I would have to say they stink.

product_title: SEIKO ProspEx diver scuba SBDC001 men's watch
review_headline: Good watch with few major flaws keeping it from being great
review_body: This is probably the most famous Seiko watch there is. All the specs are widely known so there is no point of describing them. While I think Seiko makes good watches for 50-200 dollars and Grand Seiko at 1000s dollars, IMHO, Seiko does NOT make decent watches with consistent QC for anything in between that I consider good value. They keep putting the 4R into watches that cost more than 500 dollars and 6R into watches that cost 1000 dollars without spicing up the details of the watch (or even regulate it a bit).  First and foremost, the clasp of the Sumo. The clasp, oh boy. It is cheaply made and rattle like a toy every time I wear it. This is the same clasp they use for 50 dollars watch, 500 dollars watch and of course 1000 dollars watch (the Shogun). I believe this area of cost cutting is a wrong choice for Seiko. The band is fine, it is very comfortable, albeit rough and uneven finish on surfaces. This is one of known Seiko QC problems.  It is after all, a 400-500 dollars watch. Seiko has watches that cost less than this and has better clasp (such as the SARB series). Mentioned of the SARB series, they have saphire crystal. Granted they are not dive watch but saphire crystal nonetheless. Seiko just released a newer version of the Sumo with saphire crystal and DLC on it. Prices certainly hiked quite a bit since then.  Last but not least, the accuracy of my Sumo. Quite disappointing. Like I mentioned before, I hate it when watch snobs tell people to go quartz when your watch if off by minutes a day. Look at the definition of a watch. Its job is to tell good time. 7-15 sec/day is acceptable for normal mechanical watches. Anything more is too inaccurate for daily wear. Strange and unlucky since I got a lemon with my Sumo. It was slow about -15 sec/day. After about a year of wear, it is about -50 sec/day. Sounds like it need a full service.  I still like some aspects of it though. It has a very beautiful case and dial (Again, misaligned bezel and dial, known Seiko QC problem. At least the minute and hour hand line up straight at 6 o'clock and noon/midnight). Also, I don't care for the argument of Hardflex not break vs saphire, blah blah blah. It is a 500 dollars watch and Saphire is expected.  I just don't understand as the more expensive Seiko divers has saphire (the 1000M Tunas). Then again, even the Marine Master has Hardflex when it is priced at 2000 dollars. Weird. I thought about saving for the MM but since owning the Sumo, there is just no way I'm willing to spend that much money and getting a product like that.  I don't care for the 8L "sub" Grand Seiko movement either for the MM.  After owing quite a few mechanical watches, I found that with an un-regulated watch, it is just luck. You can get a watch with COSC out of the box. Or 20 sec/day and still within specs since Seiko's movement have a wide range (Seiko's focus is on reliability rather than precision for anything that is not Grand Seiko) My Orient with worse specs than the Sumo average 0 sec per day. That's right, 0 second per day for 3 straight months of wearing. Only set the time at the beginning at that was it. That is unheard of for a mechanical watch. My other Orient is about 4-6 sec per day. My 4R36  Seiko is 10 sec per day. The Sumo though, will become a Seiko classics in the future since Seiko as a brand has so much history. The end of my rant and I still like my Sumo, as flawed as it is.

product_title: Watch Casio Pro Trek Prw-6000-1er Men´s Black
review_headline: Can't beat the features at this price point.
review_body:
This is my new favorite watch to wear at work. For the price, you can't beat the features offered in this watch. I have other watches that have some of the functions in different combinations, but they're all collected in one place here. First, and most importantly for an analog/digital watch, the digital movement/display is synchronized to the analog movement. There's no cumbersome process of trying to get the hands synchronized to the digital display. The second hand also acts as the pointer when in compass mode. A really cool hidden feature is that you can push a combination of buttons to get the hands to move out of the way of the digital display and smaller dial for easier reading. It's solar powered, so you don't have to worry about draining the battery when you use all of those cool features. You can even set the backlight to come on automatically when you raise the watch to look at it at night.
Two minor drawbacks: The watch strap itself is lower quality than some of my other resin or rubber bands, but the strap lays nicely against my wrist because the point where it attaches to the lugs is angled downward (unlike the G-shock which sticks out). I also was never able to get the radio time to manually set, although it does update automatically each night. That initially caused problems because it didn't automatically set DST (another nice feature); I had to turn it on manually. After it automatically updated that night, I was able to put DST back in auto the next day.

product_title: Swatch Unisex SUOB714 Originals Black Watch with Patterned Band
review_body:
This Swatch was given to me by my lovely wife as a Valentine's Day gift. This happens to be my second Swatch watch. Overall, I'm very happy with it. It's low key, with subtle details and good sized profile that doesn't dwarf my, admittedly, thin wrist.

The style is very sedate compared to the decorative options that Swatch can deliver. I enjoy the brief amount of design elements found on the dial. They don't obfuscate the minimalist approach. On a black back, the thin, red markings are only broken up by light gray second denotations. The day and date window pops with its white background. The font on these perfectly stands out. No squinting necessary.

The band is comfortable and reversible. The material used on it is fantastic. It's some form of super-soft silicone, soft touch wonder. Highly flexible, it makes looping it a breeze. The strap, at least on my copy, came with the black face out. The reverse red side is bright, but not retina blinding red. I opted to switch for the red side. The contrast between the black watch and the red accents within it with the red strap gave it more pop. The band is easily changed as long as you have a thin metal item to take out the pins holding the straps. I like the versatility of the strap. If I want to be less conspicuous, I can reverse it back to black, just flip the strap.

There are some drawbacks, of course, as anything out there at this price point aught to have. First, the hands don't have any kind of lume. After all, they have an opening in the middle. It's a good stylistic effect, specially when paired with the highly reflective chrome-like finish. In highly lighted areas, these puppies stand out from the dark background. But in the dark, guessing the time would be more effective than looking at the watch dial.

Also, the dome is subject to scratching. I mean, this is a sub $100 watch, can't expect more than the bare minimum protection. The watch is water resistant, but not water proof--no dunking it in water or under a running faucet. Lastly, if you hate ticking noises, this is a loud one. The seconds hand is undeniably loud when you have it in a quiet environment. I don't have a problem with it (I find it oddly satisfying), but others might want to muff it under a shirt at night, or store it out of sight if such minute histrionics aren't your thing.

Even so, I like this watch. It's subtle, and well designed and keeps time. The red and black style is well done, and it has a great strap that makes this watch a joy to wear. It might have a few inconveniences (noise and durability) but if you need a casual watch, I wouldn't hesitate to get it.

product_title: Casio Men's GW-9400-1CR Master of G Stainless Steel Solar Watch
review_body:
This is the best watch for the outdoorsman! I found this watch to be very useful as you can tell barometric pressure right from the timekeeping mode by a graphical display and a barometric pressure change indicator as well. This thing is also very easy on battery power even with the auto light function on. It has many more features than I can go into here. Some like the world time helps me know what time it is at home when I'm away some where like Utah, I live in California. I found it very useful while I was in the UK. The altimeter has a resolution of 1 meter which is very fine, it takes it's information from the barometer and air pressure can change in minutes so it's necessary to get reference altitude from a topographical map and set the altimeter accordingly before you set out for the day's endeavor and at easily identifiable points on a map along the was; see reference altimeter setting. The compass works quite well for getting bearings which are shown on the big display. The directional indicator is in the "small bezel " , the circular display, it has very fine lcd markers that show north, west, east, and south. It's actually pretty easy-to-use , I find using the strap laid out flat makes it easy to mark north and the bearing for your direction of travel.
It can take temperature readings but you have to take it off for about 1/2 hour to get the surrounding temperature correct, remember that it's warmer inside a tent from body heat. On your wrist it's gonna read your skin temperature as well as ambient temperature.
This is the reason i bought this Triple Sensor watch over the other ones... it, is a G Shock! Which means that you will always have a watch that tells time even if you beat the hell out of it But... i think the altimeter, barometer, compass internal sensors might be disfunctional after beating the hell out of it. Being a G Shock it will provide a bit more protection than say a Casio ProTrek or a Tissot or a smart watch. It looks great on my wrist and it's not too big. It's got a nice band and metal strap hold down. I think the buttons being cross cut is a fantastic idea and they are stainless steell. I like the sunrise sunset function too and the only thing I wish it had is a moon phase function. I use the sunrise function for night hiking and sunset so I know how much light I have left and when to kick back and watch the sunset and color show. review_headline: Great watch for a month or so BUT ABSOLUTELY POOR SERVICE BY AMAZON'S REPAIR FACILITY
review_body: Great watch - 'time' will tell how long it lasts. I chose this watch because of it's small size compared to a mans watches that measure 42-47 mm in diameter. That large size would just about drape over my entire wrist. I also chose this because it is all stainless steel. My skin, for whatever reason, destroys other types of metal and removes the finish from anything other than gold or stainless steel. One warning ... the hands are very thin and it takes more than a quick glance to tell the time. Nice stop watch.  UPDATE ON MY REVIEW IT STOPPED WORKING just past the deadline to return it. The watch stopped. Here's what I did to figure out what the problem was - I pulled the stem so the battery was not being used - hours later I pushed the stem back in and the watch started - watch stopped hours later - pulled the stem - let the watch sit for several more hours - pushed the stem in and the watch worked for an hour or so and then stopped.  I explained to a friend who is a jeweler and he assured me that 100% of the time, with the symptoms I explained, that the battery is the problem. The watch was warranteed so I sent it to Amazon sanctioned watch repair in Brentwood, TN. They have had the watch since the 28th of April. I just finished talking with 'rep' in Tennessee. He tell's me I probably will not have the watch for maybe another 4 weeks. He has no idea what 'they' are doing to the watch even though 'they' are working on it at this very moment. BEWARE OF AMAZON WATCH REPAIR AND CONSIDER BUYING A WATCH FROM A LOCAL ESTABLISHMENT. UPDATE/UPDATE: It is the end of May and I STILL have not received my watch. AND this is after I contacted Amazon and the Amazon rep said he would escalate my problem to management. He did give me a partial refund on the watch but the 'escalation to management' appears to have done ZERO as far as getting the watch back to me.

I urge anyone considering the purchase of an OEM bracelet (Rolex, TAG, etc.) to seriously consider a bracelet by this manufacturer.
As other reviewers have noted, attention to the tightness of the link screws is necessary. If they loosen, a tiny dab of Blue Loctite will solve the problem. So far, on two bracelets, I have not had to do this.
Finally, before you spend $1000 or more on a replacement watch bracelet, read the other reviews of these products. I have this one on a TAG Heuer, and am delighted.

product_title: G-Shock GW6900-1 Men's Tough Solar Black Resin Sport Watch
review_headline: I am very happy with this watch
review_body:
I am very happy with this watch. This is my first Casio G-Shock and so far, I love it. I think the size and shape are just right and I like the functionality. I was a little worried that it might be a little big and bulky on my wrist but I think it fits just right. I have an average size wrist and the watch doesn't look abnormally big on me.

I really like the solar function. I wore Timex Ironman watches for years but changing the batteries was such a hassle due to the difficulty in getting the back off with the wrist band in the way. And I had to replace a couple of watches when I didn't get the back sealed properly and water got inside. I'm hoping that with this solar powered one, battery replacement is a thing of the past! It really doesn't take much effort to keep the battery fully charged. When I got the watch in the mail the battery level was at the third level (of four), or the level just below full charge. Initially it took a little bit to get the charge up to full and it went back and forth from full charge to down a level a few times over the first few days. I'm assuming the watch had been sitting in a warehouse out of the light for who knows how long so it probably needed some extended light exposure to fully charge. After a few days I was careful the expose the watch to direct sunlight for longer periods and that brought the charge up to full and it stayed there. Since then I haven't made any special effort to expose the watch face to light (sun or electric), just the exposure it gets through normal everyday use, and it has stayed fully charged.

I've been really happy with the atomic timekeeping as well. The instructions go to great lengths to explain how you need to position the watch a certain way on a window sill at night so that the watch can receive the time keeping radio signals. It sounded like it was going to be a real pain since I prefer to sleep with my watch on. So far my watch hasn't missed the signal once even though it stays on my wrist in bed at night. I imagine that results might vary depending on where in the country (or world) you live and what the surrounding terrain is like. I live in the northeast US and in pretty hilly terrain but so far, no problems with reception.

Other than those specifics, I like the overall look and function of the watch. I was concerned the numbers might be a little small but so far that has been fine. Figuring out the controls was not difficult. I did read the instruction manual to find out about some of the specific functions but overall I just played with the buttons a little bit and most of it is pretty intuitive.

I've only had the watch for a few weeks so I can't speak toward it's long term durability but it definitely seems very well constructed and I look forward to many years of service. It looks like the band is relatively easy to replace should the need arise. Overall I think it is a great watch. If you are looking for something that is functional and durable, I highly recommend the G-Shock GW6900-1!

product_title: Timex Expedition Shock Digital Compass Watch
review_body: I was looking for an inexpensive EDC watch that I would not have to worry about if it gets hit, wet or dragged through mud. I really like negative display watches so this one works great for me. A lot of people complained that the display is hard to see but I like it that way. The Indiglo does a good job to see the time in complete darkness and it is subtle enough to not dazzle you.  The watch is a bit big, it is bigger than the average Casio G-Shock but fits well on wrists 6 inches and bigger. The compass is accurate once you calibrate it right. It is recommended to calibrate it in the area or for the area you want to use it. If you calibrate it near your pc or electrical power cables where there will be electromagnetic interference then this would obviously affect the accuracy. The compass has the feature to input the declination for the area you are in so that you can use easily with a map to navigate.    All in all at the price, this is a really great watch for everyday use. you can wear it and forget it. Much more functional for me than the expensive $200+ ABC watches as I don't need the additional features, so no sense in paying for what I don't need    Update: February 23rd 2015.  I have been using this watch for a couple of weeks now and it works well as an EDC watch for me. It does run a little slow, I have see a drift of about 3 seconds in about 2 weeks. this is not a big deal for me as I can sync it manually to a GPS clock whenever the drift gets to about 5 seconds.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNK807 Seiko 5 Automatic Stainless Steel Watch with Blue Canvas Band
review_body:
Very nice for the price, like most of the Seiko Automatics. The dial looks a little plainer with the flat numbers and tick marks, but it has the raised \\"5\\" appliqué, and the luminous dots at the hour positions. The case has a smooth matte, bead blasted finish, while the back is contrasting polished stainless steel with the clear exhibition back.

The buckle and dual loops are also a matching matte finish, with the blue canvas strap having a leather appearing reinforcing strip on the holes. The buckle is stamped \\"China\\", while the movement and back are marked \\"Malaysia\\". It has the 7S26C 21 jewel automatic movement which is very dependable, but I have three of them and they all seem to run a bit fast. I've found that if I take them off at night and place them face down the time seems to even out fairly well. The day complication is the dual English / Spanish which I really dislike; very annoying when you get the setting wrong, but not too big a deal. One of my other Auto 5 watches is English / Arabic, which was an interesting surprise.

All in all a very good watch for the price which gets a lot of compliments, and is also available in green, khaki and black. It's hard to go wrong with a Seiko, and my first automatic which is 37 years old is still going strong. Recommended by me.

Note: I should have mentioned in my original post that this being a 37mm case you may not like it if you have a large wrist. Mine is only 6 ½\\" around so this watch looks well proportioned, and I feel comfortable up to a 40mm watch. Seiko makes a similar 23 jewel version with a 42mm case, but it cost about twice as much; in my opinion that is still a bargain.

product_title: Casio Men's Ana-Digi Sport Watch
review_headline: Was a great watch until the hands quit turning after 3 months. Replaced under warranty.
review_body: Great watch - looks good, not too heavy, and it goes well with my "outdoors casual" wardrobes. I particularly like the compass and thermometer options.  I'm not a big fan of the stretchy rubber watch bands so I replaced that with a military style nylon band and the whole package works well for me.  3/8/15 My watch is now three months old and I'm no longer a happy camper. The minute and hour hands stopped working - I can't even move them using the adjustment feature. Yes, I did change out the batteries and the digital portion of the watch still works as does the compass feature. So its time to send the watch off and see if Casio will make good on their warranty.  4/10/15 Now for an update on my watch. I sent the watch off to Casio's west coast service center on March 13. They received it on March 16 from USPS delivery confirmation. I gave the service center a couple of weeks and contacted them via e-mail on April 6 to see what was happening. I got a reply on the same day and the service people basically said "Yes, your watch is broken, We'll send you a replacement. By the way, what's your address?" I gave them my address again (I'd enclosed all of that when I sent the watch in for repair) and I'm glad to say that I received a new replacement watch today, April 10.  Since I have to give Casio a final grade on this experience I guess that I'll go with two stars. The watch never should have failed in the first place and I'm out six bucks for postage to send the watch back to Casio. It took the service guys about a month to get a new watch back to me, but they did honor their warranty in a better way than they promised (new watch vs "reconditioned" - whatever that means). So I'll treat the new Casio gently and wear my Timex Expedition for dirty and watch hostile days.

product_title: Citizen Men's AT0200-05E Eco-Drive Stainless Steel Watch with Green Canvas Band
review_headline: My first Citizen watch . . . I love it!
review_body:
I'll preface my review by saying that I have only had the watch for about a week. That being said, I love it! The packaging was satisfactory - both the Citizen box and Amazon box were properly insulated and wrapped, where the watch was unlikely to be damaged during transit. Upon putting on the watch for the first time, it fit perfectly on my wrist. I should note that I have a very small wrist and I really dislike watch bands that \\"wrap around\\" the wrist where the strap is not held close to the band by a band loop (i.e., sticks out). Similarly, the watch itself is perfect as well - the diameter is not so big where the face overwhelms my wrist. I really love the Casio G-force watches, but usually the watch face and/or the rubber band is way too big for my wrist. I also think the band is handsome and rugged. I have no plans to switch it out, \\"dress it up,\\" etc. The watch has a military look which I like (I was on a medical rescue team in the Air Force and I wish I would have had something like this back then).

Time keeping is excellent. I just checked the watch's time and it hasn't lost any seconds since I set it last week. Bravo to solar power. Damn, did I hate changing batteries on my other watches! For this reason alone, I love it. I always use to admire Seiko and have many of their watches. However, I now believe Citizen has trumped Seiko . . . I would definitely buy another one of their watches.

Concerning the illumination of the watch - I tested it in a darkened walk in closet and the illumination worked really well. I had no problem discerning the time. Regarding the watch time keeping and chronograph - I thought the large Arabic numerals were easy to read and the 3 chronograph dials were easy to read as well. The chronograph itself is very simple to use and I had no problem figuring out how each functioned. My only complaint is the date window . . . I can barely see it. Perhaps this is more due to my poor vision then anything else. However, it is a minor complaint. Last, but not least, the cost to me was $135 (I believe the watch is selling now for $168.75, i.e., I was fortunate to get the watch while it was discounted by 40%).

All in all, I would recommend this watch to anyone; and, as I alluded to earlier, I will probably consider a Citizen watch before other brands, if I am in the market for a watch again.

product_title: 20mm Military MoD Vintage Distressed Leather Watch Strap - Brown
review_headline: It doesn't look as nice as the photo
review_body:
It doesn't look as nice as the photo. The leather is ultra thin and stretches out after only a few wears. I have switched to a smaller hole 3 times now and will soon run out of holes. As it stretches the width of the band shrinks in the area before the holes, while the area after the holes in unaffected, so it now has an imbalanced width to it. The surface of the leather begins to look more distressed as it stretches as well, and not in a good way. Probably not noticeable to someone casually glancing at your watch but definitely annoying as the owner.

It is notable that I normally wear my watches pretty loose and don't put them through any sort of abuse that might cause excessive stretching. It stretches out by itself to the point where the watch face will flop around to the inside of my wrist while doing benign activities such as driving. Also the watch I put this on was the normal size Timex Weekender which is probably smaller and lighter than a lot of watches a man might want to put this band on.

I would not buy this product again.

product_title: Seiko SNKN02 Analog Display Automatic Brown dial Men's  Brown Leather Watch
review_headline: Great Looking Automatic Mechanical watch, well worth the price
review_body:
I noticed the description here is confusing and not correct so I thought I would write a review.
First this is not a quartz watch and it's not a Japan movement. This is an automatic mechanical watch as it says on the dial and is self winding. You can see the video of the display back and the automatic movement in the photos. The movement is made in Malaysia by Seiko Time Corp. It's a 21 jewel movement - Caliber 7S26. This model is part of the new Seiko Recraft series of watches.

Even the strap seems to be high quality leather calfskin and is about 4mm thick. It's also long enough for the largest wrist.

The dial is champagne toned with gold hands and the case is stainless steel with a gold finish. The watch looks fantastic and keeps great time. This is a great price for a automatic watch. The display back is a plus and the movement looks good. Seiko is a highly respected quality brand and I have Seiko Automatic watches that are running fine and 30 years old.

This is a sharp looking watch, it's solid and has a great retro look with a tonneau style case.

product_title: Swatch Women's GS138 Swatch Baby Blue Dial Watch
review_headline: It's ok...  At least it's aesthetically pleasing?
review_body:
I would have given this watch 4 or 5 stars due to the fact that it's a gorgeous color (true to photo), great size, very durable, and very comfortable... but I had a couple of issues with it.

The Good:
I bought it for work (as a veterinary technician) because it is water resistant. No issues there! This watch takes a beating and it's definitely pretty damn water proof (for my needs, anyway). Definitely recommend it... as long as you don't have issues like I did.

The Bad:
This watch stopped keeping good time about 4 months after I got it. I have never dropped it, smashed it, or exposed it to extreme heat or cold. Nevertheless, it will intermittently slow down to the point where I'll take it off at night and it will be several hours behind by morning, but still ticking normally.

Speaking of ticking... This thing is loud... Like... super distracting loud. I thought the other reviewers were just being fussy... but holy crap, man... I need to keep it in a drawer when I'm not busy and when I'm driving, listening to music is a must. Do not sit in silence with this thing on; you will go mad. At first, it wasn't so bad. I kinda just dealt with it (and was somewhat in denial) when I first got it, but... after having it for 10 months and having to reset it at least 10 times in the past 6 months (due to it randomly slowing down), I just can't overlook the noise anymore.

If it were even a _little_ quieter and kept good time since I got it? I would have given it 5 stars... but for the price, I expected better (considering I've had $10 watches that kept perfect time, lasted multiple YEARS, and didn't drive me crazy). I wish I could recommended it wholeheartedly, but I just can't.

review_body: The Waveceptor Solar is my favorite watch. I have owned this watch for over nine months. product_title: G-Shock MTGM900DA-8CR Men's Tough Solar Atomic Stainless Steel Sport Watch
review_headline: Best watch that I have ever owned
review_body: I got tired of buying the less expensive non-Casio digital watches and having them wear badly. I used to swear by Casio, but got tired of the resin bands cracking after a year or so, and switched to a different brand that had metal bands. I did work in a harsh environment (aboard ships in the tropics), so possibly sweat and strong sunlight may have had something to do with that. Anyway, the battery in my old inexpensive watch died, so figured I would look into a better watch. This one looked like it had everything I could possibly want or use in a watch. I was right. It is a little heavy and clunky, but to me that means substantial and well built. I also found the band to be a real pain to shorten. I watched the YouTube video, and I do have a set of jewelers screwdrivers, but it was still a royal pain. I almost broke down and took it to a jewelers, but finally got it done. After you get the first link out, the rest get a little easier. This watch is fantastic. After a day, I don't notice the weight. It looks very nice, and I have no problem wearing it as a dress watch. I wish they had this model when I first started shipping out since it looks pretty much bullet proof. The atomic clock resets the watch from anywhere in my house. It doesn't have to be near a window. The watch came about half charged, and after leaving it outside in direct sunlight for a few hours it now constantly stays on full charge. This is the ultimate watch for anyone who demands accuracy, durability, and dependability (and looks) in a watch. I only wish that they had an extra fold over locking piece on the clasp. The clasp seems sturdy, but the extra safety of having a double lock would have made this watch completely perfect.

product_title: Seiko Bedside Alarm Clock
review_headline: Well made QUIET clock...but if only....
review_body:
I have taken some time to live with this clock before writing a review. When looking for an alarm clock, my initial goal was to try to find one that was quality built, even if I had to pay more to purchase it. I'm tired of cheap products. Also, and VERY IMPORTANT to me was I wanted a QUIET clock. My needs for this clock was not as an alarm clock, so I can't comment on that aspect. Rather, I wanted a clock to place in our powder room which is next to the toilet area. We use it to keep track of the time while getting ready for work in the mornings. I also wanted to be able to know what time it was in the dead of night when I got up to use the restroom. I wanted it quiet because the last little clock was noisy. It pronounced a loud "click" each second and was annoying. This clock is so very quiet, which we love.

I couldn't tell from the photo when deciding to purchase it if what seems to look like metal on the clock was actually metal, or plastic. I ordered it and was very pleased with the quality of the build of this clock. It turned out to be plastic painted to look like metal, but it is still quite nice for being that. The only issue I have with this clock is that it is lighted so supposedly it can be read in the dark. With it's normal light setting, I have to put my face up close to it to tell the time...unless I push the bar on top, which lights it beautifully and I can read it normally. My wish would be that one would have the choice of choosing either the lower lighting setting or the higher lighting setting without having to push the bar. Yes, I know I can tape the bar down, but something I would rather not have to do. I would have gladly given this product 5 stars if that were an option. Yes, this is an excellent clock, but the lighting issue causes me to give it 4 stars.

It came with a thin necklace type chain that is the same color of the case. So, it has a ring to put the chain through which is attached at the top, rather than the clip shown in the photos. However, I think it only adds to the beauty of the watch and doesn't take away from quality or design.

If you're in search of a gift for someone special or simply something special for yourself, this pocket watch is perfect and would even make a treasured item to pass down through generations. product_title: Citizen Women's FC0000-59D "World Time A-T" Stainless Steel Eco-Drive Watch
review_headline: I found it VERY easy to set the time
review_body:
I received my watch yesterday and it is stunning. It is large and heavy, but I was ready for that after reading other reviews. I found it VERY easy to set the time. Just read a few lines of the included instruction manual, pressed the buttons a couple of times, and it was all set. The watch came fully charged so, after it was set, it was good to go.

Pros:
- The face is a beautiful mother of pearl
- Even though I wanted the rose gold version, I bought the silver because it was over $100 less. After receiving it, I am still very happy with the silver. It is much more beautiful overall than the photo shows.
- The hands do glow in the dark and it is pretty awesome!
- It is very sturdy and seemingly well made

Cons:
- The links pinch skin and hair- maybe this is all metal band watched but I've never had one before
- I tried to adjust the length of the band myself (it arrived very long), I couldn't remove the pins. After taking it to my local jeweler and having to pay $12, I found out that all of the pins had been installed in the wrong direction meaning that they were really jammed in there. I found this odd considering this is a brand new watch, and it makes me wonder what else might be wrong with it. Nothing obvious thus far...

All in all, it is a beautiful, waterproof, sapphire faced, classy watch. I would buy it again.

review_body: This posting might be slightly premature but I will update if something changes. The crystal and bezel are beautifully crafted and without imperfection. The "beating-heart" movement in this watch is mesmerizing, both my wife and I both catch each other just staring at it and admiring it. The watch I received does vary slightly from the one pictured, however. The portion of the skeleton just behind the "beating-heart" with the Flor De Lis symbols on it is non-existent on my watch. I'm completely okay with that though as it makes the innner-workings of the watch that much more visible. I've had the watch for nearly a month now and it has kept pretty much perfect time; very impressive for an automatic. The two-year warranty, low price (especially on Cyber Monday), and made-in-USA with Swiss technology and I couldn't be happier. This is my first watch from Stuhrling but it will certainly not be my last.

review_headline: A modern, faithful recreation of a WWII flieger watch.
review_body: I now own three LACO B-Uhr watches with Swiss ETA movements. All are top quality in every respect. This model has a hand-winding movement, similar in function to the original flieger watches of WWII. The watch spring will break if you over-wind it !!  Stop winding when you feel increasing resistance (20-25 winds)! If you're looking for the most accurate and practical reproduction of the granddaddy of all pilot watches, this is it. LACO is one of the original five watch companies that produced the 55mm B-Uhr watches for the Luftwaffe. The ETA Swiss movement will last for generations if properly cared for. If you don't like the idea of winding this watch daily, buy yourself one of the less costly LACO quartz watches -- or the automatic movement version of this watch.

product_title: Totoro Wrist Watch 3
review_headline: but a higher quality band would be nice. All in all I am very pleased with ...
review_body:
I purchased this cute little watch as a gift for my fiancé. It keeps decent time, but a higher quality band would be nice. All in all I am very pleased with this item considering the price.

I do want to address something I read in a different review someone left for this item. One customer complained that she was NOT able to open the watch using only his/her fingernail. I repair and sell watches for a living and I must say that you should be concerned if you CAN do that. A watch opened that easily will have zero moisture resistance and will be equally as bad at keeping dirt/dust/other debris out of your watch.

I address this not to attack the person who made this complaint, but in hopes that anyone who reads that particular review will see this and not be dissuaded from making a purchase based on that one comment.

product_title: Casio Men's G9300GB-1 G Shock Digital Quartz Black Solar Watch
review_headline: I'm very happy with the G-Shock G9300GB-1
review_body:
I'm very happy with the G-Shock G9300GB-1. I was looking for my first G-Shock and decided that this was the one I wanted. I initially bought the GA150 but the digitla display was too dark and too small. Plus I wanted a solar watch. I didn't want to have to deal with replacing a battery every 2-4 years.

Pros:
- Blackout display is readable unlike other inverted displays on G-Shock
- Tough Solar. So you don't have to worry about changing batteries
- Compass functionality. I was looking for this
- Looks great

Cons:
- Moon phase functionality. Not really a Con but it was a feature I could live without. When you press on Mode to go through all the functions of the watch, Moon phase, is the first one. I would have preferred it to be last and have something like the stopwatch first.
-When selecting local time, it didn't have my city; Toronto. I had to choose New York for the same timezone. It had other Canadian cities like Vancouver or Edmonton but not Toronto. Not a big issue. Just odd.

The Cons mentioned above are very minor. Overall, I love this watch.

product_title: G-Shock GWM5610-1 Men's Solar Black Resin Sport Watch
review_headline: Easily my favorite watch I've ever owned.
review_body:
By far my favorite watch ever. My first G-Shock was bought a year ago, a GWM-6900-1. I loved it. But I wanted the "Speed Style" squares. I didn't want to give up the solar and atomic features of the 6900 I had, so I had to get this GW-M5610-1.

I ended up selling the GWM-6900-1. I have not regretted it once!

When you first get one of these watches, you will check daily to see if it shows "RCVD". Trust me, that acute and annoying symptom goes away after a few months. I put the watch on daily now and it just works. It doesn't "RCVD" or receive every single day, that's mainly because sometimes I leave it laying on the couch or something in the middle of my house. I would estimate it receives 90% or more of the time though. What is important here though? That it shows perfect time! Even if it skips a few days of receiving, it will still match "official" time.

The battery showed "H" for High when I first got it. It has not changed from that since I got it, but I do work outside quite a bit so it gets to soak up the sun quite often.

I do not know if it is recommended, but I wear mine in the 180°F dry sauna at the gym and it keeps on chugging along (I use it to set timers).

I used to be a "heavy" watch guy. But I sold every single one of my "heavy" watches and now this G-Shock is the only watch I own. It is so light you don't even know it is there until you want to check the time. It is very comfortable, more than the GWM-6900 was for me. I think I have been "Squared" and will probably never go back.Some will tell you fancy bands and adapters are needed, but I just wear it like it was made and I have never had a problem.

This GW-M5610-1 is the best watch all-around. I would recommend this watch to anyone looking for a G-Shock, likes the movie "Speed", and wants a tough watch with useable features without a lot of extras that wouldn't beused.

product_title: [Newly Upgraded] Versa Automatic Double Watch Winder in Black
review_headline: Works Great and My Watch Keeps Time...Beware of the Noise
review_body:
It's been six months since I started using the Versa Watch Winder and I must say that I am very pleased with it's performance. I use it for my Movado watch that I only wear on occassion. It keeps great time on the winder even though I sometimes leave it on there for a couple weeks at a time. The most the time has been off is by 3 or so minutes. My husband uses it for two of his watches, putting the watch he's not wearing in the winder, and he has been pleased as well. He has one cheaper watch that sits in the winder most of the time but he also has an IWG he puts in the winder occassionally when he's not wearing it and it has kept perfect time.

ONE IMPORTANT NOTE: As other reviewers have stated, this winder does eventually make a knocking/clicking type noise. It doesn't happen at first, but by after about four months or so I noticed it. It's pretty loud so if you are planning on keeping this by your bedside, I would not recommend buying it. The noise is not good for sleeping. We keep our winder in our closet so the noise isn't a big deal to us and we can't hear it in our bedroom.

product_title: Seagull Guilloche Elegant Automatic Men's Watch M186s
review_headline: Came in a nice box securely packaged and arrived direct from China without ...
review_body:
Not a big fan of made in China items due to past experiences but I must give credit when it is due. This is an outstanding time piece at very reasonable price. Came in a nice box securely packaged and arrived direct from China without damage.

As for the wrist watch: beautiful domed sapphire dial window, high quality genuine leather strap, classy clasp, hands that appear black but reflect a very cool blue when light hits them. Precision time keeping thus far. I set the watch exactly to official U.S. time and have lost only 5 seconds per day since. Really like that I can stop the second hand when setting the time because it makes exact setting possible.

Read the history of Sea-Gull watch making in China (founded in 1955) and you'll discover that they provide many parts for vaunted "Swiss Made" watches you pay high prices for. CHINA MADE is proudly stamped on this watch and now I understand why. I will be looking to buy more SEA-GULL watches in the future.

product_title: Citizen Women's EW1540-54A Eco-Drive Silhouette Sport Stainless Steel Watch
review_body:
I've only had this for a week, but so far I love it. It was replacing an automatic winding Seiko I had for about 3 years. I tried to get it fixed for about 6 months. It kept getting returned to me, and would eventually stop working again. So the whole first week I had this, I was constantly checking other clocks to make sure it was keeping accurate time. It is! Perfectly!

One thing I didn't realize from reviews that I thought was interesting is that it doesn't require sunlight - even artificial light will charge the watch. Sunlight is more effective, but if you spend lots of time indoors, it should still be fine. I also wear this on my wrist overnight with no issue. With a full charge, Citizen claims it can be left in a dark storage box for 6 months! This is a welcome change from my last watch that charged with movement, because you couldn't really take it off for more than maybe an evening.
