product_title: Casio Men's PRG-270 Pro Trek Triple Sensor Multifunction Digital Sport Watch
review_body:
This is a good watch that provides solid value for your money. As the entry level in the Pro-Trek series, it gives good functionality at a reasonable price. I was really torn between replacing my previously owned Mudman 9000ms with another or, with this watch. I preferred the band of the 9000ms (I actually liked the nubs on the back) but, the readability of the PRG-270 is much, much better. It is very readable in bright light or at night using the back light. The band however, is not as comfortable and frequently pinches and pulls. I had reservations about a solar battery but, it has worked fine thus far, showing a full charge despite my wearing long sleeves most of the time. I'm not a mountain trekker, just someone who lives and works at high altitude. I can't really speak to compass functionality or temperature but, altitude and barometer work fine for my purposes. Keep in mind that altitude is displayed in meters, if you need to know feet, you'll need to multiply by 3.280. This is a mild inconvenience but, it is what it is. Lastly, the manual... printing a booklet this small is simply ridiculous. I have to pull it up online to enlarge it or start looking for a magnifying glass. This is supposed to be a manual, not a used car finance contract.

Summing up, great value for the price but, take off a star for the band and the manual.

product_title: Timex Men's Ironman Classic 100 Full-Size Watch
review_body: This is a great watch.  For swimming, biking, running, and lifting I have found it super useful.  My favorite feature is that it has an interval timer and a countdown timer instead of just a stopwatch.  I do a lot of interval work, and this is exactly what I needed.  Another kind of cool feature is the flick light.  You can set it to turn on the indiglo light when you sort of flick your wrist, so you don't have to use two hands.  I've owned this watch for over two years and it just now needs the battery replaced, which I will be doing ASAP.  Hopefully it keeps on ticking for a long time to come.  EDIT: Replaced the battery with no real issues.  Had to look up a tutorial online, but didn't need any tools I didn't already have.  I've been looking at other fancy watches at running and fitness stores lately, and they frankly don't measure up.  Unless you are looking for a GPS watch or something that tracks heart rate (which will both be much more expensive), there really isn't anything out there better than this.  I use mine almost every day.  The interval function on this watch allows you to set up to 9 unique time intervals and run through them once or automatically repeat at the end.  Most of the much more expensive watches I saw only allowed 2 unique intervals, and the most I saw was 5.  Maybe 2 or 5 is enough for most people, but I have used up to 8 on mine for actual workouts.  If you're just interested in timing things, you can't get much better than this watch.

product_title: Bulova Men's 98A128 Self-Winding Mechanical Watch
review_body:
I'm trying hard to like this watch. As a timepiece, it's great.

As a design statement, I can't tell if it's trying to be a dress watch or not. Crystals on the band and around the bezel scream dress watch. Fake screw heads in the bezel and and notches on the non-rotatable bezel circumference say, it's not dressy.

Then there's the face. Minute hand and 24-hour hands are so close to the center that they are useless for at least four hours of every day. Open heartbeat watches were a novelty for me, but ones that make the face look asymmetrical kind of spoil the look. Then, there's that attempt where they tried to do something with hour markers five through nine. That arc tying the odd-ball markers together with the subdial complications looks like a tilted-head, bug-eyed Gremlin giving me an evil grin. Then what did they do? Add more screw heads at the ends of that arc! There is no lume on those weirdo markers either.

Something about kitchy Bulova designs like his one seem like a betrayal of Bulova history when watches were special.

It was a gift, so I'll wear it when necessary.

product_title: 22mm Premium 2 Piece Ss Silicone Striped Navy Blue / White Interchangeable Replacement Watch Band Strap
review_headline: Excellent 22mm Navy Blue and White striped silicone band.
review_body:
"Premium" silicone watch band, they say? They're right! This 22mm navy blue and white stripe silicone band is indeed premium and is worth the admittedly high $18.95 price tag.

I like silicone watch bands because they are waterproof, soft and flexible. There are other makers including some that make striped and colored bands like this one. These are the best I have found to date and have purchased several over the last 6 months for existing watches in my collection as well as a new watch this band is destined for.

The colors don't bleed. On another manufacturer's bands like this I've bought in the past, the colors tend to bleed so a white looks like a light gray. Not the case with these bands from Clockwork Synergy. The contrasting colors are bright and vivid. What you see on the Amazon product page is what you get. The hardware is nicely polished stainless steel.

These bands already come with spring bars or pins installed. Not just any spring bars, they're quick change bars - no tools needed. As soon as you get the old spring bars off, these go on easily - meaning that you can change looks as frequently as you want. The bars themselves are built into the bands so they won't spring away from you while you're trying to take them off/put them on.

If you look at the underside of the half that has the holes the buckle pin goes through, the holes aren't just straight through. On the underside, it also has the holes drilled at an angle so the buckle pin just slides right in. That's attention to detail!

These are the best silicone bands I've found and I recommend them with five stars.

product_title: Citizen Eco-Drive Men's BM8475-26E Stainless Steel Watch with Leather Strap
review_body:
Mine has a genuine leather band that looks and feels nice, not a stiff, synthetic band.
The display isn't as bright and easy to read as the picture, but it has a nice, unique appearance.
The mechanism has more backlash than my $35 Timex T49963, so it's hard to align the minute hand so it's exactly on a marker when the second hand is at 12 and it doesn't stay aligned - I expected a tighter mechanism.

The luminescence doesn't last very long (none of them do anymore) but this has no backlight (nor did it advertise that it did).
The orange against black display just isn't that easy to read, somehow, I think the hour marks are too thick compared to the thin hands, so it's hard to pick out the hands from all the distractions for my middle aged eyes.

So it's a good, solid and somewhat unique looking watch that probably will outlast my $35 Timex 10:1.
I wouldn't buy it again, but I like it. If you have small wrists, it's not for you.

product_title: Seiko Men's Black Dial Automatic Divers Watch
review_body: A few years back I purchased a Casio dive watch (MDV102) for approximately $60 total.  It wasn't fancy but it was solid, looked good, and did the job.  I recently decided to upgrade with another dive watch and purchased the Seiko SKX173, which actually looks quite similar to the Casio, and which ended up costing slightly more than $220 total.  I've owned Seikos in the past and generally thought they were a good choice, not a Rolex but good value for the money.  However, this latest Seiko turned out to be a disappointment.  First of all, it was very hard to get a good grip on the small knob between the two prongs on the side.  Second of all, despite following the directions closely, I was never able to set the day / date indicators properly.  The day indicator disk seemed to be "sticky" and did not rotate smoothly, if it rotated at all.  Finally, the quality of the numbers and tick marks on the rotating bezel just looked cheap, almost like a circular decal on the metal bezel.  The day / date indicator disks also looked cheap.  Overall, I was disappointed by this Seiko and returned the watch for a refund.  Despite a few dings, the Casio still looks good and works fine.

product_title: Casio Men's Sport Analog Dive Watch
review_headline: Getting More Than You Pay For
review_body: For the price, this is one fine bargain.  While I have not given this watch any major underwater test, I am confident that the 10 Atmosphere water resistant rating would make this watch fine for swimming and shallow diving.  I sail the waters of the Pacific coast and wanted a watch that could handle foul weather and the dousings with salt water heavier weather or the need to clear a fouled prop might bring.  In addition, I wanted a watch that could be read easily in low or no light situations.  Properly "charged" with exposure to sunlight or even a flashlight, the luminescent dial and hands glow all night. Granted, by 05:30 the glow is a bit dim but is actually brighter than my $200 Skagen Titanium watch.  So far, minor bumps to the crystal have not produced any scratches.  I think the notion that one can have such performance for less that $20 is the coolest aspect of this watch.  If it gets damaged from hard use why should I care?  I can just order another.

product_title: Casio Men's PAG240T-7CR Pathfinder Triple-Sensor Stainless Steel Watch with Titanium Bracelet
review_headline: Good looking, but if you actually intend on adventuring with it, think twice.
review_body: This is a great functional watch, don't get me wrong. The thing is, if you are buying it, you most likely are using it for some sort of adventurous purpose, say, finding yourself on a path for example. Well, the metal band will limit the flexibility of your wrists, making it very inadequate for any sort of elevation gain hiking. I flexed my wrist too hard for it and a pin dislodged and the band snapped off. This was the very first time I took the watch out to begin with, and was severely disappointed breaking it unintentionally. A resin band version of this watch would never, ever have such a thing happen to it, and would have been more lightweight to boot. I chose looks over functionality and I paid for it.    The titanium is also only a coating on the band, and it scratches easily. You do not get the weight reduction a full titanium band would give you, which is also purpose defeating.    I have been told the watch is too ugly for formal use, and it's too fragile for adventure use, so I don't see who would actually want this watch. I would recommend the brand, but only ones with resin based bands. Get a nice metal watch for dress and business affairs, but stick to resin if you actually do any sort of real climbing or physical activities with it, or risk the band breaking.

product_title: Yoption Touch Screen Unisex LED Watch Ultra-thin Digital Wrist Watch Black Color
review_body:
The Touch Screen Unisex LED Digital Watch comes in a number of colors, and is priced very affordably at under $6. Basic functions do all work, and its unique/fun to wear. The watch band itself is made out of soft silicon material that is comfortable, but the watch part is made out of plastic on the back (battery compartment, internals), which can be rough on the skin. The fit is overall pretty good, and the actual watch looks accurate when compared to the stock photos.

The watch is splash resistant (rain, sweat), but NOT water resistant, so don't take it swimming! All navigation and settings are done via the front 'touch' part, so the design is quite modern looking (no buttons at all). No instruction manual came with mine, but free digital versions can be found on Google. Works and acts a conversation starter. Very cool night effect under low light conditions, and the LED time is also readable under direct sunlight. The watch' display is usually 'off' to save battery (will last about 1 year), but tapping on the surface of the watch turns the time on (with a nice animation). However, the 'touch screen' part is not 100% accurate. It's more like a giant button that takes up the entire screen than an actual touch sensor like on an iPhone （not capacitive, and there are no fancy touch gestures).

Overall, the watch works as advertised, however, the 'touch' part is not quite as the descriptions might suggest. Still, a pretty cool, inexpensive timepiece.

product_title: Yoption Touch Screen Unisex LED Watch Ultra-thin Digital Wrist Watch Green Color
review_body:
The Touch Screen Unisex LED Digital Watch comes in a number of colors, and is priced very affordably at under $6. Basic functions do all work, and its unique/fun to wear. The watch band itself is made out of soft silicon material that is comfortable, but the watch part is made out of plastic on the back (battery compartment, internals), which can be rough on the skin. The fit is overall pretty good, and the actual watch looks accurate when compared to the stock photos.

The watch is splash resistant (rain, sweat), but NOT water resistant, so don't take it swimming! All navigation and settings are done via the front 'touch' part, so the design is quite modern looking (no buttons at all). No instruction manual came with mine, but free digital versions can be found on Google. Works and acts a conversation starter. Very cool night effect under low light conditions, and the LED time is also readable under direct sunlight. The watch' display is usually 'off' to save battery (will last about 1 year), but tapping on the surface of the watch turns the time on (with a nice animation). However, the 'touch screen' part is not 100% accurate. It's more like a giant button that takes up the entire screen than an actual touch sensor like on an iPhone （not capacitive, and there are no fancy touch gestures).

Overall, the watch works as advertised, however, the 'touch' part is not quite as the descriptions might suggest. Still, a pretty cool, inexpensive timepiece.

review_body: Shipping: Arrived in about a week and a half as opposed to the 4-6 week estimate!    Quality: The quality of the band feels slightly cheap, probably due to how light/hollow it feels.  The color is scratching off near the release button before it was even put on the watch.  Comes with tools to adjust links and pins for attaching to watch.    Fitment: I purchased this band to use with my Moto 360.  One side fit in immediately but the other would not after struggling with for 15 minutes.  I realized that it was the two plastic tabs on the Moto 360 that were keeping it from going far enough in for the pin to meet the holes. product_title: Yoption Touch Screen Unisex LED Watch Ultra-thin Digital Wrist Watch Light Blue Color
review_body:
The Touch Screen Unisex LED Digital Watch comes in a number of colors, and is priced very affordably at under $6. Basic functions do all work, and its unique/fun to wear. The watch band itself is made out of soft silicon material that is comfortable, but the watch part is made out of plastic on the back (battery compartment, internals), which can be rough on the skin. The fit is overall pretty good, and the actual watch looks accurate when compared to the stock photos.

The watch is splash resistant (rain, sweat), but NOT water resistant, so don't take it swimming! All navigation and settings are done via the front 'touch' part, so the design is quite modern looking (no buttons at all). No instruction manual came with mine, but free digital versions can be found on Google. Works and acts a conversation starter. Very cool night effect under low light conditions, and the LED time is also readable under direct sunlight. The watch' display is usually 'off' to save battery (will last about 1 year), but tapping on the surface of the watch turns the time on (with a nice animation). However, the 'touch screen' part is not 100% accurate. It's more like a giant button that takes up the entire screen than an actual touch sensor like on an iPhone （not capacitive, and there are no fancy touch gestures).

Overall, the watch works as advertised, however, the 'touch' part is not quite as the descriptions might suggest. Still, a pretty cool, inexpensive timepiece.

product_title: Casio Men's WV58DA-1AV Waveceptor Digital Atomic Sport Watch
review_body: It's a great way to try a solar/atomic watch for the nominal price of approximately $30.  I've owned mine for two years now, and it sometimes doesn't reset correctly at midnight as it is supposed to.  However, Casio literature does warn you that at certain times of the year the radio signal from Denver is weaker, and may not set your watch, thus you may have to manually set your watch for a while.  It is a classic good looking watch, weighs about 3 ozs, and fairly easy to adjust the band if you need to (see helpful videos on YouTube). It's hard for me to hear the alarm signal on this watch, so this may be a negative.  It's great for astronomy to set your GoTo telescope to the exact time.  Just got a second WV58DA as a backup (consider the very low price), and because of my experience with this watch,have decided to also get an MTG900DA-8V which has features that interest me, including how well your solar battery is charged, and how strong the WWV signal is from Denver.  I'm sold on Casio Solar/Atomic watches.  Once you're accustomed to having the EXACT time when you're out and about, you can't go back.

product_title: Casio Women's STR300 Runner Eco Friendly Digital Watch
review_body:
Looks good on her wrist---not tacky/gaudy like the Timex watches, and does not sacrifice functionality for a dainty/petite size but is not overly bulky either for the female wrist. Have owned Casio digital watches before, and always found them easy to use and very durable, although the plastic face is bound to get scratched much more easily than more expensive mineral glass but good luck finding MG at this price point.

My only small complaints, and the reason why I'm taking away one star:

1. The countdown timer only allows one interval---since interval training is so popular these days, you'd think watch manufacturers would get a clue and add a second interval so that you could do, for example, 2 minute work periods followed by 1 minute rest periods, the way that boxers train.

2. The watch does not display clock time while it is in stopwatch mode, which my other digital watch does...nice to know the ongoing length of a workout or run as well as clock time without need to hit the mode button to go back and forth to the clock...the watch face is more than big enough to do it since it has 3 display lines simultaneously.

Anyway, for the price, and Casio's proven quality, I'm more than happy.

GENERAL
This Intelligent Quartz compass watch comes in dozens of different configurations and features, depending on the model and year. My watch is the T2N721 Tide-Compass-Temp watch. It has a cream (aka natural) colored face, and a brown brushed leather wristband.
It is a large watch, very handsome looking. Interestingly, Timex has sort of hide the name Timex in small font under the top bezel. Anyone looking at the watch being worn will not see that it is a Timex. They will just notice a very attractive looking time piece.
OBSERVATIONS
The brown brushed leather wristband is actually one of the nicest features of this watch. Beautiful medium brown band, almost suede-like, super comfy and durable. Rugged clasp.
The hands of the watch are the same color as the face, making time reading somewhat difficult. Especially with three other hands to sort out. ( Second hand, red indicator hand (aka fourth hand), and highest tide hand).
On the positive side, the hands and dial are very lumenescent, watch is very easy to read in darkness. Go easy using the Indigo light-it is very bright and will drain a battery with regular use.
Mostly this is a temperature taking watch. Two temperature scales, Celcius and Farenhiet, take up a large portion of the watch face. To the extent that there is no room for hour numbers or numerals. Instead, there are small black squares where to indicate the hourly positions. Actually they are not small black "squares", but look like small black trash cans or waste baskets to me. Great for seeing how much time you are wasting at work. And if you are bored, you can always take an ambient room temperature reading.
I would of much prefered to have a moon phase indicator than a temperature feature. Temps are everywhere: on our cell phones, on TV, the radio, and on our little thermometers. Moon phase is not as ubiquitious as temp, and also ismuch more usefull. Plus, this watch would really look awesome with a nice moon phase indicator.
The printing of the watch face is poor. If this watch was made in Switzerland or Japan, all the minute marks would be equi-distant and aligned. But this watch is made in the Phillippines, so we cant expect such attention to detail. The hours 'till high tide and low tide numbers are not aligned with the waste baskets, niether.
There is a silver hand that most people dont know the function of. Timex makes no mentio of it in the directions. Most people think that the function of the silver hand is to make the watch look cool. But it actually has several different functions. This is the "highest" tide indicator.
When setting the high tide hand, when the circle in the silver hand perfectly frames the chrome date bezel, this indicates highest tide. Also useful for reading highest tide.
The compass is a disappointment. Accurate to only + or - 45 degrees. It will give general direction bearing, and often this is all you need. But never depend soley on the watch compass. Make sure you have a real compass on hand as well. (Cell phone compass app should suffice).
The compass is difficult to calibrate. You should be at least 250 yards away from any motor vehicles or iron fences. The directions for calibrating the compass do not remindyou that you need to "set" the red indicator hand (aka fourth hand) first, before you even think about calibrating the compass. Failure to first set the indicator hand first (like I did) makes compass readings be way way off.
The date can be tricky to set also. Here again, the instructions are poorly written. My date was a day off every day, even though I followed the directions and reset the date every day. Anyone experiencing this problem should disregard the date setting instructions. Pull the crown all the way out, (not half way out as per the directions), and advance the watch hands 12 hours. Push crown all the way in when done.
SUMMARY
This watch has been in production by Timex for several years now. This model seems to be being discontinued. It is very hard to find new ones in the box available anywhere at any price now. This particular model, with the cream colored face and brown leather strap is fast becoming a collectors piece, largely due to its beauty. I predict that by Christmas, 2014, you will no be able to find this watch new in the box for sale except for the occasional one on ebay. Expect to pay around $200 US if you find a new one for sale.
I feel lucky to have been able to find a new one for sale. I live on the coast, and I am a boater. The tide, and highest tide feature is very nice and very accurate. Plus, as mentioned, this is a very cool looking watch.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNKM95 Stainless Steel Automatic Watch with Blue Canvas Band
review_headline: Not An Automatic For The People
review_body:
There is no question that when it has came down to great watches, Seiko has been a strong innovator in style and movement for all kinds of companies from Invicta to Android and Citizen. They have made some excellent watches over the years. But nevertheless, they have also made some watches that just haven't made the mark at all in price, but also design. This Amazon exclusive timepiece absolutely is one of the worst-looking Seiko Automatic watches out there. The red face and the blue nylon strap do not go at all, and it makes the design lose its character in class and quality. Not to mention you do not have as much water resistance than other automatic watches on the market. You also only have to wind the watch by the wrist. not by the stem of the piece unlike other automatic watches. Overall, I do recommend you seek a better watch from Seiko for its value. This one doesn't have the appeal that it is shown to have.

Price: C-

Setup & Comfort: C+

Overall: C 1/2+

product_title: Casio Men's AW80V-5BV
review_body: So far, I really like this watch. It doesn't snag the hair on my wrist like a metal bracelet watch does, and yet my wrist doesn't get as sweaty as it would wearing a rubber-strapped watch. It is very functional, too, and I like the alarm function. I have only two minor complaints: first, the light feature is not very bright and it is programmed to only light up for a slit second and then turn off, whether or not you are still holding the button down. So I find myself needing to press it two or three times sometimes before I can read what time it is. It also only lights up the analog face, not the digital face. Second, after only some light use, the buttons are already failing to rebound, or pop back up, upon release after being pressed, causing them to stick. product_title: Casio Men's PRW-3000-1CR Protrek Triple Sensor Multi-Function Watch
review_headline: Good as ABC watch, but it does not seem durable
review_body:
I had this watch for less than one hour before I decided to return it. I really liked it at first. In fact I felt really happy after unpacking it. It had everything I was looking for. The v. 3 sensors were great, the size and weight were perfect for practicing most sports without noticing the watch on your wrist. But then I realized that it had a small defect in the painting of the bezel: a hairline of silver aluminum stood out from the black painting. It was hardly noticeable except when you exposed the watch to daylight. But given that I bought this watch to use it in outdoor activities, I realized soon that the defect, even when minor, was not acceptable. If the bezel was like this before I even started to use the watch, how would the watch hold up after one year of heavy-duty outdoor activities?
I returned the watch the same day and I bought the smaller solar G-shock I found (GWM5610-1). I give the watch 3 stars for its technology, but I take 2 stars out for seeming more fragile than you would expect of a Protrek. I will sincerely miss all the great sensors of this watch and Casio is still my favorite digital watch company. review_headline: the invicta 15072 has a substantial feel and a comfortable bracelet. the coin edge bezel clicks smoothly around ...
review_body: i purchased the invicta 15072 diver analog display from amazon at even lower than the low price listed .  the invicta 15072 arrived a day earlier than scheduled and was brand new ( i can always tell ) .  the invicta 15072 is one of the very few watches still made that display all twelve arabic numbers on the face .  that makes it a collector's item .  it is big and heavy -- but not too big and heavy .  the invicta 15072 has a substantial feel and a comfortable bracelet .  the coin edge bezel clicks smoothly around the dial .  the magnifier makes reading the date easier .  the invicta 15072 is the best inexpensive diver style watch presently available from any manufacturer .  it is simple uncluttered accurate and well built .  the invicta 15072 is supposed to be waterproof down to a thousand feet .  i never get any of my watches wet .  i do not dive or swim and honestly i do not believe that invicta's low priced watches are actually capable of submerging 1000 feet without filling up with water .  i suspect they claim 1000 feet waterproof to sell watches .  the movement is japanese made and the watch is probably assembled in china .  for the price i paid this watch is outstanding .  the watchmaking technology of asian manufacturing has improved 100% in the last few years .  time will tell how long this invicta 15072 holds up .  i highly recommend this watch .  a true bargain .

product_title: Fossil FS4735 Grant Brown Leather Watch
review_body:
Overall, I like the styling of the watch. It's heavy enough to give it a good quality feel and the leather strap is thick enough that it should last a long time. The one major flaw in the design is the chrome hands over a shiny white face. There is not enough contrast between the hands and the face to easily read the time. One has to rotate the wrist to get a reflection on the hands to read the time. It looks good on the wrist, but it's not as functional as it could be. The other flaw is the timer function. The faces of the timers are so small that they are virtually useless. They are there only for the design element, not functionality.

Also, if you're considering this as a gift be aware that it is packaged in a rather cheap and juvenile looking tin box with cardboard lining. This is a $105.00 man's dress watch, but the packaging looks like it was designed for a $25.00 child's watch. This may not matter if it's for personal use, but the presentation is incongruent with what's inside and this may be a show stopper if considering this watch as a gift.

product_title: Citizen Men's CA0265-59E Eco-Drive Titanium Watch
review_body:
Very nice watch (4/5 rating), but I'm going to dwell on the negatives since those can be more helpful in reviews:

Even though the watch lacks a perpetual calendar, you need not worry about resetting it for months with less than 31 days. That's because the date is so small and recessed so deep into the face that it is virtually impossible to see without the aid of a magnifying glass (NOT an exaggeration). This is certainly not evident in the photos and is a major design flaw - no other way to characterize it.

A major reason I purchased this watch was the light-weight Titanium - roughly half the density of steel. Yes, it is lighter than a steel watch with a steel band, but considerably heavier than a steel watch with a leather band. That's not Citizen's fault. That's my own fault for not thinking it through. If you want a really light watch then go for titanium with a leather band!

The large \\"second hand\\" does not work - it is stuck on 12! That's because what would normally be the \\"second hand\\" is used for the chronograph/stop watch. The actual second hand is in one of the tiny insert circles. I prefer the standard second hand layout

After buying the watch, I regretted not getting one with radio control - many available at similar prices. In fact, I just placed an order for Citizen Men's CB0020-50E World Perpetual A-T Dress Watch.

Here are a couple positives that may not be obvious: The actual color is better than it appears in the photo. On my computer screen the watch appeared to be VERY dark green - not quite black. It is jet black. Also, it is much easier to read the time in almost all lighting conditions than some other Citizen watches. I purchased the Citizen Men's AT8013-17E Eco-Drive Limited Edition World Chronograph Dress Watch. It is a beautiful watch but can be difficult to read the time under some lighting conditions unless turned at just the right angle.

Hope my review helps some of you.

product_title: PromiseU Women's Bracelet Tree leaf Decoration Quartz Wrist Watch
review_body: I got this watch in a different color and I love it, but I have to say that it is not high quality, though good enough for less than $10.00. It is unique and cute. I adore the style. Some things I dislike about it are that it only has two size adjustments, which means if you have a small wrist, you'll have to get used to it sliding around like a bracelet and always hanging with the watch face down since that's how gravity likes it. The other thing to beware of is it is absolutely not water resistant. Even running water over it for a second will cause it to get water droplets on the inside, though they will dry out. My latest issue is that I went swimming with it on by accident and the face filled up with water. It stopped ticking for several minutes, but then came back to life for about a day even with the water still sloshing around inside of it. Now it's rusting and has stopped again, which is why I'm here because I really want another one! I got the brown one originally for a more natural look, but now I am interested in trying white because I'm going to a wedding soon and I think it will match what I'm going to wear. Another thing to mention is it jingles a lot because it has loosely connected metal pieces to support its style and they clank together when you move. It reminds me of a dog's collar, but I guess some bracelets jingle like that anyway. I think the cuteness makes up for the low quality. Just don't have high expectations and you'll be able to enjoy it for what it is. It's not the type of watch that you strap on tight and position it perfectly. It's more like snap it on and view it as a fun decorative thing with a cheap clock attached. I can see why some reviewers think it's crappy while others love it. Its biggest strength is style and concept, but not reliability, and you have to come to terms with that or else you may be setting yourself up to feel disappointed. For $5.00, I'd say it's reasonable. I'm giving it four stars because it's not excellent,but I'm very pleased with it and would buy it again.

product_title: Invicta Men's 6412 Python Collection Stainless Steel Watch with Link Bracelet
review_headline: If it doesn't do its thing, it ain't nothing but bling.
review_body:
First I need to say that the watch does not look like the one in the picture. The minute and hour hand are silver with white only at the end of the hour hand and a thin white line on the inside of the minute hand. It is difficult to quickly tell the time because you need to look for the hands which are lost against the busy face (the lines at the 5 minute marks are also silver not white as they appear in the photo) Silver on silver is like white ink on paper. In the photo you can easily and quickly tell what time it is as they appear to be white hands over a black face providing good contrast. This is a major drawback for me because knowing the time is the only reason I wear a watch. It also states in the ad that the hands and markings are luminescent. This is simply not true. They are silver. Forget about reading the time in low or no light.

The chrono function worked about 6 times when I first used it. It then suddenly got off calibration in two separate directions. I have done both the standard reset and the factory/battery reset described in the manual and online. Neither of these methods corrected the calibration. As a result, within 3 hours of receiving the watch it no longer works as it should. The elapsed minute dial is off by -1 minute and the large second hand is off by +6 seconds. With no usefull chrono function I am simply left with a watch that is very hard to read in the daytime and useless in the dark.

It is a great looking watch. Seriously, this thing is beautiful! It has a great price too. But if it doesn't do its thing, it ain't nothing but bling.

Amazon is of course AWESOME and is refunding my purchase price. I am once again looking for a new watch and will probably go back to a more expensive but superior Smith & Wesson. I highly recommend that you buy your watch from Amazon - just not this one. Good luck guys.

review_headline: Beautiful design, neat appearance, but it's extremely difficult to see the digital faces.
review_body:
Firstly, the watch came at the designated time and period which it stated (Bravo to supplier). The watch sits on the hand comfortably and I am an fairly built guy. However the band softness can give the feel of inferiority and cheapness.The band has a nice light eggshell gloss to it (No shine just a notch above matte).

The only issue that made this watch a non five star is that the most important aspect of any watch is the users ability to tell the time by it which have proven difficult from two aspects of this watch: Digital display is difficult to read , and the light is inadequate.

The digital background for this watch is black on clear, the digits are small which really isn't the issue, but because of the dark appearance of the watch face, reading time off the digital display an above average task. I found my self having to adjust my view of the watch face several time before I could have read the display.

Light on this watch serves not purpose to read the digital display. The watch gives off a orange light from a led located six o'clock of the watch, however this serves no purpose since the light only illuminates the analog hands of the watch and not the digital display located beneath the analog surface of the watch.

product_title: Timex Unisex Weekender Analog Quartz Watch
review_body:
I bought this to have a simple, nylon-banded watch that I could wear instead of the litany of metal strap watches I have. It looks great and the indiglo is handy to have, the color and style are nice and understated and have elicited several compliments. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end.

The first problem I had was timekeeping. The watch seemed to repeatedly be losing about 4-5 minutes a week. I stopped wearing it and it kept time pretty well, losing about a minute a week, which I understand is not out of the realm of acceptability. I've just come to understand that the way I wear this watch somehow manages to affect the movement or adjust the dial in such a way that stops time somewhat regularly.

Finally, and critically, this watch is loud. I know what you're thinking, because I thought it too - How loud can a watch really be? Well, distractingly loud. The volume you can hear across your 20 foot-long bedroom while a fan is on high kind of loud. It's distracting when I'm wearing it and a simple, understated watch should not be distracting. I've had to start leaving it in other rooms at night so my wife can sleep and I dislike putting it on in the morning because I know it's going to be a pain to listen to all day long.

This is a nice watch and I love the style, but I would absolutely not buy it again.

review_body:
I originally ordered a 78" cover to use over my rowing machine. It isn't designed to be outside, so I needed a waterproof cover. We have high winds, so it couldn't be flimsy or it would shred. Although not designed for the shape of my machine, it was so close that it adapted perfectly - especially with the draw strings, which DO work.

The product is a heavy canvas. All the seams are flat-felled and double-stitched. The drawstrings are substantial, but have a quick slide so they are easy to use. Because of the weight of the material, you need to work the gathers around the first few times to adjust to your chaise. After that, the stretch in the drawstring will allow you to take the cover on or off without undoing the drawstring - it just pops back to the tight shape!

100% waterproof and substantial enough for any weather. They also look attractive. Right now they have some pollen on them, so I am just going to hose them off. Comes with a custom bag to make it easy to store the cover when not in use. Terrific product and a good value at this price. Much better than the lighter-weight, water-resistant, beige versions you find at box stores.

I ordered a second in the 66" to see if it fit my regular-size chaises. Perfect again, and ample enough that I can leave the back up and the cushion on the chaise. Today I am ordering a second one for my other chaise.

product_title: Sprout Men's ST/7006BKNV Multi-Function Tree Bark Dial Navy Corn Resin Bracelet Watch
review_body:
Surprisingly light at just 1.8 oz. (compared to say, my 45mm Fossil at 5.5oz), which may or may not be a plus, depending on what your preferences are. There are several prior reviews suggesting that the light weight results in problems with the strap/clasp breaking. While I have not had any issues in that regard, time will tell. Also, most likely as a result of the light weight, the overall feel of the watch is somewhat cheap, so if you are looking for a big, bulky, heavy watch, this one is not for you.

Also of note is that after more than 4 decades of wearing a variety of wristwatches (yeah, even one of those calculator watches in the 80s), this watch was the first one I have ever needed to read the instructions to be able to set it. While setting the time is straightforward, the date is a little more difficult and setting the day is downright ridiculous. The instructions can be found under the \\"customer support\\" link of the Sprout Watches homepage.

I was specifically looking for a lightweight watch I could wear on a tropical vacation without having to worry about breaking (or losing) one of my more expensive ones and this fit the bill perfectly, even more so at the Gold Box price. I would have second thoughts at its \\"regular\\" sales price and probably not recommend it at its \\"retail\\" price (unless your needs are a super eco-friendly watch).

review_body:
It did exactly what it was supposed to do, and did it well. I have seen complaints that it is hard to adjust. If so, then try this, it shouldn't take more than 5 minutes:
1. Insert the proper set of tips into the wrench.
2. Adjust the lateral setting until the two farthest tips fit into the holes or slots on the watch back 1/3 circle away from each other.
3. Twist the handle to adjust the third tip until it fits the remaining hole or slot.
4. Fine tune
5. Press down firmly and turn.

product_title: Timex Unisex T2N893 Weekender Silver-Tone Watch with Leather Band
review_body:
Yes, this watch does have an audible tick. This was possibly the first thing I noticed about it. It doesn't bother me, and I no longer notice it until I am either thinking about it or in very silent situations, but if this kind of noise bothers you, do avoid this watch.

The strap stretches. As do the holes. I started wearing it on the second or third holes alternately, depending on how tight I wanted it or how active I was going to be. I've had it over a year and now have to wear it on the fourth hole because of both looseness and enlarging of the third hole. I don't believe this is a problem as a) I will no doubt just keep using new holes through its life and b) we're on amazon and the options for new straps are plenty (I am actually looking at this watches listing again because I had been considering getting a new strap just for different fashion settings.

Considering fashion, this watch and strap combo is exactly what I want in a watch. It looks great with a t-shirt, jeans and sneakers, but I've also worn it with a suit and it doesn't look overly out of place. I'm at college in the north-east and I think it's a great look for a young guy. I don't want to look like I'm over-dressing with a dress watch, nor do I want to wear a digital or sports watch around like a kid.

People are giving the thin strap a hard time, and while I would like to defend it (it does look good and not too aggressive as some heavy leather can), it is soft and malleable and does slip out of its little metal loops quite easily if you're wearing it on the outer holes (ie if you have large wrists).

product_title: Seiko Men's SNK809 Seiko 5 Automatic Stainless Steel Watch with Black Canvas Strap
review_headline: Worked for less than a year
review_body:
I just purchased my first "proper" automatic watch (german build, swiss movement) which reminded me of this sad creature sitting in the bottom of my sock drawer, years of inoperable service since purchase. I just pulled it out and was compelled to share my experience.

I remember happily wearing this rugged watch with decent reliability for a time (believe I bought this in 2008), but within about 6 months it would be completely stopped when I put it on each morning. Of I thought I simply wasn't winding it enough and would even consciously wind the watch gently in my hand while sitting at my desk; same problem every morning. Eventually I just gave up and started wearing a quartz Victorinox until my most recent purchase.

If it worked, this watch would be pretty ideal - it has great styling and a comfortable feel to fit most occasions. That is all quite secondary though to its actual reliable operation. The movement also has a very noticeable and unsettling metal-sliding-against-metal sound.

I realize that this watch isn't meant to compete with a Swiss movement but after seeing it in action there really is just no comparison. I also think it's a little silly that the cost to service this piece would have been substantially more than buying a new watch.

Save your hard earned dollars and buy a serious watch, even a quartz, this one will unfortunately let you down.

review_headline: Handsome watch, but the band is uncomfortable.
review_body:
This is a great-looking watch that can be bought for looks alone.

There are some concerns about function.

1) The backlighting is only partial; it's not a full backlight - - you basically get a halo that doesn't work well to help you tell the time. Timex does a much better job on its other watches with the backlight feature.

2) The band is soft rubber or plastic that traps sweat and tugs on arm hair - - which wouldn't be such a problem if this watch wasn't so….

3) Heavy. This is a heavy watch, and very sturdy. You'll know you remembered to put this watch on in the morning because the weight will gladly let you know.

Overall, this is a good, beautiful watch. Timex could improve it by replacing the band and using lighter components.

review_body: The rangeman is one of the newer models of the sensor variety and you will like its functions and versatility. The negative display will grow on you and it is plenty readable in most lighting situations. It has a back light so it is usable in any light for the most part. It is a little shinier than many Casio's but on the same note it is blacked out on the top. The screws and button on top are black so it balances out that way. It is light weight on the wrist and the band keeper stays put well which can a little bothersome on some watches. It is tough and useful and the compass and barometer and altitude work well enough for almost any scenario. I have four triple sensors and the compasses' work well and these new gen sensors seem to be more accurate. These are not weather stations but they do provide a good general picture of coming weather changes well before the tv weather man gives them to you. If I were lost somewhere I would love having one of these with me. This watch is a good choice for those guys who like gadgets that do something useful in their lives.

product_title: Casio Men's PRG-270-4CR "Pro Trek" Digital Sport Watch
review_body:
Through years I have owned several models of Pathfinder and Protrek watches. The basic functions of this watch are no different than any of the many models which came before this one. This is the basic model of Protrek watch which houses the third generation sensor module with improvement in accuracy and seize, improving overall measurement performance and overall weight of the watch.

This particular model the PRG 270-4CR is very light on the wrist and sometimes you feel like your not wearing a watch. The weight difference is significant. I can tell the difference between this model and the PAG 240-1K or even the PAW 1500-1VR. The overall operation and functionality of this watch does not differ from previous models of Pathfinder or Protrek watches. Therefore, if You've owned any of the previous models, you shouldn't have to deal with a big learning curve as the basic functions have not change at all.

The one thing this watch has is BAD display visibility. It is horrible you literally have to be outside in a real sunny day or well lit room to see the display, let alone any of the readouts this watch is capable of giving you. My advice by a different model of the PRG 270. There is at least 4variations of the 270 which are positive display models:

1) PRG 270-1
2) PRG 270B-2JF ( Blue Japanese Import Model with a Nato Strap for a band)
3) PRG 270B-3JF (Olive Drab Japanese Import Model with a Nato Strap for a band)
4) PRG 270D-&JF (Silver Japanese Import Model with a Titanium Metal Band)

I gave it the two star rating because the way I see it, this watch is a piece of equipment. Especially if you like to be in nature you need a watch that will be a tool which could help you survive if need be. If you can't read the display of it, then is pretty useless in my book. I returned mine for a refund. Will order the Olive Drab version of it.

* The crown guard is a nice homage to the Graham Chronofighter Teapot.
* The constellation of star logos on the bezel makes me shine like a star.

Cons:
* It runs a little fast, but I can't complain because of the prominent disclaimer on the dial that shouts "HIGH SPEED" in all uppercase letters.

product_title: Seiko Men's STP011 Digital Display Japanese Quartz Silver Watch
review_body:
Bought this specifically from amazon just in case something went wrong and guess what, something did. This doesn't ship internationally so I had it mailed to a relative then spent $40 to have it shipped to me (yes, I wanted it that bad as a birthday gift for my husband). When I got it, I compared it to his seiko kinetic and it's a lot more heavier and bigger, but I still hoped my husband would like it. He looked somewhat pleased when he opened it and the FIRST THING he does is press the mode button AND THE BUTTON POPS OUT, SPRING AND ALL!

I called Amazon immediately and the rep told me she'll email me a PREPAID international return label and for me call around the 21st to check if they've got it in stock again and I can request a replacement instead of a refund. She also said that Amazon jewellery and watch department would ship the replacement directly to me for free (I've ordered a lot of items from amazon that shipped internationally to me directly so I believed her). When I got the email it WAS NOT a PREPAID return label, had to call again, was told by another rep to just pay the return shipping (which turned to be almost $30) and when they receive the item, they will refund me. At this point, I'm out $70 just in shipping costs. As instructed, I called to check if watch is in stock to request replacement, this rep tells me that she can request a replacement but it would CAN ONLY to be shipped to the original address (regardless of what I was previously told) and my only other option was to get a refund and just order the item again to have it shipped to a different address which as it turned out can only be within the US. So she expected me to shell out yet another $40 in shipping if I wanted this watch replaced.
Well you can guess what my answer to her was. I told her I just wanted my full refund now plus shipping costs. She placed me on hold to talk to her supervisor and when she got back with me said that she has put in the full refund with return shipping cost ONLY and it will take about 3 days for the refund to appear in my account.

So, I am still out $40 for shipping costs of a defective item and having HAD faith in Amazon. Didn't expect this from Amazon and am very very disappointed.

product_title: Wittnauer 12D100 Montserrat Collection 16 Diamond Quartz Mens Watch
review_body:
This picture doesn't do the watch justice. This is truly a classic piece that a man shouldn't ignore. I've had this watch 8 years and it still runs very accurately. I've gotten so many good comments and second-looks from people regarding this watch. This will always be a keeper in my collection of watches.

Since then, I've moved on to a Tag Heuer Automatic Carerra Day-Date and a two-tone Raymond Weil Automatic Freelancer (skeleton at the 12 O'clock). This Wittnauer for cosmetics definitely competes with these more expensive watches. I've scratched the crystal off concrete and never leaves a scratch (sapphire crystal is the second hardest mineral known to man-----for that reason, the only thing that can scratch the crystal is a diamond). The butterfly clasp is very secure. The two-tone black bracelet is AMAZING! Most black watches should come with this.

In general, for a swiss made watch, you'll definitely get you bang for the buck. Also, this will outshine a Movado (which I truly hate bc they're so over-rated and over-priced). Get this watch and enjoy the beauty and the many years of comments that you will get.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNK803 Seiko 5 Automatic Watch with Beige Canvas Strap
review_body:
This is my third "Seiko 5". I inherited two from my father a few years ago and was impressed with the clean design and heavy feel of quality Seiko watches possess.

This is supposedly a military watch style (as used in Iraq), but it does not have a 24 hour face. In fact, the minute hand and 60 second number display dominates the face. The unusual and very appealing light sand, or tan, color of the face is what drew me to this particular watch. And, with the khaki color canvas strap, the watch is simple, tasteful, attractive, fetching, masculine, and classy. Pick your favorite adjective! A few people have already commented on the unusual and nice looking watch I am wearing.

The weekend days are lettered in blue. The dial and hands glow in the dark. The band is exceptionally well made with reinforced stitching. The clear back allows one to view the interior movement of the watch. The watch case is anodized a dull gray to cut down on reflection as one would expect with a military style watch. It is also waterproof. This is simply a first-class timepiece.

The first watch I ordered and immediately returned was defective. It ran fast by 6 minutes a day! After a couple months I decided to re-order. These are self-winding, mechanical watches but this one is incredibly accurate! I set it four days ago and it is still spot on. So far I cannot detect any change in the time. It is still where I set it from a quartz master clock. That is spooky.

I needed this watch like I needed a hole in my head. I have too many watches! But its distinctive and retro appearance was irresistible. So was Amazon's price. It was simply love at first sight!

June 2015 update:

I am still wearing my military Seiko 5 every day. The cloth khaki band needs to be cleaned now and again to brighten it up. The watch still keeps great time for a self wind. Still love the watch!

product_title: Avalon EZC Unisex Voice Series Low Vision Gold-Tone 4-Button Talking Watch, # 2608
review_headline: Great for Someone Whose Mobility Is Not Impaired
review_body:
The good thing about this watch is that even my severely hearing-impaired mother can hear the voice for the date and time. And the face and hands are visible to someone with limited vision, such as someone with macular degeneration.

Because her arms do not have a normal range of motion, my mom was unable to put the watch (on her wrist) up to her ear (or even her face) with one arm, and push the buttons with the fingers of the hand on the other arm.

I took the watchband off and attached a gold loop to the pin that usually holds the band. Then I fastened a gold chain through the loop. The chain is long enough for her to put on and take off without unfastening it. Now she can bring the watch up to her face and see which button she's pushing, and the watch is close enough to her ears that she can also hear the voice.

product_title: Seiko QHE086SLH Alarm Clock - 3.5 in. Wide
review_body:
This alarm clock is a great deal; so reasonably priced, decent looking, and works perfectly. The smooth-sweep second hand makes the clock virtually silent. If you put your ear right up to it you can hear a faint hum of gears, presumably, but definitely can't hear it easily even a few inches away and quite silent in normal use next to the bed. And I have good hearing and notice sounds outside and in other rooms at home quite easily.

This Seiko keeps very accurate time to the second in the few weeks I've had it, and other Seiko clocks and watches I own have always been spot on for years of dependable service. The little light (on by pressing snooze button on top) is faint as others have noted, but adequate for me to see and not too bright at night which I would find more annoying than being a little dim. I like that there is glow in the dark material (lines on hour and minute hands, dots on clock face) which lasts through the night surprisingly. And I am glad that the green alarm "on" signal isn't a light but is a green dot in a little window; a light would be too bright and just one more thing which could burn out. The snooze button is easy to use and I love the 5 minute interval timing which I use once or twice each morning before finally getting up. The alarm hand is quite accurate even though it's analog, not digital, very reasonable fine tuning quality.

And to confirm: the clock is 3.5" square. A little larger than the classic Braun that I was replacing, but I actually like the size now that I've been using it. I miss the old Braun as it was a beautiful little clock but this Seiko has grown on me quickly and it's even quieter than my Braun (and the poor reviews of the newly reissued Brauns indicate that the quality of those has dropped noticeably...which is too bad!). All in all this alarm clock is a definitely a five-star product to me!

product_title: SE JT6216 21-Piece Watch Repair Kit
review_headline: GREAT KIT - BUT WHERE ARE THE INSTRUCTIONS?
review_body:
When you take a look at all you get, it's a wonderful value for less than $8! If you bought retail at your local hardware, first, you wouldn't find these things and second, it would cost you more than this just for the pliers, let's say, or the hammer. I ordered it to size a new watch I bought online. You can poke out the pin that holds the sizing links without this gear, but you risk damaging the band. See the blue plastic vice and the black square watchband holder? These, plus a punch (provided) and the small hammer, make it easy (plus the needlenose pliers to pull out the pins once you have them started). By the way, quite a few reviewers said they broke gear on their first try. Some of the parts are small and delicate - like the pins and inner workings of a watch itself. Take it easy, people!).

A local jewelry store wanted $12 plus tax to size the watch, so you can see, for $8, I saved money by sizing one band only - AND I will never have to do such a thing at a jewelry store again. Plus, with the jewelers' screwdriver set and the red-handled knife, you can pry the back off most watches and change the battery yourself - or use the metal watch vise to unscrew a screw-down back.

This is great value, but I knocked one star off because there is no instruction book included. A few cheaply printed pages (as long as the English was good and the instructions clear) were all that was needed. The product description on Amazon does include a link to a website. (They complicated this needlessly by trying to add html formatting which doesn't work). You can copy-and-paste the link I repeated below, where you will find the instructions you need. product_title: Timex Unisex Weekender Analog Quartz Watch
review_body:
I purchased this watch as an everyday watch which could stand up to day to day abuse/use. And I’ve not been let down!

PROS:
- Price. The price vs value for the watch is wonderful. It is cheap enough that if I lost it or banged it up too bad, I would not worry about purchasing a replacement.
- Quality. The watch itself has held up to several years of day to day use. Cold, heat, and humidity (even being left in a hot car for a week) didn’t adversely affect this watch. Amazing quality which holds up to the Timex name
- Readability. My eyes are not the best, but the high contrast hands against the background make it easy for me to quickly read… and after all, that is the purpose of a watch.
- Stylish. I enjoy wearing this watch to any casual to semi-formal events. It fits with most men’s outfits and only looks out of place in high formal events.
- Band replacement is a snap! Probably the easiest band to replace ever!
- Feel. The band has never caused any issues with my skin. It feels comfortable
- Waterresistant. I like that I can take the watch into the shower, or when close to water. I really like not having to be worried about another electronic device.
- Indeglow!!! Baby, I love this!!! When it is dark, I don’t have to take out my bright cell phone to know the time, just a quick button push and I can see the clock face. Wonderful invention which works so well… even on the black watch face!

CONS:
- The watch band itself does not hold up well with time. It is something that needs to be replaced every 18 months or so. Where it has worn out for me is where the pin intersects the band holes. Simply put it starts to break down and defray after a while.
- Band selection. While it is easy to find a variety of watches at the store, it is much harder to find replacement bands… but then again, you can pick on and order it online.

product_title: ESS Mens Black Leather Automatic Mechanical Watch Skeleton Swiss Design Man WM096
review_headline: A Great Mechanical Watch for the Price
review_body:
At less than $15, there is not a better mechanical watch that looks as elegant or works as functional. It took much less longer to ship here from China than I thought, so props to the seller and the shipping services on that. When I first opened it up, it was miraculously still running, and only 5 minutes off the right time. How that happened, I have no idea.

Anyway, I found that the build construction of the watch is extremely durable. The main rose-gold body and functional parts of the watch appear to be made of stainless steel while the black part of the casing seems to be a sort of die-cast. I would take caution in bumping the watch on the black part though, as the paint does seem to chip and scratch easily. I saw that many other reviewers did not care for the band, but I find it comfortable and complements the overall look of the watch. It does seem like it may break after many, many on and offs, though, but I see that it can easily be replaced since the bars that hold it in place are removable via springs.

The functionality of the watch itself is accurate and convenient. The watch takes a lot of winding though, which should be expected because it has a large power capacity. I usually wind it for about 10 minutes in the morning while watching a video, then I wind it occasionally throughout the day while it's still on my arm. I don't think I will ever wind it all the way, just to prolong the life of the spring. (A side note about winding, after a while, I noticed the winding became harder after a few days, even if the spring was nowhere near wound the full way. This can be fixed by popping the crown out, then pushing it back in. Then the winding goes back to normal tension. Not a big deal, but just something to keep in mind.) The watch appears to stay accurate as the day progresses. I expected it to lose time as it ticked on, but it seems to gain about a minute every two days. It's not much of a hassle to readjust it anyway, only takes about 10 seconds.

The mechanism itself inside the watch looks amazing, which is the main reason I decided to buy this skeleton watch. It seems to be similar to that of other watches I see on Amazon by different companies, leading me to assume that the companies only make the case and not the actual parts. But, this one caught my eye the most as it is not too formal that it would look out of place wearing it on a normal day, and is just enough to be able to catch a few eyes. I get many compliments from people saying they like the watch. Even from someone who owned an expensive Invicta, but of course I did not hint to them the price of this.

I was expecting the watch to be almost useless in the dark, so I thought I would just pull out my phone then and check the time. But, on the contrary, I was especially surprised to see that the white portion of the hands are actually coated with glow-in-the-dark paint. This further adds to the functionality of the watch and just makes it that much better.

So, as a summary, here is a list of the pros and cons:
Pros:
Looks great and functions well
Holds a nice amount of power from the spring
Glow-in-the-dark paint on the hands
Durable build construction
Comfortable to wear
Water resistant as well (wouldn't recommend testing it)
Get lots of compliments from it

Cons:
Band may break after repeated uses
Takes a lot of winding
Winding tension becomes stiffer sometimes, but is fixed by popping the crown out and back in
Gains a minute every 2 days or so.
Die-cast portion scratches paint easily

As far as I can say, the pros greatly outweigh the cons. And for $15, how can this price be beat? I am greatly pleased with the look, functionality, and comfort-ability this watch provides, and hope it will be able to serve me for many years to come.

product_title: G-Rescue Solar Atomic Classic Color Watch
review_body:
Let me start with the only negative point: the "screws" on top. They're apparently just decorative and don't serve a purpose. I just got mine and noticed they're already loose, I found that they're not really screws because when I tried to tighten them they just spun in place. I'm assuming they'll fall out sooner or later, like others have said.

That being said, I think the positives outweigh the negatives with this one. Atomic timekeeping is great, select your home city and push a button and it calibrates in a few minutes. Also auto calibrates every night. Solar powered speaks for itself. Tide and moon charts appear to be accurate. Buttons are large and easy to push, which is a big deal if you have larger hands like me. The band is very comfortable and is a bit nicer than other generic resin watch bands. The watch itself is a bit larger but if you're buying one like this you probably don't care. I work in law enforcement and this watch looks very sharp in uniform.

Overall would recommend.

product_title: Citizen Men's JY0005-50E "Eco-Drive Skyhawk A-T" Stainless Steel Watch
review_body: I loved this watch and would have rated it a 4 up until recently.  What keeps me from a five star rating is the complicated use of the functions.  It is difficult to memorize how to do everything on the watch and you need to go to the manual, which I keep on my iPad, to look up infrequently used functions.  After 3 years and 1 month the analog hands on the watch stopped.  I followed the instructions in the manual to reset it.  It would not reset and went to "ERR" (error) mode in the digital window.  The owner's manual says to ship the watch to Citizen when you get the ERR displayed.  Once Citizen looked at it they said the watch had been dropped and had a dent in the case.  I did not know of any dent in the case or off any dropping of the watch.  Bottom line, Citizens five year warranty is subjective with the customer having little say.  If you are an active person and want a watch that handles shock well, this isn't the watch for you.  For the first two years I owned this watch I set behind a desk much of my time.  During the third year of ownership I was retired and much more active.  I would have probably been better off with a Casio or Seiko.  I bought a Casio Parhfinder to replace this failed Citizen.  Citizen offered to fix my failed watch by putting a whole new movement in it for $200.  I bought the Pathfinder for less than that and it's a lot better.  Also, when talking with someone at Citizen about their solar power, they indicated the sensor only lasts for 5-7 years.  So, do not expect a $500 plus Citizen to last.a lifetime or be passed down to a child.

review_body:
This is the second G-shock I purchased. I like the white color on this model the most. Smaller Face and Smaller structure than my other bulky G-shocks.

And to be honest, since I have small wrist, and this is the one that fits the most. Since its small slim structure, I especially like it when I wear long sleeve or jacket. Don't you thought so?

Small face but has big digit which is very easy to read. It has all the info I need on it. Especially, the Day of the week is in three digit, ig. SUN, not SU. Also moon graph and tide graph are the features I like the most.

In addition, also has regular stopwatch, world time, countdown timer and 2 alarms.

The set up of world time, Tide and Moon graph (UTC time Differential and Lunitidal Interval) are all manual, and may be a bit confusing once you just getting start setting it. Once you read the manual through, you will be fine. It's all base on your current location. Remember that.

The only down side is the button is a bit small to press on it. I have to use my nail to click it. Not a big deal though.

Overall, very solid, functional and stylish G-shock for those don't like bulky ones. This is a very good choice. Highly recommended !

product_title: Rotary GLE00007-10 Men's Editions Automatic Partially See Thru Silver/Black Dial Black Genuine Leather
review_body:
This is one of the finest "budget" automatic watches I've found in a long time. I have the variant with the blue hands, which I can't find for sale anymore, but otherwise it's the same watch as this. The fit and finish is impeccable; also, for a watch that rumor has it that it's made with more cheaply-sourced SE Asian movement parts, I've never seen such a one possess such accuracy.

Especially for a non-regulated, non-specialist serviced automatic, this keeps impeccable time, accurate to within a minute in a 24-36 hour period. That's just unheard of for a budget automatic.

The ergonomics are fantastic as well, and I've never had one lay so perfectly on my wrist. I'm an orchestral percussionist, and, until now, I've never been able to find a watch that I can actually keep on my wrist while playing, for they all tend to slide around or bunch down on my wrist and impede my arm and wrist dexterity. On the contrary with this one -- with the curved body-back, it simply sits exactly where I put it and does no slip-sliding. It may be a cliche, but it's a dream come true for this musician. And it's incredibly comfortable to wear: even though it possesses significant heft, I very quickly forget that I have it on.

My only quibble is that the deployment clasp is a little infirm on one side, so the locking mechanism often comes loose from the band on one end when I take it off; however, this only happens when I'm taking it off or putting it on and NEVER happens when I'm wearing it. It's really just a minor annoyance.

Overall, this is one of the best watch purchases I've made in a long time. I think this whole style line has been discontinued, at least according to the Rotary site (all instances of this watch are gone as of the New Year), so grab one while you still can.

An ENTHUSIASTIC 5 stars for this baby!!!! =)

product_title: SE JT6216 21-Piece Watch Repair Kit
review_headline: Understand I got what I paid for
review_body:
These are not professional tools. They are very inexpensive and come in one of those tough to open plastic clam containers. The tools are cheaply made and fall apart very easily. My needle nose pliers were broken on the end and unusable, the pieces were not in the container, so that means the pliers were broken before being put in the container. Luckily I had another pair of needle nose pliers prior to this purchase. Everything is poorly made but functional. I expected something like this going in because of the low cost of the tools. However, I had 4 watches I needed to remove the links from and this worked fine. 3 watches required the pins to be hammered out, the other was the removal of small screws. This did the job without damaging the watch in anyway. I will not use these tools to remove the back of the watch, or replace batteries as I fear it would do damage.

If you purchase this, understand it is not for the long haul and if you only have a few small tasks to perform on a watch. If that is all you need, then this is great and cheap. If you plan to do anything more, spend the extra money and get a better set of tools or take your watch to a professional.

product_title: Ks Royal Carving Mechanical Skeleton Black Men's Wrist Watch KS114
review_body:
This is my sixth skeleton watch and by far my favorite. It's a large watch which, though undesirable to some, I really like since it's a skeleton. The watch's works are quite visible and more revealing than my other watches. It's a very handsome watch and presents as of good quality, well made. The brass frame of the skeleton looks well machined and contrasts nicely with the watch's black case and strap.
The watch keeps good time and the self wind mechanism works well (if worn through the day).
My only criticism and the reason I gave it 4 stars is that the case, though stainless steel, is painted black vs anodized. When it arrived there was a very small but visible spot were the paint was not present. A sharpie provided an easy fix. Sounds cheesy but worked very well.
To sum up, I give this watch high marks. For a relatively inexpensive time piece it looks quite sharp, functions well and presents its skeleton works nicely.

review_headline: Irritating, won't be getting another Stuhrling again.
review_body:
Let me first say that I love the design of the watch and have no problems with it mechanically and superficially it only came with one small flaw that is barely noticeable.

The issue I take with this watch is that you can only remove 2 links from each sides of the clasp, and the band itself is quite large. So I find myself in the awkward position of having a wrist that is apparently too small for its smallest size. I went to a jeweler to see if there was anything I could do to make the band smaller and he told me that most watch makers offer smaller sized bands, but I would have to get one from them as there was nothing else he could do. So I go home, and do some searching around and turn up nothing in regards to being able to purchase another band. A bit peeved, I email their customer service to see what I should do. This is what I was told:

Once all the removable links are taken out you cannot size the bracelet any smaller.

Gee, thanks Stuhrling. If you had bothered just making 2 more links removable instead of permanent it would have ensured anybody could use your watch, now I'm stuck with a worthless piece of metal and crystal that's only worth the weight of the materials to me. Not impressed at all by the company, and will certainly not be purchasing anything further from them. Now to see if I can send it in for a refund...

product_title: Casio Men's PRG-270 Pro Trek Triple Sensor Multifunction Digital Sport Watch
review_headline: Good value for what it offers
review_body: I've had this watch for several weeks now. Documentation states that the sensors are factory preset and should not need adjustment. That was not true for the barometer, altimeter and thermometer. However once they were set properly they seem to work fine. Time was set to Japan time out of the box but once set to my time zone it was correct. The compass matches my iphone perfectly out of the box so I'm assuming it's right on. The altimeter read 330 feet out of the box which was way off. I live in Florida with an elevation of about 15 feet at my home. I have hardly any elevation here so will have to wait until I take a vacation to test it. I had to set the barometer to the most recent reading off of the internet for my city. Since then it has stayed accurate. The thermometer was off by about 5 degrees out of the box but has stayed accurate after being corrected. You do have to take the watch off and make sure that all of your body heat is gone from it before getting an accurate temperature reading. Documentation is not bad just takes a little time to get the hang of doing everything but no big deal. Just make sure to check and calibrate all of the functions when you get it. All in all I like the way it looks and works. No regrets here. Lacking one star because Casio could have done a better job of calibrating the watch at the factory.

product_title: Phosphor Men's MD006G Appear Collection Fashion Crystal Mechanical Digital Watch
review_body:
I saw this in a store and bought it. It is a very interesting watch. (I rotate about 25) Essentially it is a low tech watch concept in that it tells hour and minutes. Period. There is no question what it says and anyone who happens to see it is intrigued.

About a month after buying it, I pulled it out to wear and none of the numbers was complete. Dead battery? Probably. I have the tools and opened it. It takes a huge battery - 3032. Larger than a quarter.

In order to find this out I had to open and unscrew the battery cover. Now I had a little bitty spring that I was not sure where to replace it. I took it to a local jeweler who replaces all my snap back watch batteries. He did not have nor could he get from his suppliers the 3032 battery. They ARE available from Amazon.

With hat in hand, I went back to the store that sold it to me. They knew about the little bitty spring and had the batteries.

It works fine and I am very happy with it until the battery gives out. The seller also gave me a photo of where to put the spring if I find the courage to try it myself, and he gave me an extra battery.

Bottom line: It is fun, accurate watch. But you better be a watch mechanic or know one to replace the battery.

Also, while others ask you to specify the length of the stem, this product provides the maximum stem dimension, which is likely to fit any clock. The pictorial instructions were easy to follow. Most importantly, the movement keeps accurate time - after three weeks of use, it is accurate within a minute. Highly recommend this product for conventional clocks (i.e. not the ones with dials exceeding 6" or so, as measured from the center to the tip).I don't see how you can go wrong with this product.
