product_title: Invicta Men's 8928OB Pro Diver Gold Stainless Steel Two-Tone Automatic Watch
review_headline: beautiful watch. updated after one years use.
review_body:
Having only owned this watch for two weeks I will stick to first impressions. Too soon to rate durability and function over time.

First, you should note, this is a sub $100 automatic watch. Try to find any automatic watch for less than $100. It's slim pickings. Some of the reviews I've read compare this $89 watch to $1000 and up.

I've paid as much for a fossil quartz analog, quartz movement is much cheaper and far less costly to manufacturer. It wasn't anywhere near as good looking.

This watch is stunning. The face is a deep blue/purple. I liken the color to ball point pen ink. The attention to detail, which is a large contributor for high cost watches, is actually really good for the price. The gold logo, hands, crystal bevel, crown and movement are very nicely detailed.

The band is certainly passable but it is not the greatest. However it is absolutely on par, if not better than steel bands found on similarly priced watches. The gold plating is beautiful, even if I know it is very very thin.

The movement is 24 jewel miyota (according to my research) and it's a tired and true durable movement. In the two weeks I've been wearing it I have only had to make minor adjustments, a minute or so, to keep it on atomic clock time. That's pretty good in my book. The key is to keep the watch properly wound. I want it all the time except at work so I manually wind it a bit and it's kept good time. I will amend this review if that changes.

I'm actually surprised invicta can produce this watch at such an affordable price. It mimics the classic good looks of a Rolex submariner yet with invicta branding, it makes no attempt at being a knock off.

I am very impressed with this watch so far, it exceeded my expectations. I feel comfortable recommending to friends and family.

Update: This watch has been flawless! I wear it daily, only removing for work. I sleep, shower and everything in between wearing this watch. It requires a manual wind about once a week or it starts to lose time. Otherwise it's been basically as accurate as a quartz. This watch hasn't been pampered, it's been bumped, dropped, scraped and banged. Other than tiny superficial scratches on the band it is still flawless. The crystal is completely free of defects. I am astounded at what a great watch this has been and it still looks incredible. Can't recommend any higher, this by far has been the best watch I've ever owned.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNZH57 Seiko 5 Automatic Black Dial Stainless Steel Watch
review_body:
I have owned my watch for almost a year and i feel like i needed to write a review. Im not gonna mention movement or crazy tech details because this is if you want to buy it or not.

First off my girlfriend bought me this watch and honestly its one of my favorite watches i own. I have about a 55-60mm wrist size and at first i thought it was too small but its fits just fine on my wrist and the thickness of the case helps. The wieght of the watch is phenomenal. The weight gives it a more \\"expensive\\" feel. Not too heavy but not light either.

The looks are impecable. I get complements everytime i wear it. It looks great. The bezel has a beautiful clear enamel fill that gives it that extra dimention. The crystal is also beautiful. Its not a saphire crystal but a mineral but even so it does not have a scratch on it and mind you i wear this watch almost daily. The dial has a nice black enamel sheen that makes the watch stand out and the applied index only enhance the look.

Now the durability...GREAT! I beat on it an it has alot of scratches on the bracelet but thats because i work in an office and my arms are flying across the table surface daily. Other than that the bezel and crystal are in perfect condition.

Now with the bad...the links are folded meaning they are NOT solid links which you would find on most expensive watches (a bit dissapointing) but seiko did a great job hiding the seams. Another thing is the squeak...yes it squeaks! At first it was annoying but it grew on me. Most watches with hollow end links will squeek.

As others have said this watch does not hold power for very long but ive actually had my watch lasting for 2 days which is fine for me.

PROs:
Looks great
Feels great
Durable
Good price for an AUTOMATIC

CONs:
Bracelet hollow
Bracelet squeeks (not that bad)

Conclusion:
For the price it is a great watch and when i first got it my girlfriend paid $200+ on amazon. I am planning on buying an all gold Version

Comfort: A
Price: B
Movement: C+
Bracelet: C
Look: B+

Overall: B+

Would i recommend? YES!!

review_headline: A little lighter-colored than the photo, but still a monster strap
review_body:
This is my fourth strap and it fits perfectly with my Orient Mako XL and my fat wrist. My first military-themed strap, it is brighter than how Amazon presents the photo, but nevertheless I am undoubtedly impressed by the overall build quality of this strap.

With five rings and all stitches obviously done with the utmost care, I felt like I was looking at a Louis Vuitton hand bag. All three individual rings rotate very tightly in their places, while the last two which are grouped together have more slack but in my opinion, not too much.

The strap thickness is its most prominent feature once you get a hold of it. If you look closely at the edges, there are a few hair-thin loose threads but at most only five and do not affect the overall strap. I even noticed that one of the locking holes still had the filler inside it, giving me the impression of a "freshly-made" strap.

Over time, this will definitely get softer but I am confident that it will last a very long time and give me years of watch-wearing pleasure.

product_title: Casio Men's W756D-7AV Digital Sport Watch
review_headline: Nice looking watch, but a few annoying features
review_body:
This is a great looking watch if you prefer to have a digital face. However, after wearing it for a few months now, I've come to have a few complaints that I can live with.

One is the odd little "Countdown Timer" bar in the middle of the face. It's raised up in such a way that it cuts off the bottom of the numbers when you look at the time. I have to twist my arm a little farther towards myself than feels normal to get a good reading.

Second complain is the light...it's a bit dim and it doesn't have the option to stay on longer if you hold it. You only get the 1.5 seconds of light after you press it and it automatically goes off. My previous watch would stay on if I needed to switch through functions and it's frustrating not to be able to on this one.

Third, the Start/Stop button for the timer is flush with the rest of the face, so it's difficult to press.

Lastly is 2 issues with the face...the glass is curved outward instead of sunk down and/or flat, resulting in it easily scratching. Also, the main face/body of the watch is plastic, painted to look silver, so it scratches easily to reveal the black plastic underneath.

Overall, I would not buy this watch again.

product_title: Tirio Magic Roman Half Hunter Black Steel Hollow Skeleton Hand Wind Mechanical Pocket Watch Long Chain
review_headline: Beautiful item at a great price
review_body:
I am using this as a desk clock. I like the contrast of the white hands against the dark face. This comes from overseas, so it takes a bit longer for delivery, but delivery is faster that the scheduled date. It's fun watching the mechanism.

Unlike typical wind up watches, you can't let the stem return back while winding otherwise the mechanism doesn't wind the spring much and it takes too many windings to get the spring tight. Until I used this method, the watch would need 3 windings per day or it would run out & stop if I forgot to rewind it. I'm not sure if it needs to be broken in to keep good time & condition the spring, but it seems to gain about a minute per day. I couldn't tell how well it kept time when it it kept running out.

This is a great accessory for a coat or if you wear gloves and can't easily see your wrist, but I wouldn't depend on it for my only timepiece. At least you don't need to replace batteries if you use it only occasionally.

Anyhow expect to see a watch like this on the wrist of a Hyundai/Kia salesman near you!!

On the plus side, the entire face back is the solar panel. I left the watch in my cars glove box for about a week. when i pulled it out, the battery was still strong. i guess the watch conserves battery when its in complete dark. Neat feature for a $30 accessory

product_title: Citizen Men's JY0040-59L Blue Angels Skyhawk A-T Stainless Steel Eco-Drive Watch
review_body:
******************************************************************************************************************
Update December 2013: I have replaced both bezels at a local watchmaker, and send it off to Citizen Holland to replace the mineral crystal for Sapphire crystal. simply Wow! I really love the Stainless steel version and the weight it has (and when the metals are watch bracelets sizes, there is hardly any difference in strength between SS and Ti.). I really love this watch and can't stop looking at it...incredible since my swiss automatics are on the watch winder because I'm only wearing the Blue Angels! Sapphire crystal for me is essential, and even tho it cost me some money to get the sapphire upgrade (100)...I'm really happy I did!)
******************************************************************************************************************

There is so much to say about this watch that it is hard to start so I'll just take off..

It was pretty hard to find for a reasonable price in Holland, but finally I found a private seller that bought it second hand.
No worries since he was a pilot himself and had bought it from a pilot, I assumed the timepiece would be set right and work properly.
And so it does.. without reading the book and with only the knowledge that the dial on the bottom of the watch is the \\"main menu\\".
Pulling out the crown 1 or 2 times gives options, but I quite quickly got the hang of it and already it feels very simple to handle.
Actually it doesn't need much handling because it automatically sets itself to the nearest atomic clock signal.
Surprisingly this watch still looks great after several years of use and more than 2 owners. The glass (mineral) has a light scratch and I'm probably sending it to citizen to get sapphire replacement. I will ask them to change both bezels (if possible) because since they are printed they are beginning to fade.
Citizen seems to me like one of the most reliable watchmakers. I have owned about 3 (2 very old boot sales models), and they are the only ones that always start..maybe that's why Toyota also is Japanese.
I also own an Omega vintage automatic geneve tv screen watch but that needs service every 3 to 4 years and that's not cheap.

In the end I started looking for a new watch a few weeks ago and spend hours and hours online browsing around all the trustworthy watchmakers, when suddenly I decided to switch from swiss to Japanese for my next watch and put accuracy above mechanical complications. I had my eye on an orange G-shock Casio which was already rare and doing 150 dollars above retail price. After comparing it to this watch however, I couldn't be wrong going for a Blue Angels.

Be careful which one you buy tho, I nearly bought an almost identical looking one for 100 dollars less but that didn't have the atomic clock or the led back light. So keep the right series number in your pocket when shopping for a Blue Angels watch.

The most important thing in a watch for me are:

0: Waterproof - Check! (swimming)
1: Accuracy - Check! (Atomic Clock)
2: Primary Dial Clock - Check!
3: Chronograph - Check! (1/100sec.)
4: Night visibility - Check! (fluorescent and backlight)
5: Easy time setting - Check! (sets itself)
6: Great Looker - Check!
7: Gadgets - Check! (Bezels and digital stuff)
8: Big & Heavy but not pompous - Check! (Functional)
9: Something that can show a diamond Rolex owner that he needs to set his watch - ;-)
10:Never replace a battery - Check! (Light powered)
11:Day/Month/Date display - Check! (digital)
12:World cities - Check! (No AMS?)

There is probably much more I forgot but this is a buy I can take anywhere, anytime and rely on it.

Only downside was mineral crystal and wear on bezels, but for the price I bought it I can't complain since seemingly 2 pilots wore and used the functions on this watch daily before I got it.

Call me silly but knowing this, this particular watch makes it have even more soul for me since it has served in the air, and passed the tests these former owners threw at it.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNK809 Seiko 5 Automatic Stainless Steel Watch with Black Canvas Strap
review_headline: Excellent Value in a Very Nice Watch
review_body:
To begin with, this is a very attractive watch, especially for wearers with smaller wrists (for reference, I wear even this band on the second-to-smallest notch). If you are seeking a functional aesthetic and prefer a smaller watch, this one is absolutely worthy of consideration. The movement works more than adequately, I find I have to adjust the time to remove about five minutes per month, which I do on the first of the month, when I adjust the date. The recessed, off-angle adjustment crown does a nice job of not bashing one's wrists, even when you wear the watch working. The clear back that reveals the clockwork never fails to impress children, not to mention adults who enjoy observing the mechanical workings of things. The self-wind is effective, I wear it most every day and have never had it stop on me.

This watch costs little more than all-plastic \\"sport\\" watches, so if you are a gentleman on a limited budget who has no interest in dressing like a 10-year-old boy, but is not interested in dressing like a want-to-be country club member either, this timepiece offers is a fine choice.

After reading reviews here, I was a little wary of how durable this watch would prove when exposed to vibration and moisture. Mine has taken who-knows-how-many hours of running an orbital sander and quite a few dunks in water. It's gone shooting skeet, been cycling on gravel roads, experienced plenty of wood splitting, even a little firefighting--- in sort, I wear it everywhere, and it still goes. For the price, I could not be more pleased, were it to fail tomorrow I'd likely buy another-- or certainly, at least, another Seiko. Highly recommended.

review_headline: Swiss Parts, Not 'Swiss Quartz' in Any Normal Sense
review_body:
The description on Amazon.com said 'Swiss quartz': in watchmaking 'Swiss Quartz' is a legally defined expression under Swiss law, I believe. The watch itself, to be fair, did not say 'Swiss Quartz' but mentioned 'Swiss parts' in the movement.

I also found the watch very hard to read: the colors and fonts used were almost designed to make the watch look pretty but hard to read.

I returned the watch and was promptly refunded as promised by Amazon. If the description on Amazon.com had said 'Swiss parts' rather than 'Swiss quartz', I wouldn't have ordered it.

Moral: check the dial in the Amazon.com photo. If it says on the dial 'Swiss Quartz', then that's what it means.

Would this Invicta have worked OK? Was it really a watch with Swiss-made movement parts assembled elsewhere? I don't know.

No, it doesn't have day/date, doesn't glow in the dark, doesn't have buit-in GPS, and won't help you start a campfire. But it keeps excellent time, looks great, and it is very comfortable. I have three watches with sapphire crystals, one about twenty years old, and none show the slightest wear. I expect the same from this watch. The band seems to be very well made. The machining on the clasp is downright beautiful; it is a shame no one else ever sees it. It is the first watch I have had with the double \\"butterfly\\" clasp, and it is easier to use than I thought it would be. Being so thin makes it the most comfortable watch that I own.

If you want a watch with style, this is it. To me, and expensive name only says you are good at spending money. This one shows taste. I am very pleased with my purchase.

product_title: Hadley-Roma Men's Genuine Silicone Diver Sport Watch Strap
review_headline: didn't hold up to first use!
review_body:
I purchased this strap 8 months ago, but last night was the first time I've used it. It's a quality looking strap, with a pleasingly soft texture, dark, charcoal color, and bright yellow stitching, length 120mm x 75mm.

So, after going for a swim, the watch was missing from my wrist! Luckily, I was able to retrieve it from the bottom of the pool with only cosmetic damage...took a licking...(you can finish the rest!). the strap had torn along the spring bar. It could be that this band was only one of few defective ones, because I have another just like it with Orange stitching that has held up fine for 8 months. Also, I consider Hadley Roma to be of the best quality when you compare it to the other inexpensive strap-makers.

review_body:
I really enjoy this watch. The style is exactly what I wanted; a red tipped sweeping second hand, ticks across the outer face, an arrow at noon, hours within the minutes, luminous hands and a matte finish on the bezel. The crown is tucked away and does not dig into the wrist of those of us who wear it near the hand, which is a major plus in my book.

The con to this watch is the strap, but it is easily replaceable (see my review of the JP Leatherworks strap I just put on it). A new strap really sets this watch apart. The original has a thick, coarse nylon texture and does begin to fray at the edges shortly after some use. The links to hold the strap are also a bit bulky compared to the profile of the watch itself and does not fit it properly as a day-to-day user. A good NATO style strap or thin leather strap does this thing wonders.

The only other con I have is that mine seems to run about 30 seconds fast per day. At this pricepoint I really can't complain too much, but I was hoping to receive a model that was closer to the 10-15 second range I've been reading about. An adjustment every few days doesn't bother me too much in the end. I'd highly recommend this watch (or it's other colored brothers).

review_body:
I use this watch for sports, working out, and casual wear. Here are some thoughts after using it moderately (3-4 times a week) for about a month.

-Light and slim; unobtrusive and adds to just about any outfit
-The rubber band and its light weight make it comfortable and enjoyable to wear
-The price allows me to wear this just about anywhere and not have to worry about dinging it
-Controls are easy to set up
-Keeps time accurately; ironic that I feel like this is a pro, but I've owned other cheap watches that would be off by a bit after a week

Cons:
-Cheap band: The band is already showing signs of wear; mainly watermarks that will not come out (I've worn it in slight drizzle weather).

product_title: Timex Digital Expedition Watch
review_headline: Apple design sense seems to have rubbed off on this Timex watch
review_body:
Why do designers of digital watches insist on clunky implementations, such as constantly trying to put an inherently RECTANGULAR readout on a ROUND dial? It's illogical, yet that's how an awful lot of men's watches are made.

So in my search for a good-looking, simple (and affordable) digital watch, I automatically had to discard about 80% of what's available out there. Nor was Timex my first choice of brands. To people my age (mid-50s), Timex is like Oldsmobile -- it's your dad's brand.

But this watch just made sense for me. I have a thin wrist, so while it's big (the current style in men's watches), it's not too big. The readout is easy to see in daylight, and in dim light indoors and at night the Indiglo feature is nice and clear. Despite the wide band, it still fits my wrist. It has a rectangular (almost square) form-follows-function design. And it's straightforward -- free of the geegaws, doodads and other whiz-bang miniature dials-within-dials that some watch manufacturers seem so fond of.

I'm happy with it. The only complaint I have is that this design looks so nice, I would have liked to have seen it in a metal case with a metal band.

review_headline: Solid watch band, a little darker than pictured
review_body:
I just got this watch band, but so far it looks like a really high-quality band for the price. The buckle seems solid and the leather also seems like it will be durable.

Some recent reviewers have mentioned that the band they received was very different from the one pictured. That has not been my experience. One thing I wonder about is how well this band would work for someone with a thicker wrist than mine. I think I have a relatively average wrist size and the band works fine for me. However, the tail of the band has a bit less slack than others I have tried, and I think someone with a wrist that was more than about an inch bigger around than mine might find the tail of the band will be too short to run through either of the loops that hold the tail end of the band in place.

product_title: Citizen Men's  BJ7000-52E Nighthawk Stainless Steel Eco-Drive Watch
review_body: I really liked the dial and the fact that the slide rule is enclosed within the crystal. I own other citizen watches in the Navihawk and skyhawk AT range and the slide rules either get damaged or the paint wears off. However, in this case that will not be an issue. This is my second watch with the slide rule inside the crystal and am not looking back. The watch is an eco-drive (solar powered) and takes care of the need of changing batteries every couple of years. The dial has the standard slide rule markings as well a unique way of displaying dual time. It is not the way a traditional GMT watch with a 4th hand pointing to the hour; on the other hand (get it) the watch has 2 hands, one colored white and the other red corresponding to the 1-12 and 13-24 sets of hours, respectively, and move in conjunction with the main hour and minute hands to provide the give second time. The dual time is only displayed on the left half of the face in a concentric half crescent, which makes it quite unique. The date is displayed on the 3 o'clock marker and easy to read. The bracelet is sturdy and seems to be made of good quality material, and so do the clasp and locking mechanism. All the time related adjustments are performed by the textured and branded crown located at the 3 o'clock position and slide rule is operated by a similar crown at the 8 o'clock position. The watch glows a brilliant light blue, instead of the traditional green lume, which is a nice change of pace. Overall the watch is well made and a utilitarian finish on the body and bracelet; it wears well and the bracelet is quite generous in size and fits large wrists. I like it.

product_title: Tissot Men's T0264201105100 Sea Touch Quartz Chronograph Touch Screen Black Dial Watch
review_body:
I had my eye on this watch for over a year, really wanted it, and received it as a gift from my sons who are Amazon Prime members and bought it from Amazon. We immediately went on a scuba diving holiday. I purchased the stainless band, white face, metric dial, Tissot Sea Touch, but the comments below apply to any of the Sea Touch range.

1) as received, the watch already displayed low battery signal. Others have complained about this and the cost ($100+) to have it done by Tissot service center which is mandatory
2) Watch box contained lots of documentation about Tissot history, did not include an operating manual.
3) I downloaded the operating manual. Interesting that here they fill it with legalese \\"This is not a divers watch\\". Can you believe it.
4) First dive I made, switched it to dive mode. The hands convert to depth guage indicator and the digital watch starts - NOT. when I submerged, just got an ERR reading, which means no time or depth function! So I went back to the operating manual (on line) to make sure I had used it properly and tried again. Same result. Less than totally worthless, this is dangerous. Luckily, I had brought my old, cheap, trusty Timex Expedition watch with me. Not a dive watch, but good enough. Had it for 3 years, still not replaced the battery. Timex Men's T45581 Expedition E-Instruments Tide Temperature and Compass Watch
5) I wrote directly to Tissot customer service on line to seek advice. It has been several months, No reply of any kind.
6) My sons returned the watch. Amazon refunded the money, great service from Amazon.

Don't buy this product. Tissot does not deserve your business.

review_body:
I've had the watch for a few days, so I can't comment regarding durability. However, I had a Casio beater watch (also a 10-year battery, same price range) which proved trusty for almost 8 years.

Feature wise, this watch has plenty of nifty ones:

- Worldtime,including some of the \\"irregular\\" time zones that most World Time watches lack, i.e., Newfoundland time (UTC-3.5 h), Afghanistan - Kabul (UTC+4.5 h), India (UTC+5.5h), Nepal - Katmandu (UTC+5.75h), Burma - Rangoon (UTC+6.5h), Central Australia (UTC+9.5 h). The one missing is Venezuela's time zone (UTC-4.5h). As you scroll through the time zones, the three letter code of the city or airport changes, along with the time zone in the small Mercator map.

- You can set up to four time zones for easy time check, at the touch of a button (or continuously on Auto Display mode), from the main screen. Times can be set with or without daylight saving time (DST).

- Light is orange in colour, not too bright but plenty to see most details of the watch dial. It can be set for 1.5 or 3 seconds in duration.

- Five alarms setting (useful to wake up deep sleepers, if you set them at 1-2 min intervals) plus hourly chime. The volume is not too high.

- Stopwatch and countdown timer, programmable from 23:59:59 to one second (not sure who would need 1 sec timer, but there you go).

- A pretty gimmicky analogue type dial on the top right corner. It shows hour, minute and second.

- One cool thing that a lot of Casio watches lack: the characteristic beep when you press any button can be turned off; a good thing for keeping social etiquette.

The band is simple to adjust, the arrows point to the pins that need to be depressed in order to slide the links out. There's nothing fancy about it, but I find it comfortable to wear, and it does not pull any hairs from my wrist.

Bottom line: A bargain watch with plenty of good features, especially if you travel quite a lot. You can't go wrong with this Casio. Master approved.ly if you travel quite a lot. You can't go wrong with this Casio. Master approved.

product_title: Seiko Men's Silvertone Black Dial Solar Calendar Watch
review_body:
Having owned this watch for a while, I feel it would be a terrible injustice not to update my review. Mine has been through its paces and here are the results.

Bracelet: my one knock on this piece, so I'm going to get that out of the way. Do not wear this watch "loose"-- unless you want your end links to start flapping about. Seiko could have put solid end links on, even at this price point, I'm sure.

Crystal: surprisingly tough. This watch has lasted me through 3 jobs-- one in a retail store, one warehouse, and one as a desk diver. Two tiny little scratches, and barely noticable at that.

Movement: I got bored one night and decided to open it and get a look at the power plant. I'm expecting: some heat-staked, lozenge type job, modified for a solar cell from some bargain bin in China. I get: fully servicible, 2 jewels, made in Japan. Big thumbs up here for quality.

Capacitor: not what I expected. It's been drained completely at least 3 times in its life from being left in the dark too long-- and has somehow managed to come out still holding a charge.

Clasp: pretty standard, boring actually. The typical stamped clasp, side button setup expected for most Seikos under $300. Nothing to write home about, but doesn't dig into your wrist.

Water resistance: while mine has been submersed in sink water, I refuse to take it swimming with me, as I don't trust it. It's probably going to be fine to keep on your hands while you wash them, however.

Other features: I really dig the blue "Sat" indicator, it's something not all watches have. Red "Sun" seems to be pretty standard these days.

Other things to note, are that this watch is great for smaller wrists-- think 7" and below. 7 1/2", maybe, but would be pushing it a bit. Also, this is not the type of watch to get when you are fishing for compliments. It isn't flashy or blingy. This watch will serve you well otherwise.

Then I discovered I could wear (own) more than one watch at a time and it opened up a whole new area of interest for me.  So now, this watch is one that I wear consistently along with 4-5 others depending upon the occasion, activity or how I feel.  I get a kick out of the Orange face, most of my other watches would be more conservative in appearance, so for me, this one has a lot of character. For the watch collector - enthusiast that doesn't care to spend a small fortune on a single timepiece, this watch will not not disappoint.

product_title: U.S. Polo Assn. Classic Men's US5211 Black Analog Watch
review_body:
Alright, the first thing that needs to be said is that this is a $20 watch. That should be obvious, but some of the reviewers don't seem to know that.

The watch arrived very quickly in a nice leather(ish) blue box. The face is huge. It has a 2-inch diameter. The big knob on the right side adds to it, giving it a total width of almost 2 1/2 inches. The band is very thick, making it slightly hard to adjust. But once you've worn it a few times, the band \\"remembers\\" where it's supposed to go, and it goes on fairly easily.

The two knobs on the left side do absolutely nothing. The top knob on the right side does nothing. I haven't figured out what the purpose of the giant knob is. The one on the bottom right is what you use to adjust the time.

Alright, on to the positives. I wanted a big black watch that I could wear everyday. I have an Invicta Grand Diver, but it is a metallic watch with a big yellow face. I wanted something a little less \\"flashy\\" to wear to class and just to wear around town. I also wanted something that I could fit somewhat tightly to my wrist, so it doesn't move around while I'm typing (I'm a programmer). I really, really love this watch.

Some people have had problems with the band snapping. I haven't had any issues with it. It actually feels pretty sturdy to me. The two little button-type things on the band next to the place where the band attaches to the body are a little loose. It doesn't bother me, and they don't really serve any purpose. If they were taken off, the watch would still stay together. I just thought I'd mention it, in case you are after craftsmanship.

So to summarize, this is a great watch for only $20. It keeps the time, it was inexpensive, and it looks amazing (...like, really amazing.). My advice is to make the leap and buy it. I would definitely buy it again. But if you do, don't compare it to a $100 watch. Compare it to the $15-$20 watches at Walmart. It blows them away.

UPDATE:
Okay, so I may have overestimated the quality of the watch band. The part of the leather that wraps around the buckle snapped when I was trying to take the watch off. Admittedly, I may have been a little rough with it, but upon further inspection, that section of the leather is incredibly thin. Fortunately, I happened to have some Gorilla tape lying around. I just put a little strip through the buckle, and it seems to be strong enough now. Also, that section is covered up by the rest of the band when it is worn, so no one can tell the difference.

I lowered my rating, but I still think it's worth 4 stars. I still really like the looks of it, and I still recommend buying it. Just be a little careful with it until you get more familiar with its design and strength.

product_title: Orient Men's CEV0M001W 21 Jewel Automatic with Full Day and Date Watch
review_body:
I first came by the orient brand by reading watchuseek and other watch forums; they have quite a following of loyal customers. Orient makes their own movements and is now owned by seiko. I am not a watch snob and happen to think seiko, citizens and orient all are great brands. I own a variety of Swiss made quartz and automatic watches including watch snob brands, so I can now personally say after purchasing this one that orient makes a quality product with great fit and finish in its price point. I also have to say, for this price, this is an unbelievable value. You would pay substantially more with a better known brand because of its substantially higher marketing costs. With orient, you are not paying for the marketing, just the craftsmanship. I highly recommend this watch and other orient watches. By the way, I am wearing this watch as I write this review. It sits on my wrist while other watch snob brands sit in my drawer. The description provided; however, is a tad inaccurate. The watch is on the larger side at about 42 mm. One of he pictures show the watch next to measurement markers. That picture is completely inaccurate. I have not measured the thickness, but I would guess it falls around 10-11 mm. It easily fits under dress shirt and has no issue with getting tangled in the cuff. Overall, it is a classy looking dress watch that can be worn casually at a bargain price. What's not to love?

product_title: Invicta Men's 9211 Speedway Collection Stainless Steel Chronograph Watch with Link Bracelet
review_headline: Class, for a fraction of the price
review_body:
Every now and again a watch from Invicta comes out and I cannot simply fathom the low prices they command with the looks they have.
I realise that the Invicta $MSRP price is really no indication on what the watch actually sells for. I've found most of the models sell for 20-30% of the original $MSRP.

This watch may not have Swiss movements but it makes up for it with a beautiful crown, dial and sub-dials. The bezel is beautiful, in fact I cannot fault the watch in any way cosmetically and aesthetically.

This watch is almost a Rolex Daytona Replica and I have been stopped and asked if it was a Daytona, although I would absolutely love a Rolex I can't afford the $20,000 that a Daytona commands.

Invicta have thus produced a very pleasing time piece, it looks the part and the movement isn't terrible, for the price I would challenge you to find a better watch, it would be difficult, especially in this price range.

Invicta has done the \\"Speedway\\" range justice and the watch itself is very handsome.

product_title: Casio Men's Sport Analog Dive Watch
review_headline: Nice watch, but the luminous hands and numerals are a disappointment.
review_body:
I looked at dozens of watches before picking this one. I wanted something analog and easy to set, but did not want one with added digital features that, if I bumped a button, would require me to dig out a manual to figure out how to get things "back". One of the analog + digital watches I really liked had in its instructions "push button B six times to....". No thanks. No way I would ever remember all that sequencing for all 4 buttons.

I suppose I am spoiled by my old Timex with Indiglo. And that is what I just ordered again to replace this Casio watch, which I'll keep as a spare, since it was only $17. I put this Casio under very bright direct LED flashlight, (30 bright white LEDs) about 6 inches from the dial, for half an hour, but within 15 minutes after removing it from the light, the luminous items on the watch face were already so dim I could not see the watch in a pitch black room. I had hoped for better performance from a watch with a luminous face.

The band is indeed very long. I have large wrists and have often had to buy extra long watch bands. But this one fit me very well on the 4th hole. I like the "zig zag" design of the band adjacent to the watch, which provides a little give in sizing. It was easy to set, although a bit confusing at first. They do not explain how to deal with AM/PM at all in the provided instructions. So I turned the hands forward until I found midnight and watched the day and date change. From there I could figure it out. The weekday is bilingual, alternating languages for each day, and what it does is actually change TWO positions, so it stays on the language you choose when you set it.

product_title: Seiko Bedside Talking Alarm Clock Silver-Tone Metallic Case
review_headline: Still love this loud and obnoxious clock!!  Great for Handicapped or Seniors.
review_body:
Our family is very, very, very difficult to wake up.
About 10 years ago, I bought everyone in my immediate family, this clock.

My 87 year old Mom, was recently having difficulty seeing the digital clock across the room, and was getting up at midnight, thinking it was noon.

With this clock, all she has to do is reach over to the night stand, tap the bar at the top of the clock with her little arthritic hands, and it will tell her the time.... with A.M. or P.M.
She can touch this part of the clock with any part of her hand... heel, finger, back of hand. This makes it easy for her.

This clock is durable.
She has dropped it from the nightstand several times already and it doesn't break.

The one I have at home....I can't remember ever having to change the battery and it still works.
My husband changed his battery about a year ago.

The small digital area of this clock does NOT light up at night.
There is no need for it to light up.
You just tap the top button, it will tell you the time.

The volume on the clock can be set LOW or HIGH.
You can have just the LADY's voice wake you up or the LADY and the Rooster which is the obnoxious, loud, and you WILL get out of bed NOW, sounds.

Why just the 4 stars, you ask?

The clocks purchased years ago had a clear, crisp voice when the lady spoke to wake you up.
This clock's voice is somewhat garbled and takes a bit to understand her \\"accent\\".
Mom could not understand her for about 4 days and I was going to return it. After 4 days, Mom said she was used to it and could understand her now.

product_title: Seiko 5 Men's SNKL23 Stainless Steel Automatic Casual Watch
review_headline: Attractive Watch & Good Value for Price
review_body:
I have a narrow wrist & had difficulty finding a smaller bracelet style watch. Based upon listed dimensions (case and bracelet width) this one seemed promising. However, actual watch appeared to be larger than as listed and on the heavy side. (Battery watches might be a better bet for less weight than automatics or solar powered ones.) Notwithstanding, decided to give it a try. Once on the wrist weight is not too noticeable and size not overwhelming.
There are other comments available on the issue of the bracelet adjustment (including some You Tube do it yourself instructions). Decided to save some time and aggravation by taking it to a watch store. Any place that installs watch batteries should be able to do this and it will cost you an extra $8 - $10. Also, removal of links may not result in a "fine tune" adjustment. Best I was able to do left bracelet slightly tight on my wrist but if I added back a link(s) it probably would have been too loose. This may not be an issue for most.
After three weeks, automatic mechanism seems to work fine. I take the watch off at night. Has lost about 1 minute in this time period. The crown is very difficult to pull out with your fingers. When depressed, it is almost flush with the case. Once out, adjustment of time & date is easy. Day & date is a nice feature and has been accurate.
This watch is really good looking and easy to read. Hope it continues to keep reasonably accurate time.

product_title: Casio Women's LDF50-1CF Pop Tone Black Digital Watch
review_headline: Exactly what I hoped for and more
review_body:
I spent, what seemed like, forever searching for a watch that would suit me best while travelling. Typically I've become one of those "use my cell phone for my watch" types. But I'm now travelling between two very drastic time zones and that is no longer feasible due to reliability of the time change on my phone keeping up with the shift. Anyhoo, that bit is neither here nor there.
First, I'm a klutz. Any watch on me is going to get banged around and bumped against things. I also have two young boys. So it gets stolen and used for all manner of shenanigans they get up to. It's taking it's lumps and not coming up scuffed or damaged, which is a miracle so far. The wrist band fits around my wrist comfortably (and, even though I'm a woman, I don't have a petite wrist. I typically purchase men's watches for that reason.) and it is very sturdy. With little discomfort or abrasiveness, I might add. I continue to have great hopes for the watches overall durability.
The screen is bigger than most digital watches but not obtrusive or overly in the way.
Now, granted, if you're looking for a feminine or fancy watch, this isn't it. It's exactly as it looks, at least to my eyes.
The watch part itself isn't huge, but it is a little bigger than most. The buttons are easy to use if you're like me and have what my mother would call "farmers's hands." (i.e. tiny buttons are the bane of existence) Also, there are no sharp edges along the watch, even around the metal edges. So no snagging it on something. Even the fine hairs along the back of my arm don't become snagged. (which stings when it happens due to watches, though a little, but still)
The luminescent feature is perfect, with the ability to adjust how long it lasts and the (like in the picture) orange light button on the bottom right is easy to find.
I also require an alarm on a watch, which was another reason to pick this. It didn't fail me. I can set my alarm and it tailors itself to the primary time you set (I'll get to that in a second. Basically, if I'm paying attention to, say, New Zealand time and need my alarm to go off by a certain time Central Standard, if my main time is CST...it will go off at THAT time; whatever I set), which is brilliant.
Date is easy to set as well with a calendar that adjusts for off numbered months like leap years, etc. It also shows up on the main time mode.
Now, I did need to use the manual to set time(s) (which was super easy to use by the way and came in multiple languages). The reason I needed it was mostly just to make sure I was doing it right. It's rather intuitive to figure out if you pay attention. But, I don't know about anyone else, I'm prone to 'brainfarts'. Hence, me and the manual became friends.
There are four display modes to chose from -not only convenient, and necessary for my needs, but appealed to the "oh shiny, lots of buttons and features" side of me- (see that "mode" button on the bottom left in the picture? That flips between the "modes." All of which are labeled in the top left corner of the display on the second, third, and fourth displays). First is the main time, second is the alarm, third is the stop watch, and fourth is the real beauty, in my opinion: dual time mode.
I set the main time first. Then the alarm I needed. Then clicked into the fourth display and set New Zealand Time (which I need for my travel). Any time can be set in this mode, by the way. Not just NZT. Basically, your choice.
What's a bonus, is that you can not only see that an alarm is set on the DT (or dual time mode) but you can see BOTH times you have set; your main time, and the second one, on the same screen.
I adore this. I absolutely do.
Oh, and it's water resistant too. Bonus! Because I don't know about anyone else, but though I may not be a water sports type, I'm always forgetting to take the watch off. Win!
I also purchased this watch throughthe seller "Mr Watch" and I have to say I'd purchase from that seller again and again. Easy to deal with. Arrived sooner than estimated. They even emailed to make sure everything had gone smoothly. I'd say that's great service. Most importantly: The watch was exactly as listed. Brand new and pristine.
I absolutely recommend this watch.
With this watch, everything is "Shiny." (Yes. Yes, I busted out a Firefly reference. The watch deserved it.)

I've had the watch since May 2012. I've continued to get compliments on it. I wear it both casually and dressed up, and it fits both environments. When needed I just wash it in the sink; it comes out shining. I've been very happy with it. The time, date, and clock hands are all easy to see and read. It's kept perfect time so far. When I received it I just took it to the local jeweler and he took links out with no problem. Not sure what he would have charged, maybe $20; I didn't have to pay anything because I waited about an hour (it was a busy night).

There are a couple of minor kinks in the armor. The magnifying glass over the date: it works great when looking directly down at the watch, but I find if I'm looking at the date at an angle the magnifying glass actually gets in the way. Minor infraction. Also, I've found the band has scratched a little easier than I expected. How did it get scratched? While wearing it and typing on my laptop, the band scratches back and forth over the laptop and has made minor scuffs to the band. It's not scratched when doing anything else. People I've talked to, and observed, with expensive timepieces have had similar problems. Again, not a major infraction.

I love the watch. Others love the watch. Get One!

product_title: Invicta Men's 3449 Corduba Collection Oversized Chronograph Watch
review_headline: Large, quality...prepare to make a statement
review_body:
I received this watch as a father's day gift and love it. I The watch reminded me of vintage stop-watches used in track and field and other sporting events, which immediately drew my attention to this piece.

I'm not the first to mention that this watch is very oversized, and makes a bold statement when you wear it. The watch feels well built, and industrial. The face of the watch is HUGE, with large hands, bold dark numbers and a beautifully textured manilla colored watch face behind the flame-fusion crystal face. The dates are easy to read, and the japanese chronograph is easy to read as well.

I've read a number of people that have complained that the chronograph doesn't return to zero on their watches, toting it as a defect, though many quartz-movement chronograph watches have the same issue, and the most watches, including Invicta are built in such a way to be able to reset to zero, as explained here:

http://www.keepthetime.com/blog/the-faqs/how-to-set-an-invicta-chronograph-back-to-zero/

The genuine calf leather strap on the watch is soft, yet sturdy. It's bold and stitched with white thread which compliments the face of the watch. I've only had the watch a few days, and the leather is still pretty stiff, which can make getting the watch band through both leather loops (one connected right at the base of the clasp) a bit tricky, but nothing too annoying. I assume this will loosen with time as the watch is worn.

The weight of the watch takes a little getting used to, but I haven't found it annoying at all. It's comfortable to type with, which can be annoying for myself as I work as a graphic designer/ web developer and spend much of my day at a computer.

Because the watch face sits so high off your wrist (approx a half inch), the buttons haven't bothered by hand. One of my concerns with the watch was that the chrono buttons/ knob would dig into my wrist or hand, but I haven't noticed this any morethan my other watches which sit close to my hand, thus allowing those watch buttons to touch skin sooner.

Love this piece, and glad to have it apart of my collection, apart of the 'big and bold' grouping!

product_title: Casio Men's CA53W-1 Calculator Watch
review_headline: Very Cool and Practical Retro Watch
review_body:
I bought a calculator watch once before from Timex. I was reasonably happy with it, except that it would beep with every button press, which there was no way to turn off, and that it was lacking in some of the other features of a digital watch which are common. This has all of the above. I do tips in my head, but it's great for figuring taxes and unit pricing, and you'd be surprised how much more calculating you find yourself doing when you have a calculator so close at hand. It's also great to have a stopwatch and calendar, too.

Because this watch has a full complement of buttons, it's much easier to operate than something like an F-91W, and it's much less prone to accidental resets of date and time. Features are also fewer button presses away, although the buttons are quite small and require a bit of dexterity.

It's also waterproof, which is what ended my Timex calculator watch.

The only thing missing is a backlight, which I rarely use. Were I to need that, I'd just got o my phone for the time.

product_title: Seiko Men's Silvertone Blue Dial Solar Watch
review_body:
I bought this watch as my first everyday watch that I wore for school, work, leisure - basically everything.

Right off the bat I was impressed with this watch - it was easy to set the time, and I really like the fact that it charges itself from sunlight. The design is very simple, making the time very easy to read. The day/date display is also easy to read, and a very useful feature to have.

I was lucky that the band fit me without having to adjust it, although it was slightlyyy on the loose side, but I got used to it. Something that I like about the expansion band as opposed to a clasp design is that you can take it on and off very easily and quickly, so if you prefer taking your watch off to wash your hands, bathe, exercise etc., you won't be fumbling with any clasps multiple times a day. The problem with the expansion band is that if it doesn't fit you, adjusting it is difficult. I didn't want to do it myself just in case I accidentally damaged it, so I left it the way it was (ever so slightly loose).

The hands and the hash-marks are all glow-in-the-dark, and they do so very brightly. Some other watches I've had do not glow brightly enough or long enough to read at night, but this one has always been very visible. After coming inside on a bright day, they glow ridiculously brightly and it is pretty awesome to look at.

Unfortunately, this watch's band broke after slightly less than year's worth of wearing it. I wore it every day for the first summer I got it, then in the fall I wore it about 30-40% of the time once I got a different watch. I was wearing it at the gym (probably not the best idea, but I'd never had a problem before), and I looked down and one of the connecting pieces in the band had broken. It was still holding together on one side, but it wouldn't hold for long so I just broke off the other piece. I don't remember hitting my wrist on anything, so I don't know why the band broke. I think it was just a random incident, so it *could* happen no matter where you are, if you're wearing the watch on a daily basis.
Eventually I took it to a jeweler to put the band back together. They took out too many links and now it's a bit tight, but all it will take is another adjustment and it should be fine.

Overall, the watch served me well for daily use, until the band broke. Not sure if that was a problem caused by the band's design or just a random incident. The style and quality of the watch are otherwise quite good, and I would definitely recommend this watch.om incident, so it *could* happen no matter where you are, if you're wearing the watch on a daily basis.

The countdown timer is the best part. Can't figure out why it's not standard on all watches. I wish they would make a more classy/refined looking watch with same features. I would be first to buy.

Only downside is that there is no backlight, which can be REALLY annoying. But the countdown timer is now such a necessary part of my day that I live without the backlight.

A must-have watch. Esp if you toted one of these in the 80s. Nostalgia that can't be beat.

review_headline: Great looking watch, worried about the finish though.
review_body:
I'm actually used to larger watches, but this one looks very nice even though it's a little smaller than I thought it would be. Had to remove 2 pieces from the band and now it fits perfectly. I am having a little trouble getting the date set - I can't seem to find the right spot to have the date change at midnight instead of noon - I've tried resetting it a couple of times (the date setting is a little touchy to find but it's there, just pull the knob out 1/2 way instead of all the way), and I've set the watch back 1/2 a day manually as well (though adjustment of the hands not the date) but neither as worked. Hopefully I'll get that part working soon enough.

I really like that it's an Eco-Drive, and that it's black. I wear my watch sun up to bed time and after only a couple of weeks, though, and I can see a couple spots on the band that are wearing through the black color already. If that continues, I'll have to lower my review. I do type a lot at work, but that piece is normally actually resting on a cloth-covered gel wrist pad. I may be forced to not wear this around the house, just to try to keep the finish from wearing off. I'll update this review once I've had it a bit longer to let you know about the color.

Update 9/10/13: The watch itself is great, holding up well - but as I feared the parts on the underside of the watch that will touch a table/desk/keyboard rest when my hand is palm down is fading more and more as time goes on. It's not TERRIBLY noticeable unless you're looking straight at it, but not only are the edges a little worn down to the silver underneath but there is also a chip in the middle of the band as well. Great watch, just wish their coating was more durable.

-D

review_body:
$125, is it worth it? Answer is: yes, but you'll have to fall in love with it to get past it's one major flaw. [winding it, no battery]

I saw an ad for TKO Orlogi in People magazine it was love at first sight: the mint color, the size, the amazing detail of the insides. I knew I had to have it and I was going to lose the battle of not spending the money. I was weary since there were no previous [useful] reviews of it, and the silicone band. I've had other watches with silicone bands that gather dirt and grime and get discolored in a month. I only got it today so not sure if that will happen. And wait, what's this manual mechanical movement? Oh, i'll need to constantly re-set the time and wind wind wind to keep it ticking. Worth the $$ saved on batteries? Ha. Maybe.

I knew it was going to be a lot of work but the beauty of it is WORTH EVERY PENNY. It's shiny, it's see-thru, it's GLAMOROUS. And hey, no scratches on this one...it comes with protective films duhh it's new.

Flaws:

-quite heavy, I have such thin wrists...
-stops randomly..
-always in fear of \\"over winding and damaging watch\\"

It's like having a very high maintenance toy breed dog; a lot of work but nice to look at.

I'm giving it 4 stars because I just wish there was a way to keep it constantly ticking. There is nothing wrong with it, it is as advertised and lovely and amazing but I just feel like that's a little....outdated.

product_title: Black Multi-Band 6 Atomic Triple Sensor Solar Pathfinder ProTrek Digital
review_headline: Pound For Pound, The Best Sports Watch In Its Category
review_body:
I've owned a few G-Shock watches over the years. This is my first Pathfinder. I've had it for about a year now. I share a lot of the sentiments of the 4-Star and 5-Star reviewers. I love the watch. I think I got my money's worth on it (retail $250, but I got it for about $160 + tax + shipping).

On a side note, I ran into a Marine that owned the same exact watch that I had, at a deployed location in Africa. He liked his watch a lot as well. Like me, at the time, he hadn't read the entire user's manual yet (he had just bought it) and wasn't utilizing it fully but what he did figure out, up to that point, were features and functionality very useful to him.

I researched several styles and brands, including Suunto. I was looking for something that was solar-powered and waterproof and had a compass, thermometer, more than one alarm, altimeter, and timer/stopwatch. The moon phase and tide features of the watches in the next higher tier watches interested me but I was unwilling to spend an additional $75-$100 to get those features. Atomic would be nice but I would want to be able to adjust the time manually (is that possible?) and really, a quick call to the US Naval Observatory (719-567-6742) and I've got atomic time again. I have noticed that this watch does not drift as much as my Casio G-Shock, maybe a few seconds a month.

Overall, the watch has everything I need and it's very easy to use. Aesthetically, it's a nice-looking watch. I don't like the 'flashy/goofy' watches that have strange colors. I tend to like the black, blue, dark green, grey, & white (neutral colors). The numbers & letters on the watch can be any color, though. Any criticisms that I have are minor and aren't a 'deal-killer' or anything.

PROs: Has all of the features I was looking for; Looks good; I like the ability to change units (Celsius vs. Fahrenheit, etc.) turn on/off sounds, set LCD light time, etc. is really nice; user-friendly functionality; when I compared this watch to other Casio watches or other brands, the other watches didn't have all of the functions that I 'had to have.' I also like the watchband. I don't want the metal linked one with the metal clasp; I prefer the leather, cloth (or both) style.

CONs (minor): The bezel ring should have a 'notch' or 'detent' with North (\\"N\\") at the top, a bit annoying because it drifts, now and then; I like to be able to rotate it but it needs something to keep it in place in the 'north up' position; alarm is a bit soft, though it always wakes me up; Accuracy is sometimes off; the fact that I have to take my watch off to take any reading is a CON; Sunset and sunrise are +/- 5 to 10 min off when compared to actual/internet; Ballpark it's fine, you'd have to get Consumer Reports to test the accuracy and compare it against the other watches. You can adjust (if you had to) the compass readings (I didn't), altimeter readings, and I think the baro one also.

Suggestion:
You really have to read the instruction manual to fully utilize the features of this watch. It'll take some time but it's worth it and it was written in a way that makes sense (it shouldn't be confusing to you). You'll be glad that you did.

product_title: Casio Men's Slim Solar Multi-Function Analog-Digital Watch
review_body:
Function and looks were the highest priorities for me, not price (though saving money is not a bad feeling). I was willing to pay more, but I could not find anything that I thought looked OK until I got over $200 for a Citizens watch. Since I wear the same watch all the time, it had to be appropriate for both work and leisure. And I wanted a solar watch, so I would not have to worry about the waterproof seal when I replaced a battery. The solar charging for this watch works well.

It is easy to make a check list of requirements and check them off for various watches (solar, waterproof, analog, good looking, countdown timer, alarm clock, etc). Using this method, this watch scores high. The only feature this watch seems to be missing is being atomic (being able to automatically set the time itself). However, most of the atomic watches I looked at were slightly too big and bulky for my taste. Besides, this watch is so accurate, once you set the time correctly you won't need to readjust it very often at all.

However, the method of making a check list of requirements and checking them off is not the be all, end all of choosing. Interesting enough, just about every watch has its intricacies and quirks, this watch is no exception. Perhaps the biggest problem with this watch is reading it in the dark. The analog hands glow (somewhat) in the dark and and there is a button for lighting up the digital readout (which even lit up, is hard to read for my old eyes). Another defect is that the alarm (for the alarm clock and the countdown timer) isn't very loud. The only other problem I can think of is about once an hour the minute hand partially blocks the digital readout.

In short, buying a watch involves compromise. One should be aware of what compromise you are making before buying. Different things are important to different people. I am quite happy with this watch, compromises and all.

product_title: Fossil Men's FS4674 Ansel Chronograph Stainless Watch
review_headline: great watch, the only one I wear!
review_body:
I have been in the market for a new watch for some time, but I put off making the purchase. Finally, I saw this watch in a store display case on sale. It was a great looking watch and at I reasonable price so I decided to give it a try. I absolutely love it. I have had the watch for about three months now and I have had no issues. Granted, I expect a watch to last many YEARS not just months, but at this point I feel comfortable writing a positive review. The picture online doesn't do the blue face justice, the blue has a real depth that really looks sharp with the silver hands and white markings. Figuring out how to use the chronograph is a little confusing, as the directions are generic for several variations on how your chronograph might work (the \\"chronograph\\" refers to the small dials within the larger face). I have included more on the chronograph, including instructions, below. The watch is waterproof and the band is very study and quite comfortable. Something I like in a watch is a slim profile. I don't like huge faces and I don't like the casing of the watch to tower above my wrist. I can happily say that this watch is a really great fit for me in the middle of the size range. The face is very medium in terms of diameter, and the casing height is (while not exceptionally slim) not so tall that it looks weird or feels cumbersome. The watch comes with all links in the band and, at least for me, the band is very big. I took the watch to Zales and had them resize it. Just FYI there are arrows engraved on the inside of the band on the links that can be removed. It may stump some people that these arrows point both directions, when normally they tell the jeweler which way to push the pins out. No worries, the bi-directional arrows only mean that the pins can be removed from either direction. They momentarily stumped the girl who looked at my watch. She thought maybe it was some strange pin type she could not remove. It's not. Overall, I love this watch. I wear itevery day and it has held up brilliantly. I love the way it looks and I would strongly recommend it. Although this is my first Fossil watch, my wife is a longtime fan. When I went in to have this one's band resized, I took in a Fossil watch my wife has had for over 10 years to have the battery replaced. Before that day, I had no idea she had had the watch that long. It looks like it's a year old and works perfectly. I'm thus far very impressed with the quality. The last watch I had was a Swatch with a stainless steel case and a leather band. It lasted two years before the crown (the turnable knob) cold wiggle around to the point that it would stop the hands intermittently throughout the day, resulting in the loss of a few minutes to several hours each day. What a piece of junk!

CHRONOGRAPH: This model's chronograph features three dials. The left and middle dials are part of the stopwatch. The right-hand dial counts up to 24 and indicates the proportion of the day remaining. In order to start the stopwatch, you merely press the top button on the watch. The second dial (middle) will start ticking. After each minute that elapses, the left-hand dial (minutes) will advance by one. To stop the stopwatch, press the top button again. To reset the stopwatch, press the bottom button and the hands will wind back. This is more or less what the instructions say, but as I said they're a little ambiguous.

product_title: Skeleton Pocket Watch Steampunk Mechanical Movement Hand Wind Silver Tone Half Hunter White Dial PW-66
review_headline: I think you get more than you pay for with this watch
review_body:
I bought this watch after reading/examining the illustration of how a mechanical watch works in the book The New Way Things Work by David Macaulay. Although some of the illustrations are simply incorrect, I've now decided that forces you to understand the material that much better, in order to see how the illustration SHOULD be.

Fortunately, the illustration was spot-on for how a mechanical watch works, and when you see it drawn out the way it is in The New Way Things Work, you think to yourself, \\"It's so obvious! Why didn't I think of that?! How Simple!!\\"

Well, that was my reaction anyway, haha.

...so that book lead me to want to buy a mechanical pocket watch. I expected to need to pay hundreds of dollars for one - and you certainly CAN spend that much on one, but I could not afford that at the moment of purchase. (...it's still probably not a prudent idea, considering they have very little re-sale value, unless one buys an antique one. Okay, enough digression.)

Well, I was very surprised to find this gem! I didn't expect to be able to find a winding mechanical pocket watch for less than a night out to dinner for two at most restaurants!

After looking over the different pocket watches sold on Amazon, I decided on this one because - although there were/aren't many reviews, I read that Amazon backed the sale for this seller, so I knew I could return it within a month if it were a POS.

It is certainly worth $40. I'm sure if you spend much, much more than $40, you can get a more accurate watch, but adjusting the time is incredibly easy, and mine is only off by about 20 seconds a day.

Also, to the person who said you need to wind the watch more than once a day: I would recommend you to have exchanged that watch, because you should not need to wind it more than once a day.

Actually, I have found that winding it only once a day results in the watch keeping better time. Each watch is going to be different; if your watch runs slightly slow, then you may benefit from winding it a LITTLE bit once or twice additionally each day. If your watch runs slightly fast, like mine does, you should wind it as little as possible. It's due to the mainspring tension, and a $40 watch will not be built with enough precision to keep time nearly the same with each individual item.

I bought this watch so that I could use the coin pocket in my jeans, the way the watch is intended to be worn. I really like the look... although I wear my shirts untucked, the chain is just long enough for it to be seen. It's also just long enough to attach on my belt loop, and easily be read when I need to know the time. I also bought this watch to examine the intricacies of a mechanical watch.

I especially recommend THIS particular watch because the design is so good, and at such a great price. You can easily read the time through the front cover because the see-through parts of the watch are ever so slightly smaller in diameter than the arms of the watch.

In short: you can read the time on this watch without opening the case; it (should) only need(s) be wound once a day; it is very, very easy to adjust the time every couple of days when it gets off too much; the components are MUCH higher quality than one would expect.

I don't know how such a high-quality, high-precision timepiece can be had at this price, but I DO know you'll very much enjoy this watch if you want a mechanical watch that keeps time quite well, and gives you something to play with every now and again. :-)

product_title: Casio Men's WV200A-1AV
review_body: For the true watch aficionado one of life's pleasures comes from hearing the hourly time signal and taking confident comfort in knowing that the watch is keeping perfect time. Unfortunately, the Waveceptor's barely audible beep is a big disappointment. Likewise, forget about hearing the alarm or the timer unless you are in a very quiet location wearing short sleeves. If you are outdoors, or driving, or someone is speaking you can forget about catching the time signal or an alarm. A representative at the Casio repair service admitted to me that they have received other complaints on this matter. But it gets worse! They told me that they had received a mandate to lower the volume on their watches. Nevertheless, I sent the watch back to Casio for inspection and a possible repair. Bottom line: they said everything was normal, just live with it. To add insult to injury, this already quiet Waveceptor actually includes a Mute feature to silence button operations. That takes the prize for the most comical unnecessary feature ever introduced!  This watch also shows world time for 28 different cities, in case that has any bearing on your life. Even though I live 1,600 miles from the time signal I've never missed a nightly synchronization cycle while the watch was sitting at the proper angle on my dresser top.  Overall, if accuracy means everything to you, the Casio Waveceptor series is for you.

review_headline: Fell apart after a few weeks
review_body: This clasp has a serious quality control problem. If you look at the product photograph, you will see a small swiveling yoke at the bottom. The yoke holds a spring bar which attaches to the leather strap where the tang buckle used to go. The yoke is secured to one of the clasp's folding arms with two pressed-in pins. The problem is that those pins are too loose a fit and work their way out over time. The first example I bought fell apart after a few weeks of use. Amazon replaced it free of charge, but the replacement has the same problem. If you flex the yoke back and forth a few times, you can see the pins starting to work their way out. I will attempt to secure the pins with some high-strength Loctite 271, but I am not sure that will be a permanent fix. product_title: Invicta Men's 1517 I Force Collection Left-Handed Stainless Steel Watch with Cloth Strap
review_body:
I'm not a watch aficionado, but this is the nicest watch I have ever had. I like the slightly over-sized design of the watch as well as the design of the watch face. The only slight negative I have is with the watch band. Perhaps it is because I have not worn a watch for several years, and just need time to adjust to the feel or the band needs time to break-in, but the band is a bit uncomfortable. It has gotten more comfortable after wearing it for two weeks, so maybe that is the case.

On a separate note, my experience with Amazon, not the watch, was rather peculiar based on my long history of shopping on Amazon. I have had a great experience with Amazon except for when it came to ordering this watch. My overall product score is not influenced at all by what follows. I'm rating the product not packing quality which has it's own review section.

I had to place two orders for this watch. On the first order, I purchased this watch in NEW condition, but the watch that I received was in obvious USED condition. There was no protective film on the glass of the watch, there was no tag on the watch, there was lint in the crevasses of the watch, and the pins that connect the band to the watch itself, made this weird clicking sound anytime pressure was applied that made it seem as if it was slightly damaged. I was also a bit annoyed when I called Amazon customer support, that I would have to return this order and place a brand new order for it, rather than just doing an exchange.

product_title: WOLF Heritage Chelsea Black Jewelry Trunk - 16.25W x 10.75H in.
review_body:
When I first opened the delivery box, I was surprised to see how big the trunk is. Its heavy too, but in a good way, I think, being that I have not put anything in yet. But I won't be carting it around that much anyway!

So I open the truck and was again surprised, just from viewing how much storage space there is. I'm not so sure now that I have this much jewelry, but hey I use that as motivation!

As I begin exploring other parts of the trunk, I notice that one of the shelves are lop-sided. As I further inspect, I see the slat that acts as a drawer hinge can come unglued from the trunk wall. In fact, as I removed the drawer, the slat fell down, as well as the remaining slats. Looks like the glue did not take to the sides of the trunk wall, which is also not 100% wood. It's like that better quality particle board I see at Home Depot.

I am in debate as to if I should return the item, but after reading Wolf's return policy, it seems I have to file a claim with UPS if the product is found to arrive in damaged condition. The conundrum is how would I know if its a shipping defect or manufacturing defect? A defect is a defect right? All I know for sure as a Consumer, the product was delivered to me in a way that I don't think the company designed it to be.

Please note that is is faux leather on this trunk and may not be suede in the interior. I am also concerned about the gold metal material make up and its shelf life. The quality overall could be much better though.

I will say this, don't even bother with Rawallan of Scotland! They have way too much drama going on to even be in business. Their Dede trunk was an Oprah's Fave for 2012. I ordered in December and still have yet to receive due to Customs, back order, and now trunk redesign. I demanded my money back from Rawallan and found Wolf Designs for a lower cost.

This trunk is far less expensive than Rawallan. Not that cost is the issue, but Im just looking for quality and keep coming up short.

In summation, the Wolf Designs truck is okay, but make sure yours comes in tact! I hope it lasts at least thirty years.

product_title: Timex Rugged Field Metal Watch
review_headline: Heavy watch, but works so far
review_body:
I bought this watch to replace a Casio that failed. I am rating this watch 3 stars mainly because it arrived with the plastic clip that holds the stem out and the watch off partially out of place. The stem was in the set date position and the watch was running. It says in the instruction sheet not to run the watch in this position because, "damage might occur". After a week of wear, the watch still keeps perfect time, but I have not been able to sync the date change to midnight. I don't know if that is related to the watch running with the stem in the wrong position or not, but if it doesn't work right in the next week, I will have to return it.

Now, regarding the watch itself. First of all this is a very heavy watch. It appears to be very well made and, as the name suggests, rugged. I like that there are flanges on both sides of the stem to protect it. This also reduces the possibility of accidentally turning on the indiglo light which would shorten battery life. I have a medium wrist (7.5") and it fully covers the top of my wrist. I found that I had to cinch the strap very tight to keep the watch from rotating to the side. The strap is very comfortable and is adjustable for both smaller and considerably larger wrists. It is an attractive watch and I have not had the problem other reviewers have indicated reading the light-colored hands on a light-colored background. I feel that it is fairly priced.

Had it not been for the fact that the watch was running with the stem in the wrong position when I received it and the problem with setting the date, I would likely have given this item 4 or 5 stars. I may update this review after wearing the watch longer, provided I don't send this one back for a replacement.

product_title: Hamilton Men's H64455533 Khaki King Black Dial Watch
review_headline: Very nice first day; Not so much after that
review_body:
I have been looking at this watch for a long time (over a year) and finally ordered it last week. I bought it as a used item from Amazon Warehouse Fulfillment and the package arrived quickly with a damaged box, as listed on line. It was very minor damage to a corner, with a small corner taped up, so I was quite happy with the bargain. The watch looked pristine. It looks slightly smaller in person than on line, but measures out to 40 mm, as listed. It is fairly compact, however. The band is in proportion to the watch, so it fit snugly on the second to last hole on my 7 3/4\\" wrist. I like the smaller size, but I don't think this would work on an 8\\" wrist.

I like the features on the watch very much, and wore it happily for the first day. The next morning, it didn't restart. So there was, at least, a problem with the power reserve; it had been only 6 hours. I carefully moved it to rewind, which did nothing, and only with a gentle tap would the movement start up. However, it only ran for a minute at a time. The manual indicates that the watch could also be hand wound as a backup method, but that had no effect, and I was careful not to overwind. I've had automatic watches for many years and was looking at the Khaki King as an everyday replacement for a Seiko. I wore it for the day, resetting every time I looked at it, but tried to activate it with natural movement, with no success.

I am disappointed, of course, and I wonder if this is the same watch that I read about below, that the reviewer with a 1 star review returned. I would be very wary of buying a returned item again. For what it is worth, the return process was easy. I printed off a label and brought it to the UPS store. Therefore, 2 stars. From all accounts, buyers have liked this watch model. I just got one that doesn't work.
