review_headline: A cheap watch that looks nice but doesn't run.
review_body:
I first bought this watch from Yugster. When it arrived I was impressed by its looks, but I couldn't get it to start -- it is self-winding, not electric. I followed the instructions and tried and tried, but it would not start keeping time. Finally I gave up and asked my husband, and even he couldn't get it to start. I returned that watch to Yugster, but I wanted another, so I bought one from Amazon.

The second watch was better, because I got it running. I liked it and I wore it frequently for a couple of weeks, and it kept running and kept good time. Then I set the watch aside for a couple of weeks, and when I wanted to wear it again, it had stopped. Once again I went through all the motions, but I could not get the watch running again. Now it is sitting dead next to me and will enter the trash can when I finish this review. Unless...

Maybe I just happened to get unlucky, but I've been thinking about it and I concluded that they are just bad watches. It's a $20 attractive-looking watch with a leather band. It's also self-winding, which means there are delicate moving parts inside, not a battery and a chip. How all of that would fit into a $20 watch is hard to imagine, which my experience seems to bear out.

Obviously, I cannot recommend this watch. It is an ugly ogre in nice clothing. If you think it's pretty enough to wear as a bracelet, that is the only reason to buy one. And, come to think of it, I'll sell you mine for $5.

***

This is a few hours later. I popped off the back of the watch and was surprised to see a battery and no moving parts at all! Why they send instructions about self-winding, I don't know. We wasted a lot of time swinging the watch around, which is even more annoying now that I know it was for nothing.

product_title: Seiko 5 Blue Dial Stainless Steel Automatic Mens Watch SNZF15
review_headline: What an excellent bargain in time!
review_body:
Just bought this at a bargain price, and like the other Seiko 5's I've bought, I am truly impressed what a great value this timepiece represents.

While the bracelet could be a little sleeker (and quieter), the solid construction tells me this is a sturdy tool that will last a long time. The solid steel case and bracelet, while not polished to exactly Swiss grade (remember this watch only costs around $100) are well executed and attractive. The assembly quality is flawless with no material or assembly defects that I can see even with a 4x loupe.

As for aesthetics, I really like the deep blue dial (almost black) and 'pepsi' colored bezel. The lume, like most Seikos, is bright and long lasting. I think the watch is actually the perfect modern size- manly without being hideously large.

Automatic movements, particularly Seikos, aren't known for being awesome timekeepers, but this one (so far) has proven to be the exception. It is running about +3 a day which is fantastic for ANY mechanical watch at ANY price.

Don't worry too much the water resistance though, even though this doesn't have a screw down crown, it does have gaskets and seals in all the right places to actually be water tight at the advertised 100 meters. It is perfectly suited for snorkeling, swimming and many other water sports. My other Seiko 5's (with 100m WR) have gone water skiing, boating and as deep as 30-40 feet under water with no issues. I'll update the review if this one turns out different.

However, if you dive this is not your watch; rather you should get a Seiko SKX. This timepiece is not an ISO certified diver, you would be taking a foolish chance by actually using it as your primary (or even secondary) dive timer. While I honestly feel it would hold up, but I am not likely to dive to 333 feet any time soon to find out.

If I were to suggest improvements, I would like to have the newer 4R35 that hand winds and hacks, but the7S26/36 series of movements really doen't need it. The watch will usually start running the moment you pick it up. Give it 30 shakes (swirl like a wine glass actually), set it and put it on for the day, it will be fully wound by the end of the day, and keeping it's best time.

Also I would like the winding crown to be a bit larger and easier grasp for my monster sized fingers.

Now I just have to get the black one (SNZH17)... let's go Amazon, make me a deal I can't refuse! :-)

product_title: Casio Men's AL190W-1 Solar Digital Watch
review_headline: A Solar Watch For the Minimalist In You
review_body:
My other solar watch starting resetting itself three times in 24 hours so I decided it was time to get a replacement when I came upon this batteryless watch. Instead of using a battery that gets charged by the solar cells, this watch uses a capacitor. When the capacitor is fully charged there is enough power to run the watch in total darkness for 14 days. The use of a capcitor instead of a battery sounded like a novel idea, but actually a \\"relative\\" of this watch, the Casio AL-180 was created back in 1987.

The watch is RETRO in looks and operation and reminds me of when LCD watches first came into existence. It has the tiny silver buttons, no LED backlight, no automatic daylight savings feature and no automatic leap year. For daylight savings and leap year, one needs to manually make the settings. Very old school (like back in the early days of LCD watches) which I think is part of this watch's charm.

However, this watch does have alarm/chrono functions with 5 alarms, plus hourly chime, 24 hour countdown timer and 1 hour stopwatch.

Initial Charge
--------------
I received my watch in the evening. Since it was dark outside I decided to charge up the watch using artificial lighting. I have a task lamp with an LED light bulb (that screws into a regular incandescent fixture). Since the watch's power reserve was low, a low power icon that looks like a sun was showing up on the watch's LCD display. The goal is to expose the solar cells long enough to light so the icon goes away. Since I was using an LED bulb which there is very little heat at the surface of the bulb, I placed the bulb about 1.5 inches away from the watch and left the light on overnight (about 8 hours). By morning, the low power icon had disappeared.

Likes:
-----

- solar power, battery-less
- retro look
- easy operation
- great price
- includes stopwatch, countdown timer, 5 alarms plus an hourly chime
- countdown timer can be set up to 24 hours
- easy to charge with artificial lighting

Dislikes:
--------

- no LED backlight (but this is not a deal breaker for me)
- display window tiny compared to other watches
- stop watch can only go up to 59 minutes, 59 seconds (but one can use the countdown timer as an extended stopwatch, in a sense. See the \\"geek alert\\")
- low power indicator only has one icon symbol (not H-high, M-medium, L-low)

** geek alert -- tip on using countdown timer as extended stopwatch **

If you are satisfied with only a 59 minute, 59 second stopwatch, then you can skip this section. But if like me, you want a longer stopwatch time, then read on.

I was disappointed that this watch only has 59 minutes, 59 seconds as the maximum amount of time in the the stopwatch function. But, by math, one can actually use the countdown timer as a stopwatch by subtraction. The idea is to think of hours and minutes instead of just hours on the countdown timer. I set my countdown timer to 11 hours. 11 hours is the same as 10 hours and 60 minutes. So, let's say you want to time something that takes about 2 and a half hours. I can start the countdown timer which counts backwards from 11 hours. When the timing stops, you stop the countdown and the watch shows 8:15 (8 hours, 15 minutes remaining). By math (10 hours/60 minutes minus 8 hours/15 minutes leaves 2 hours/45 minutes which is the total elasped time for the event. Note: I chose 10 hours/60 minutes as the start as that is just easier math. But for longer durations, one can choose a larger time to start from (for example, 23 hours, that is 22 hours/60 minutes). The math isn't really that difficult if one thinks in terms of hours and minutes instead of only hours as the starting point.

** end of geek alert **

In conclusion, I really like this watch. It doesn't have an LED backlight, but the watch is simple and retro. Plus, being solar and batteryless, should last a long time.

Everything old is new again.

Update (2/10/2013): I've owned this watch about a month and it works as good as new. After the initial charge when I first got the watch, the low power indicator hasn't turned on even once.

product_title: Orient Men's SEL03001B0 M-Force Stainless Steel Automatic Dive Watch
review_headline: Watch is OK except for the bracelet and poor regulation
review_body:
UPDATE

After 3 months, this watch stopped running. I sent it back to Orient to fix and also asked them to regulate the watch, it is losing 20-30 seconds a day. Orient took 4 months to get it back to me without contacting me once. They did fix it - but it still runs 20 seconds slow a day. Worse than any of my 10 other automatic watches.

While waiting for my Orient watch back, I purchased a Seiko Monster 2nd Generation - the new one with hacking and manual winding. In my opinion, it's a much better value. The Seiko bracelet is reasonably thick and has solid end links. It runs about 2 seconds fast a day. It cost me $50 less. Its only downside is that it does not have a sapphire crystal. I can get one put in for less than $50. BTW - it looks like the price for a new Monster is going up.

----------------------------

ORIGINAL REVIEW (except where starred)

I own many high and mid level Swiss and German automatic watches. From $400 to $4,000 list prices. This watch can hold its own with my watches around $400 to $500 except for the bracelet. The bracelet looks pretty good at a casual glance, but upon closer inspection, is more like one you could purchase at any mall watch shop for $30 dollars. It does not, in any way, match the quality of the rest of the watch.

Besides the weak bracelet, the fit and finish is pretty good, but the winding mechanism and screw in crown both feel gritty to me. In addition, my watch loses 10-15 seconds a day and will need to be adjusted to gain some seconds each day.

On the positive side the watch is substantial, looks great and feels good on my wrist. It also has hacking and manual winding which are a must for me.

I would only recommend this watch if you can get it for less than $300 new.

***If it doesn't keep time within 15 seconds a day or better in the first 3 weeks after you purchase it, I recommend you just send it back to Amazon. If my experience is any guide, Orient will be of no help to you.***

product_title: Citizen Men's BN0000-04H Stainless Steel Eco-Drive Dive Watch
review_body:
I read all the reviews I could find for several weeks before deciding on the Citizen Men's BN0000-04H Eco-Drive Professional Diver. Let me say right from the start I have been a Luminox fan for the last 10 or 12 years and Seiko Dive Watches before that. Also I use bifocals. I ordered this watch after returning a Timex Military Combo which had enough complexity to satisfy the most ardent Watch Geek. That's not me! Also, although it was large it was difficult to tell time with both by day and by night.

Now lets look at the Citizen Men's BN0000-04H Eco-Drive Professional Diver. The packaging was very well done. Upon seeing the watch in person for the first time I was impressed with the look. I like large watches. Rather than call it small I would say it is compact. Even without my bifocals I can tell the time because the face is compact without being cramped. It is a clean look. It is definitely not as large as Luminox or some Seiko but it has a presence and a weight that is very appealing.

I did have trouble with the small crown but solved it with a latex glove which allowed a secure grip. Not a deal breaker for me. The luminosity is very good (not as good as a Luminox but as good as Seiko).

Now the MOST important factor for me is that IT HAS NO BACK BECAUSE IT NEEDS NO BATTERY! I can't tell you the frustration over the years of changing batteries in a watch I liked and having it lose it waterproof ability because once the hatch was opened it became a heavy, expensive sieve!

The Citizen Men's BN0000-04H Eco-Drive Professional Diver has no back cover because it need no battery. This allows a very sleek look and should ensure a long life of waterproof service.

I did not like the band so I switched it out for a Hirsch Pure Rubber. You may like the original if you don't mind a rather stiff band. Is it terrible? No. Could I live with it. Sure.

I set this watch the day I got it and so far it is dead on afteralmost two weeks. That is outstanding. In short the Citizen Men's BN0000-04H Eco-Drive Professional Diver is comfortable, good looking, keeps really good time, requires no battery, and the Amazon price beat anyone else I could find in whom I had confidence.
BUY THIS ONE!

Mike

review_headline: A great watch even if the cost were double
review_body:
For the first time in a long time I am happy with a wrist watch.

The watch looks great. Clean and shiny out of the box, it was easy to adjust for my wrist size (required easy removal of two links from the band - one on each side), was simple to reset for East Coast time and will run forever (10-years) on the internal battery. product_title: Seiko Men's SSC019 Solar Diver Chronograph Watch
review_headline: Looks and feels like a much more expensive watch
review_body:
I have had the SSC019 for a while now and wanted to offer my thoughts about the watch. First off, it really does look better in person than it does in the stock photos. The red/blue scheme, commonly referred to as a \\"Pepsi\\" scheme, looks great and the fit and finish of this watch are top notch. It feels solid without being too heavy and is equally at home in both formal and casual settings. Bottom line: this watch looks and feels much more expensive than it is and it draws a lot of compliments.

The fact that it is solar powered means it requires little or no maintenance and will still be running even if you do not wear it every day which is something that mechanical and battery powered watches simply cannot do. The power reserve is good on the watch and, though I have not tested to see exactly how long it will last, I know it is good for at least a couple of weeks and the Seiko manual claims it will last several months on a full charge.

Being a true 200m diver, the crown and both pushers have screw-down locking mechanisms to protect it underwater. While the Chronograph buttons do not provide any feedback or \\"click\\" when they are activated, they are very smooth and always seem to work with a normal touch. The diver's extension on the band is also a nice touch that many manufacturers seem to leave out these days. When unlocked, the extension offers enough extra space so the watch will fit over a wetsuit. In true chronograph style, the red hand (normally the second hand on a 3-hand watch) stays at the 12:00 position until the Chronograph is activated. The \\"seconds\\" hand is at the 9:00 position and a 24 hour count is at the 3:00 position.

I can only come up with two small issues that could be improved on this model and they would not merit a full star being removed from the rating. One is that the date window (between the 4:00 and 5:00 positions) is a bit small and the background behind the numbers are blue like the dial. Rarely do I need to look at the date more than once a day and it is easy to spot once you get used to it but it is something to be aware of. Also, while the links of the bracelet are solid giving the watch a great balance on your wrist, the end links which attach the bracelet to the watch are folded. Again, this is not really a complaint, especially at this price point, but it is something that a lot of watch enthusiasts will want to know.

As I said before, this model easily passes for a much more expensive watch and, if you have any hesitation about the solar technology, all I can say is give it a try. It really is nice not having to remember to wind, shake, or replace batteries and I expect to enjoy this watch for a long time.

I hope that helps a few out there with their decision.

product_title: Bulova Men's 96A116 Marine Star Black Dial Watch
review_body:
This watch has a classy and beautiful design. The titanium case and wristband have been abused and beaten daily by yours truly, but the brushed metal still looks great. It's also much lighter due to the titanium construction than other watches made entirely from stainless steel. The Mineral face has not a single scratch or mark even though the round metal Bezel has suffered a few. I've owned watches in the past made only from Stainless steel, but after wearing this titanium watch for a year or so now, I will never buy another watch unless it's titanium. I would also be more than happy to own another watch made by Bulova, but by no means because the first Bulova stopped keeping time or failed me in any way. Great watch! Well worth the price.

Five Years Later! UPDATE: This is the best watch I've ever owned. It's received many compliments over the last five years. The last person that said, "hey.. nice watch.." I grinned and said, "yeah! it's five years old and you'd never know it .." I like taking the watch off and placing it into the hands of those who notice and they are amazed at how light it is because of the titanium steel band and case. I found something out by wearing this titanium band every day and that is that it is extremely tough. It does show some wear now on the bottom clasp but it's still minor compared to the disaster that stainless steel exhibits after five years of identical wear. The most impressive detail about the titanium case and band .. NO oxidation whatsoever. I work outdoors in a humid climate and upon inspection, no corrosion. My past Stainless steel watches would last a couple years before they started getting grimy.. I'll never own another stainless steel watch again. Titanium. Bulova. Oh.. and I forgot to mention, I have had to replace the battery twice! Good luck and if you buy a Titanium Bulova, wear it every day and don't worry about it .. it's made to last and look good years later. I'lldo another update in another five years. :)

product_title: Seiko Men's SNZG15 Seiko 5 Automatic Stainless Steel Watch with Nylon Strap
review_body:
I've wanted an automatic watch for daily wear for some time now. I wanted one that was reasonably accurate so I don't have to re-set it all the time. However the general rule has been that cheap ones are never accurate and accurate ones are never cheap. This watch seems to be an exception. It's self winding, which is a plus and is plenty accurate for my needs.

It's a classic looking watch. Nothing flashy or gimmicky which I prefer. It's great for daily wear with the super comfortable nylon strap. The size of the watch is about perfect on my wrist which measures 7.25\\". I use the 6th out of 10 holes on the strap. The hands & hour markers glow in the dark. The glow is quite strong if you were in sunlight all day. If you hold it near your ear, you can hear the watch ticking. I have a Malaysian movement watch.

This watch is a great value. It keeps time as well as an ordinary quartz watch, but never needs batteries or even winding, just wear it. It's stylish and comfortable enough for daily wear. Definitely keeps time better than automatic watches from designer brands that cost up to 3x as more. I never understood why people buy watches made by companies that specialize in designing clothing. Buy a watch from a proper watch maker, not a generic manufacturer white labeled watch!

review_headline: nice watch, but NOT chocolate colored
review_body:
First, this is an inexpensive fashion watch. If you are expecting something high end, don't get this watch.

I think it's VERY cute and very large. It's also lightweight, and not super substantial, but it doesn't detract from the look of it on your wrist. It is easy to adjust the bracelet and it looks great on. The face is huge, easy to see, and has 3 subdials. The crystal accents gives the watch a blingy feel.

The clasp is pretty weak, though. I can see the clasp breaking with repeated use. But for the $$ I paid, I'll probably still be able to wear it until I just get tired of it. Again it's a super cute watch.

Really, my only complaint is the color. This really isn't CHOCOLATE. I ordered the rose tone version of this watch when I ordered this one, and honestly, I thought this one WAS the rose tone watch! It wasn't until I got the rose tone watch that I could see there was a difference between the two. The color of this watch is more like a penny copper color. The face is a little darker, but \\"chocolate\\" this is not. The picture of this watch looks brown. But that's not what the color really is.

I am going to keep this watch, because the color is a bit more subdued than the very flashy-looking rose-tone version of the same watch. But I had to take off a star because the description on this is way off.

Overall, I do really like it, though.

product_title: TAG Heuer Men's WAJ2110.BA0870 Aquaracer Automatic 500M Calibre 5 Watch
review_body:
Hi, I see that many people are very excited about their NEW watch... so was I. I've had mine for almost 2 years already and still love the watch. There is however a terrible design flaw: the tube in which the crown screws down into is extremely fragile. Please note that I used the word \\"extremely\\" and I am not exagerating. If you are going to use your watch all the time, then probably there is no issue. But if you are going to use a different watch frequently for the weekend, let's say, then you should consider this issue.

On my first year with the watch, I never took it off, even while doing sports. I play tennis 2 -3 times per week and go to the gym in the morning 3-4 times per week also. This is when the watch seemed to big and smelly (because of the sweat), to carry arround all the time, so I decided to buy a Polar watch, which you can hardly feel in your wrist and is suitable for my lifestyle. This meant I was only wearing my tag on some weekends and had to fix the time and date very frequently. One day I noticed that the crown did not screw down properly so I took it to the repair shop where they told me that the tube had broken. No big deal, I fixed it for about $150. The told me I had to be very careful when screwing down the crown, because the tube was really fragile. Ever since then, I was VERY careful when setting the time and regardless of being VERY carefull, the tube broke again 6 months later.

At this moment, I am getting the watch fixed for the second time and decided to do a little on-line research. It turns out that this is a common problem for this model and Tag has not changed the spare tubes, with stronger/tougher ones. They still make the tubes with \\"merde\\" (pardon my french)... and this is supposed to be a tough watch!

I am keeping my watch, because I really love it. It seems that the solution would be to buy an automatic winder, so I don't have to be setting the time and date every weekend. Hate to say that I've had for 6 years a $120 Citizen for diving, that has never broken the tube, even when handling the watch like a man!

product_title: Invicta Men's 1894 Subaqua Nomo III Chronograph Stainless Steel Watch
review_headline: Great balance of style, function and size
review_body:
There's a reason why Invicta hasn't been able to retire this model from their line-up. I own several Invicta watches - I'm an addicted collector of the brand. I'm slowly picking up most of the \\"classic\\" models over time as well as snapping up the newest models that suit my taste. If you like larger, over sized watches this brand is for you and if you're just getting started in collecting the brand this is a good model to start with. Compared to other watches in the line up this is on the larger \\"mid-size\\" - but remember compared to what you would buy at a department store that doesn't sell the brand it'll appear to be HUGE. This model is SUPPOSED to ship with a set of poly straps, extra lug pins and a bracelet removal tool - mine shipped from Amazon did NOT so I promptly returned it and made a purchase from Costco - I'm not a member (the closest store is about a 40 minute drive so it's not worth the drive to have a membership) but you can still purchase this model (straps, pins, and tool included) for about $40-60 less then most of the partners or Amazon fulfilling it charge - even adding in the fee for non-members and taxes I was ahead with the Costco purchase. Ok so on to the watch itself. The finishing, details, and overall quality of this is on-par with Invicta's Reserve Collection even though it's not part of that series. The outer portions of the bracelet are high polish with the textured inner portion - the look is of a 3 piece link but it's not (which is ok - it's still solid stainless and well finished). You (should) receive 5 additional straps and they are indicated as poly though they really feel as soft as silicone - very comfortable and if you're new to larger/heavier watches you may want to first wear the straps instead of the bracelet to get used to the weight of the timepiece - you'll most likely have to size or have sized the bracelet as only someone with very large wrists (probably close to an 8\\") would be able to wear the bracelet unsized. The watch is easy to read and there's plenty of lume to help in low/no light situations though I haven't tested the lume yet for overall brightness or length of charge. The watch face sports a date window at the 4:30 position, a second sub dial at the 3:00 position, a 10th of a second dial at the 6:00 location and a 30 minute \\"totalizer\\" at the 9:00 mark. The second hand moves during the use of the chronograph along with the 1/10 sub dial and the 30 minute sub - when the minute hand reaches the 30 second mark the \\"fast runner\\" stops but registers when the start/stop pusher is depressed to stop the chrono. The unidirectional rotating bezel is easy to operate - I don't know if it's 120 clicks or less - it feels somewhat \\"cheap\\" compared to higher end dive watches but no where close to being \\"cheesy\\" or poor quality - it's not loose or excessively tight but a bit \\"hollow\\" sounding as though the spring is a bit long - this is a very, very minor \\"nit\\" and if you hand the watch over to someone asking about it the watch feels of high quality and detail. The crown and function pushers are screw-down type which no doubt adds to the 500M WR. The locking crown guard adds to the look and ruggedness of the timepiece. The second hand (for the chrono) came perfectly zeroed which I can't say the same for some other brands at much higher prices. The pictures don't do this timepiece justice - the main dial/face is more silver or shinny pewter not as \\"white\\" as it looks to be in the pictures.

The bottom line here is you are getting an incredible deal:

500M WR - even though you may not dive - it's bragging rights
Swiss Made (not just Swiss parts or Swiss movement)
5 additional straps in addition to the stainless steel bracelet
screw down crown and pushers with locking crown guard
nice 3 slot dive/impact case - you can store more of your collection or other items in

For under $300 (purchased pretty much anywhere will be closer to the $200 mark) you're getting what would be at most retail stores over $1500 - the retail price tag on the watch was listed at $1100 - most of the time those price tags make me laugh - on this one I'm not so sure it's _that_ far off.

I'm not really sure about some other reviewers that have had hour markers or hands come off - I guess that with over 3000 models and probably hundreds of thousands sold there has got to be a few \\"duds\\" but that hasn't happened to me and if it were I'm not too sure I would be soured on the brand - Invicta quality has always been top notch for me - I am a bit concerned about the overall customer service if/when I need to get my watches serviced - I think that for any of my watches rated at 200M and beyond I'll have the manufacturer replace the battery - otherwise I'll have my local watch shop (yes there are still a few around) service them.

Update:

The smaller links in the bracelet ARE 3 piece - not a huge deal either way - the larger (end links and second to end) are one piece - they are linked together with screws - all links that are able to be sized are 3 piece but are extremely well fitted which gives the impression they are from piece of steel - the bracelet links are all solid steel.

review_headline: Digital chimes are still not as good as real ones
review_body: We have two clocks with physical chimes in them, but wanted a third for our bedroom. product_title: Hamilton Men's H64425135 Khaki Night Pilot Black Day Date Dial Watch
review_body:
Very classy and beautiful watch. The skeleton sword hands and outer minute markers are an elegant and unique touch. The raised minute markers of gleaming brushed steel is also quite majestic. The lume is fantastic, however the numerals are not lume painted.

The reflective design of the numerals will reflect even the lowest amount of light, and I gather this may have been both an aesthetic and utilitarian design choice to increase visibility in low light conditions.

This particular model is 38 mm, and it's very wearable on my small wrists. The lack of a bezel makes it wear more like a 40. This pilot model is also available at 42 (quartz only) and 46 mm.

The ETA 2836-2 workhorse movement will not disappoint. Mine's running a bit fast, but only less than 5 seconds a day. I hear it takes a while for these movements to \\"break in\\".

The steel bracelet adds a reassuring heft and is balanced, comfortable and well constructed.

This model DOES indeed have a case back display. Amazon's description needs to be corrected.

Amazon shipping is first rate. Next day shipping to a great carrier. I received mine in just 4 days with expedited shipping to Canada.

If you're on the fence about this one, I hope I helped!

product_title: Tissot Men's T0444302105100 PRS 516 Stainless Steel Watch
review_body:
Having never owned a wristwatch, I was struck with idea of getting one. Since I didn't know much about what makes a good watch, I spent some time doing research on the internet.
I know I wanted an swiss automatic sport watch. I discovered brands such as Tag, Oris, Omega, Hamilton, and Movado. For my first swiss automatic I didn't want to spend a lot of money but still wanted a nice looking, solid timepiece.
The Tissot PRS516 caught my eye and the reviews were almost unanimously positive. It is quite heavy and really sturdy. It feels more expensive than it is. Very classy looking.
I do have several minor complaints. It seems to need some calibration because it runs a bit faster than I like.
My second complaint is the bracelet. It surely is of high quality but the fit is a little off. I had a half a link and a whole link removed and it still is a just a little large. When I removed two whole links, it was too tight.
The moral of the story is: if you are looking for a great quality swiss automatic sport watch that doesn't break the bank, this is your watch.
Just a side note that you do not get the manufacturer's warranty. Instead you deal with Amazon (which I hope is not painful).
After a week of wearing the PRS516, I went out and purchased an ORIS F1 Williams. I can see a watch addiction forming. (by the way, the Oris F1 willaims watch is a step above the PRS516 but I love the Tissot too)

product_title: Casio Men's W756-1AVCR Sport Watch
review_body:
I referee soccer and was looking for a decent, but relatively cheap watch to wear when I call games. The fact that this watch has preset countdowns for all the variables I would need for soccer is outstanding. No setting the time for every game. I also love the fact that when the countdown hits zero, you can have the timer automatically start over (not ideal for soccer) or start to count up. This works great for keeping track of added time or just keeping track of time for the half.

The functions seemed easy enough to set (I didn't have to crack open the book to reset the time).

Cons/Pros: The alarm sound isn't extremely loud which could be a pro or con depending on how you look at it. If you are allowing play to continue and players hear the beep, they might stop even though you didn't blow the whistle. If you aren't paying attention, you might miss the sound, but you should be paying attention to your watch throughout the match.

The clasp on the band seems a little weak so I'm a little concerned about how well it will hold up, but for under $18 you can't expect too much. If there were a higher priced version of this watch that had a nicer band and maybe a split time (count up and count down shown simultaneously, I would probably buy it.

As mentioned in another review, the actual time displays in the small portion of the screen when you are using the countdown timer which is nice.

product_title: Invicta Men's 6932 Speedway Professional Collection 18k Rose Gold-Plated and Stainless Steel Watch
review_headline: Excellent Value for a brand name timepiece
review_body:
I own a LOT of watches. Everything from a $40 Timex Ironman to a Breitling Aviator. Ask any good Jeweler and they will tell you, when you buy any watch you not paying for a time keeper, a cheap Timex will keep just as good time as a $7000 Breitling or Rolex, and if taken care of will last a long time. When you buy a high end watch (Or even a lower end watch for that matter) your paying for the Jewelry and appearance. The local Jeweler that I take my watches to for repair (He is a small shop but rated number two in the state), has this exact Invicta on a shelf. The asking price is $315, the retail is $450. Now I know you can get Invicta's even at Walmart for under $100. But this particular model (The 6932) does usually run around $250-$350. But what you get for this price is pretty good. Dont let the fact that it is made in Japan deter you, the Japanese have moved light years ahead in recent years when it comes to precision time pieces.

First, the flying wing is Invicta's, but it is clearly a knockoff of Breitlings design. It is slightly different, but it is a nice touch to a less expensive watch as it gives it a more high end look.

The bezel and crown are 18k Gold Plated. That is something you usually see on a more midrange watch. On lower end watches, a lot of times they will use Gold "Color". If you look at some watches, like the Marc collection sold at Saks, they go for around $250-$300 and that isnt Gold, thats Gold Color. This is Gold. Plated yes, but still Gold.

The rest of the watch is Stainless, unlike some of the cheap pot metal or tin that is used in watches in this price range.

The first thing I did when the watch came was take my watch tool and pull the back off to look at the movement. I believe its pretty intricate and is going to last a long time, and even if it stops or breaks would be worth fixing. I compared it to my Seiko SBDC001 (A $600 watch) and one of my Hamiltons, I am no Jeweler but they appear to be near identical movements and the two I compared it to are both $5-600 watches, I think for the movement, this is a great value.

Another thing I always consider is "When would I wear this watch?". I rarely wear my Breitling, its way too flashy to be walking around with on a daily basis, I wear my Ironmans, G-Shocks and Seiko on a daily basis. But the Timex Ironman and the Casio G-Shocks I wont wear if I have to go to a function, Ill usually wear either my Seiko or a Movado I own. I put this watch like my Seiko, I can wear it daily, in jeans, or I can wear it out to a function. Its one of those just right watches, not cheap looking, but not over the top either.

The bottom line as far as I am concerned, on this watch is "This is the best $600 watch your going to get for under $100". Period. review_headline: Bad reflections with lights on - hard to see the time
review_body:
I was actually waiting on the watch counting days for it to arrive - I liked the photo on Amazon so much that wanted bad to wear it. You may be totally fine without having high expectations like I did, but as for me - I'm disappointed.
I will start with PROs: it keeps time fine, it is made well. There is an extra black strap in the box with extra pins. Pins are great, they have special tabs to press so straps can be changed with no tools, takes 1 min.
However, for me there are two serious cons so I'm thinking about sending the watch back. First issue: the face is black but it is not true black like on the Amazon's picture. I've posted a picture of my cheap Invicta Russian diver (paid less for it actually). The black face is much darker and it makes time easy to read. Second issue for me: the crystal (glass) is not flat. I guess it is more expensive to make the crystal domed on top but I see two problems. 1. The crystal sticks out about 1/8\\" from the case on its center so it is much easier to scratch it. 2. Combined with the face that it is not true black, it adds A LOT of reflections with the lights on in my office (they say that doomed crystal shouldn't have any!) and adds distortion. So, every time I check the watch I find myself wanting to grab a napkin and clean it even if it is totally clean.
Don't get me wrong, it is a good watch. 3 stars I mark it - \\"It is OK\\", not \\"I love it\\" and not \\"I like it\\". If you are not picky it will work fine for you. But the Amazon's photo and the original look too different for my test.

product_title: Tech Swiss TSNP20CHERRY Watch Box Storage for 20 Watches Extra Clearance Burlwood Window
review_body:
If you've purchased watch boxes before from this seller (Watchmaterial) beware that these are not the same high polished lacquer finish as they previously were. The description makes it clear that they have a "Burlwood Finish" but what they do not tell you is that the boxes appear to be made from some sort of pressed wood material and then covered with some type of "paper" finish. These boxes that are now being sold are nowhere near the quality of what they were selling 1 to 2 years ago (I have several of those also). I am aware that I could have returned them but I needed to get some watches put away and didn't have time to look for another box vendor that would give me the quality box that this vendor (Watchmaterial) sold previously. If you look at the date of the reviews, most were done when the other boxes were still being sold and one of the reviewers even has pictures that show the high polished lacquer boxes and not the ones currently being sold.
If you have big watches, Invicta Sub-Aquas for instance, do NOT think that you can fit them side by side, that won't fit without the crown guard hitting the adjacent watch!

I guess that my biggest problem with the boxes is the cheap paper type finish. If you want to pay $80 for what in my opinion is a $20 product, go for it but don't forget that you were warned............I know after buying many of these boxes from Watchmaterial in the past, these will be my last. Fool me once.........

product_title: Citizen Men's AT0200-05E Eco-Drive Stainless Steel Watch with Green Canvas Band
review_headline: My main watch when I'm not wearing a suit or a smart watch 4 years later!
review_body: And in all of the time that I've owned it (EDIT: Year+ or so), I've only ever had to change the calendar date (for those months which don't have 31 days), and for daylight savings.  This thing is accurate, easy to read, and with the solar panel in the face, I have no fear of having to change the battery.  The crystal is pretty durable too, I have only very fine chips along the other-most edges, with no noticeable (read deep or distracting) scratches.  I haven't been beating the hell out of it, but I haven't been ginger either.  The glow in the dark numbers stay very readable in the dark with just room light, better from sunlight.  One thing, the band has grommets in the openings for the size holes, so I suggest you search for a separate band (like any of the 20mm Zulu 2 Ring Nylon Watch Straps, which is what I'm currently using).  I replaced the stock band within the first week, that's my only complaint.  UPDATE:  OVER 4 years later, still have the same watch, and all features work perfectly :)  It has scratches and a few minor dings, but nothing serious, and I only replaced it with a Pebble Time Steel because I wanted a smart watch.  This Citizen is going as strong and accurate like the day I bought it.  I STILL only have to update the time during Daylight Savings, and the calendar when I leave months that don't have 31 days - that's it!  It keeps time really well.  Never had a battery issue.  Go solar!  It's worth it. :)

product_title: Seiko Men's Watches Premier SNP003P1 - 5
review_headline: a technological marvel - but I cannot always read it -useless dials
review_body:
This must be the ultimate geek watch. An electromechanical alternator charges a lithium ion battery. The watch is powered by a 2mm thick PIEZO-ELECTRIC motor. A technical marvel, electrostic voltage changes in a piezo-crystal contract the crystal periodically, in just the right places. The periodic contractions move a cog wheel. (Note, no magnets and copper coils are required.)

The watch features a \\"hibernation mode\\". After longer times of no wrist movements (usually a few days), the piezo-electric motor and all mechanical parts of the watch are shut down. However, the electronic circuits keep working and counting the time. The \\"hibernation mode\\" can last up to four years. When you pick up the watch again, and thus activate the little alternator, all the hands and dials start moving for a few seconds, until the correct time, date, month and year is displayed.

Also, the watch is VERY accurate. Much more accurate than any mechanical (Automatic) chronometer. In fact, my SEIKO Premier Kinetic is fast by only one or two seconds a month.

A word also about the \\"complications\\" often touted for automatic (e.g. Tourbillon type) mechanical watches, costing tens of thousands of dollars. The SEIKO Premier Kinetic has more mechanical parts than most of them.

Now for the \\"BUTS\\":

- the watch dial is all about 'bling', 'glitter', and myopic eyesight. Result in an elegant dinner table setting, with low light levels, I often cannot read the time. In a few cases I had to look at my cell phone. Once even, in Germany (where my cell phone does not work) I had to ask the lady next to me what time it was. (She did admire the watch.)

- the display of 24h (military) time, month and leap year is all but USELESS. In fact, the watch does not even allow setting for a dual time zone. The ONE thing I would really like to see, the watch does NOT tell me, the WEEKDAY (i.e. no \\"day-date\\".)

- in a nutshell:
The whole setting for 24hours, month and leap year apparently, was designed for ONE purpose only, the STUPID \\"eternal calendar\\". I.e. the watch will show the correct date until Feb. 2100. Allow me to doubt, that the rechargeable watch battery would still work in 2100.
--

A note also re the availability of SEIKO spare parts (think, \\"battery\\"). In the mid 80-ties I bought a VERY expensive SEIKO Titanium watch. Alas, the Titanium watch band broke ~ 10 years later. When I wanted to buy a replacement band, I was all but ridiculed by a SEIKO US \\"Service Partner\\" for expecting SEIKO to keep spare parts that long.

I really didn't have $75 to throw around at the time, but I figured I'd be OK.

To get my watch mechanism repaired, according to the website, would cost half of what it cost retail.
Not what Amazon charges, but like what you'd pay if you went to a Macy's or something.

The yellow box it came in looks nice in my bookcase. I have since moved on to another watch.

If you're going to buy an Invicta watch, be SURE to buy the extended warranty. Otherwise you'll

Nice watch, though.

product_title: Stuhrling Original Men's 394.33111 Winchester Mechanical Skeleton Silver Watch
review_headline: Wow, nice looking watch but it broke on the first use
review_body:
I received the watch well packaged in an overly large and sturdy box. The watch was securely fastened to a little pillow and strapped down with elastic straps. It was also completely surrounded in a soft plastic cover to protect all parts from scratches. It came with the standard micro-fiber wipe to clean the crystal face and the standard documentation/warranty registration card.

I opened up the watch and wound the spring. To my surprise, I did this at exactly the hour/minute the watch was already set to! Counting it as good fortune I proudly strapped the watch onto my wrist. It was 3:11 in the afternoon and you're supposed to wind these watches once per cycle aiming to wind it at the same time per cycle, 24 hours in this case. Since I wasn't going to wind the watch at 3:11 every day I let it run out that night and in the morning my plan was to set the time and wind it again.

I was pulling the knob out to engage time setting position and it snapped off before it even moved into time set position. I fill out my warranty info online and send their customer support an email, hoping to resolve this quickly. Sure enough, they reply back within a few hours, but I notice for some reason the subject says [SPAM] and I'm wondering if my email client marked it as such. As I read through the email they indicate that since it was within the first 90 days they will go ahead and wave the return processing of $20.. well thanks since I just gave you $100 for a broken watch 4 days ago. Then I notice the subject again, in the quoted email. The SPAM was marked at their end, as well as \\"Sender is probably forged.\\" I don't have any idea why they wouldn't remove this as standard process before replying to a potentially real customer (in this case it was). I know it's some automated system, but it just angered me that they are too lazy to remove that from a subject, but they expect me to box up their defective product, pay for shipping back to them and wait an unknown amount of time without my product. On top of that I now know if anything goes wrong in the future I'll be out the cost of shipping and a $20 fine for the product's return. Maybe I'm expecting too much from customer service, but my attitude is that if I sold someone something that broke immediately I would have remorse and take a hit on my side to regain trust. Especially in a repeat market like watches.

I just can't give it more than 1 star until it's fixed and has survived more than 1 use. It's a pretty awesome watch otherwise.

product_title: Seiko Men's Silvertone Solar Expansion Scs Watch
review_headline: Nice Watch, Except for the Band
review_body:
I think this is the best-looking black dial Railroad-Approved watch out there. I like the traditional spade shape of the hour hand, and that the hour and minute hands are *white* rather than polished metal, which can be hard to see under some lighting conditions. It would also have been nice to have an orange or yellow second hand rather than the dark red, which, as you can see in the photograph, is barely visible against the black dial.

The downside of this watch is the ugly, skin-pinching, hair-pulling, hard-to-adjust expansion band. I can only guess that Seiko decided to use this band in order to make the watch look as much like the classic Bulova Accutron Railroad watch as possible. When I saw that the watch had a folding clasp, I naively assumed that the clasp must have some means for easily adjusting the band length. Not so. As near as I can tell, the clasp has no function whatsoever other than to make it *slightly* easier to lay the band out flat for length adjustment. That adjustment is performed in the traditional Speidel fashion of bending and unbending sheet metal tabs and fussing with little staples and springs. No instructions are provided.

I dumped the expansion band and installed a Hadley-Roma MB5916WCE20 Oyster-style folded link stainless steel bracelet. The curved ends fit the Seiko case perfectly and the brushed finish is a dead-on match to the satin edges on the watch case. The watch now looks and feels 100 percent better. Too bad Seiko didn't make it that way in the first place.

product_title: Hadley-Roma Men's MB4426RWSE-22 22-mm Stainless Steel WatchBracelet
review_headline: Fits my Casio calculator watch (DBC-32) perfectly!
review_body:
In an attempt to reconnect with my inner geek, I purchased a gorgeous Casio calculator watch - the DBC-32D. The watch is great, but the bracelet that came with this watch was a real hair puller. So I ordered a couple of the Hadley Roma replacement bracelets. I ordered this one and the Jubilee style with wrapped links. The Jubilee was half the price and, subsequently, half the quality. I sent it back for a refund and kept this one. The quality is worlds better.

If you are deciding between the two, get this one. It's more money, but it is ultimately what you'll want. It feels great on the wrist and holds up very well to dings and scuffs.

LIKES:
* Solid Links - it adds a good amount of weight to an otherwise lightweight watch.
* Nice brushed finish that doesn't seem to scuff easily.
* Looks and feels a lot like the Rolex Oyster bracelet.

SURPRISES:
* This is a driver's bracelet. Who new? It has an extension that unfolds from under the clasp. This adds about an inch to the length of the bracelet so it fit over a wet suit.

CONS:
* No Spring Bars! You'd think that they would've include them, but mine did not come with spring bars. I just used the ones that came with my watch. No worries, just an FYI.

TIPS:
* The bracelet I received only had flat end pieces. Curved ends were not included. This is fine, because those are the ones I needed and the ones shown in the photo on Amazon. Just make sure that's what you need before you order.
* The pins are tapped in. To remove any of the links, you'll need a small hammer and something like a thumb tack to tap them out. You could also order a cheap watch band repair kit from this site. Or... just take it to the mall and have one of the jewelery stands do it for you. :)

Overall, an awesome watch bracelet at an awesome price. I'm very happy with this purchase. Thanks for reading this. If you have any questions, feel free to write them in the comments below. Cheers!in the comments below. Cheers!

product_title: ESQ Movado Women's 7101320 Sienna Two-Tone Bangle Bracelet Watch
review_body:
Well, it was Christmas time and my wife was looking for a new watch. She's NOT a \\"watch\\" person and could care less about brand, etc. I knew she wanted (needed) a bangle bracelet watch, and I knew she wanted a two-tone (gold/silver) look.

Like most women, I also knew she wanted it to work, without constant adjustments (like an \\"automatic\\" type watch would require). I showed her pictures of many watches to get an idea of what she liked. In the end, I picked up this one. Yes, it's Movado's \\"lesser\\" line, but so what? Again, she's not a brand hound. She doesn't show off her stuff, she just wants it to work, and she want's it to look good. This watch fits the bill. Frankly, she'd have been happy with a $50 watch, but she deserves more (especially after 20 years of marriage!)

The face is classy, the two tone looks fantastic and looks great with the other jewelry she wears. I set it when I first got it (early December) and it was still spot on when she opened it Christmas morning (of course, it's a quartz watch!).

I felt it was a fantastic look and a great price for a sweet looking time piece. Time will tell if she gets many years of service out of it or not, but it will sure look great on her wrist while we find out!

One note, I needed to shorten the band a few links to fit her (very slim) wrists. This might be something that most people can't do themselves at home. I have a set of \\"watch\\" tools (I picked up for $6 from Amazon) specifically for this purpose - a \\"just in case\\". I have no problems fiddling and figuring things out (and reading \\"how-to's\\"). So keep in mind the band MAY need to be adjusted, and you MAY need to visit a jeweler should you not have the tools and/or knowledge and/or confidence to adjust it yourself (remove/replace links).

product_title: Casio Men's GW9000A-1 G-Shock Mudman Solar Atomic Watch
review_body: Previous to the Casio, my watch was an analog (different brand) that required a new battery after 5 years. Replacing the battery in a manner that kept the watch waterproof would have cost more than this watch.     From the Cincinnati area, I have been able to synch the watch with an atomic clock manually and presume that the watch perform this function on its own. As I write this, I have checked the time against the official U.S. time at the website [...] and the watch is accurate to the second.     The watch certainly appears to be rugged. I inadvertently dropped it from a height of six feet without a hiccup.     The waterproof feature of the watch means that I do not have to remove it when I wash dishes, take a shower, or perform routine activities during which watches get wet.    The manual does mention some things to avoid with the watch, particularly with respect to the resin band which is degraded by contact with toiletries, gasoline, solvents, and paint. Although the watch is waterproof, the resin band will degrade over time with prolonged exposure to water. With the possible exception of the resin band's aversion to toiletries, the watch seems more rugged than the flesh underneath it, so that works for me. Casio also recommends that the seals on the watch be replaced every two to three years, which presumably varies with use.    The time is easily readable in all daylight conditions I have encountered. The dial cannot be read in the dark without illumination, but the watch has an automatic illumination feature which lights the dial when it is turned towards the face. The automatic illumination feature can be turned off in favor of push button illumination via a button at the base of the face of the watch.    So far my only reservation with making an unqualified endorsement of the watch is the solar powered feature. Our area has had three consecutive days of cloudy skies/rain twice since I have purchased the watch and each time that has happened, the batteryindicator has decreased by one bar. All features on the watch still function at that level of power and the watch recharged successfully with about 30 minutes of sunlight once and with about 8 hours under a lamp the second time, as claimed in the user manual. Casio claims the watch will recharge for normal use through exposure to daylight even on cloudy days, but of course for the watch to recharge it has to be exposed to light and my suspicion is that I do not always have it exposed on rainy days. If you live in an area that is especially prone to overcast/rainy weather then you might want to think twice about solar power but for me, this has been an extremely minor inconvenience.    For me, Amazon's service has been so routinely outstanding that it is easy to take it for granted, but once again, item received well-packed, on time.

product_title: Timex Men's Ironman Classic 100 Full-Size Watch
review_body:
I recently replaced my \\"standard\\" Timex Iron Man watch with the T5E231 100 Lap watch and I could not be happier with the new purchase.

I've had the watch for roughly two weeks. The key benefit of this watch is the size of the display (not just a bigger case - the display itself is bigger). I was looking for a display that would be easy to see in the pool. The display for this watch is much easier to read than standard size Iron Man watches. The overall button design is simple and easy to navigate, espescially if you are used to using Iron Man's. I also like the degree of customization in terms of displaying times. For instance, in chrono mode, you can select to have your lap time or total time displayed in the primary window. I set the chrono to tracking lap times in the primary display which allows me to determine very quickly if I'm staying on pace. Since it's summer, I haven't needed to use the \\"flick\\" feature for indiglo activation but I'm looking forward to this function when winter roles around and my swim sessions take place before daylight. I also find the ability to store times very helpful in tracking my overall workout patterns.

I believe I paid roughly $36 for the watch and I believe that it is a great value - functional and good looking. I highly recommend the watch.

product_title: Invicta Men's 1512 I "Force" Stainless Steel Watch with Cloth and Leather Strap
review_headline: Not my taste, but a good watch
review_body: Let me start by noting this is not really my taste.  There's no accounting for taste, so if this looks good to you, knock yourself out.  Also, if you're left handed, it's cool that there are great watches for you too.  I don't see that very often.  The stopwatch function is the first analog one I've ever found actually useful.  It's actually better than my digital stopwatch.  It's very easy to read precisely and it's very easy to use, and more importantly, it's actually very accurate.  The buttons are also responsive.  This isn't just a showy feature to help the watch look cool.  This stopwatch is designed and intended for serious use.  The watch is huge!  And thick!  I actually got used to wearing it within a few hours... it's substantial, but the leather band helps keep the weight on the sane side.  That band is not leather on the outside... some sort of cloth (and it's a durable cloth) but is soft leather on the inside.  Comfortable and durable.  The date function (it's that little spec of white by the 4) could be a little more obvious, but it's as easy to set up as you'd imagine and works fine.  I wore this watch while helping do a lot of home improvement over the holiday break and I banged it up.  To be honest, I figured this was a good watch to wear to sacrifice that way, to keep my other watch pretty.  Surprisingly, after whacking this about, getting it wet, even grinding it into drywall on accident, this watch looks *exactly* as good as it did when it came out of that ostentatious yellow gift box.  Bottom line: this watch won't let you down.  If this watch is your taste (it's not mine) then you have nothing else to worry about.  --- a final note: I don't know why they do that thing with the pricing where they claim the real price is many hundreds more than it always sells for.  That's silly.  But for the actual price, this bargain is hard to beat.

product_title: Seiko Men's SKA245 Kinetic Watch
review_body: I received the watch from Imperial watches and it came with instruction manual , warranty book and card. The watch looks great. There was no reserve power left when it arrived. I shook it for around 15 minutes and it kept stopping . I needed to get the band adjusted , so I took it to a watch repair place and the Owner said that if its been sitting on the shelf a long time it will take some time to build up a charge. He offered to put it on his display watch winder for a few hours until he closed. So I picked up the watch 3 hrs later and the watch was then running and keeping time but had the 2 second tick meaning the reserve was low. I then took it home and started a simple wrist shake for for an hour or 2 every night for the last 4 nights. I now have the 30 second runoff when I press  the reserve button. Which according to the manual is 4-6months of reserve. So after five days the watch is fully charged and keeping perfect time.

review_headline: A new Skeleton in my closet????
review_body: Judging by the experiences of several other reviewers, this watch has some unacceptable issues, which one does not expect for a relatively expensive brand.  However, I have not found this to be the case with my watch so far, nor do I think it is cheaply made (I purchased the one with the black band and silver case).  The band is genuine snakeskin, watch came in a beautiful presentation box, and for the price, is fantastic value (there was a ticket in the box showing an RRP of $795!  It is very stylish, (so far) keeps excellent time - it's right up there with two expensive (battery powered) Swiss watches I've had for years - and it is fascinating to watch the works literally ticking the time away.  Although a man's watch and larger than I expected from the website photos, it looks great on my fairly slim wrist, is comfortable, and attracts heaps of comments - seems to me that there's aren't too many 'skeletons' on Australian wrists!  Although the instruction sheet says it is waterproof I wouldn't put that to the test; however I've never done this with any watch since ruining one in the surf when I was a kid.  My only criticisms are the band is quite stiff, but I'm hoping this will soften up as it 'wears in'; and with the 'skeleton' on view it can be a bit hard to see the hands, especially in low light.

review_headline: Great Watch Not a Great Transaction.
review_body:
UPDATE:

Amazon got back to me informing that they deliberately did not include the guarantee card because Amazon is not an authorized reseller for Seiko watches. However, this product is covered under Amazon warranty. I am updating the watch to 4 stars, but I still think they could have been proactive about letting me know that I should not expect a guarantee card in the box.

ORIGINAL:
Seiko watches are generally great, but through the watch buying experience on Amazon, I have realized that its very important who you buy the watch from. I should also mention that I have already returned two other watches I bought before this one, because they either had visible defects or the packaging was not meticulous enough which led me to believe the watch was substandard. product_title: Timex Men's Easy Reader Day-Date Expansion Band Watch
review_body:
I've owned one of these (black instead of white, otherwise the same) for a couple of months now.
I can say a couple of things:
1. The physical resistance of this watch is somewhat paradoxical. I fell from my bicycle once while using it, and although the bezel was noticeably scratched (the watch hit the pavement, ouch), it went on ticking with no other visible damage. But just some days ago I dropped it just seconds before falling asleep. The distance between the point where I dropped it and the floor was less than 30 centimeters, 40 centimeters tops, but it immediately broke open, the battery flew from within, and it took some serious technical service to repair it. Maybe something broke inside during the bicycle incident, and when I dropped it the damaged parts just broke loose or something. But it is paradoxical at first sight: it survived a bicycle crash but almost died from a domestic dropping.
2. I'm shortsighted and this watch helps a lot. The markers make high contrast (at least in my black version), the numbers are rather big, and the indiglo is of great service. Indiglo lights up the watch when the crown is pressed.

Very resistant (many watches would have sighed their last breath on an incident like that one on the bike). I like the band, but I have a womanly wrist, so \\"manly men\\" may not care for the band. It is a quartz machine, so it's reasonably accurate.

product_title: Tissot Men's T0134204720200 T-Touch Expert Watch
review_body: I've now owned my watch now for about a year and half and I just wanted to say a few words on it. The watch is remarkable. I have owned 2 other tissot watches and also very much liked them until I bought this one, this is now the only watch I wear, period and I wear it every day. I do not care to own another watch after this because I feel that I will not be as happy with another watch more than I am with this one. only way I would buy another is to upgrade this watch which I may do in a couple years. I use many of the functions, some of the functions I find useful are the compass, the chronograph, the alarm (I only wish the alarm were louder although it is loud enough to get me up every morning)and I do use the altimeter from time to time. Tissot is really a special company and this watch is one in a million in my opinion. you can't go wrong with this watch.

product_title: Citizen Men's BV1080-18A "Eco-Drive" Stainless Steel and Nylon Sport Watch
review_body: This watch has a LARGE face. Because the watch has a very slim case it makes the watch face look huge. I am sure that the fact that the watch face is very white adds to making it look so large. The watch measures about 43-44 mm with the face measuring approximately 36mm. The slim polished rim of the watch almost gets lost. The advantage to this makes for the easiest to read watch I own. If someone ask you the time just turn the watch towards them and they should be able to read it from across the room. The watch face is uncluttered with thick black hands and large black numerals. The illumination includes the hands and the numerals. My complaint here is that it does not last long, plus if you are in a low light situation and want to keep track of the seconds there is NO illumination on the second hand. The second hand is given a dedicated dial which keeps the face even more spartan. The date window is tiny and the numerals are deep set making it very tough to read. I find that I have to angle the watch so light will shine in the date window to be able to read. I had my doubts about the band the watch has but I have gotten to like it. The color is appropriate and the thickness of the band seems right. The band is well made and comfortable. I also use it with a 22mm khaki or black Zulu band just to change things up. product_title: Invicta Men's 9211 Speedway Collection Stainless Steel Chronograph Watch with Link Bracelet
review_headline: Worse looking in person - looks cheap & fake
review_body:
I must say I was not very pleased with the looks of this one when I opened the box. I instantly thought it was a fake.
I've read a lot of positive reviews on this one and loved the way it looked by the photos I've seen of it. Apparently I've only seen old photos of it..
The lovely texture on the dial's face gives it an expensive look, so based on this, and the positive reviews, I purchased this one from Amazon UK.
So I was very disappointed to see how different this one looks in reality, the dial's face is quite different than how it's presented in the photos here on Amazon (both .com and .co.uk), if you give it a close look.
The dial's face looks in reality like a plastic sticker has been put on it, and the nice texture is almost not visible. If I finally get the \\"right\\" lighting on it, so I can barely see the hint of texture on it, it just enchances the \\"plastic look\\" of the dial`s face. The rest of the watch, the case and the bracelet, looks and feels solid though, and it definately has some weight to it.
I googled a bit to see if this was a fake I have recieved..
What I found is that Invicta apparently made some changes to this watch, as photos I've seen in other forums of recent date (from 2011), looks like mine, and that photos earlier than 2010-2011 has the more \\"authentic\\"/ expensive and solid look that I expected.
If you look close to it, you'll see that the new version (2011?) has not the very visible texture (and actually less visible in reality), the markers at 3, 6 and 9 o'clock is missing, the circles of the chronograph is at a bit more distance from each other, this does not look good at all in my opinion and gives it a less authentic look, and the frame around the date is more rounded.
I could live with the changes of the markers, and date frame, but absolutely not with the plastic look and absence of the visible texture on the dial`s face. After all, in my opinion it is the nice look of the texture combined with the more centered chronograph circles that adds the solid and expensive look to it and made me buy this one.
So the photos Amazon present of this watch, as of today, (they'll probably and should change it soon), they show the old and nicer looking version.
So beware of that.
If you don't mind about this, this is probably a good watch. I will never know as I'm returning it..
(Thanks Amazon for great customer service)!

You can take a look here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-media/product-gallery/B0006AAS5G/ref=cm_ciu_pdp_images_0?ie=UTF8&index=0
Pay attention to the markers at 3, 6 and 9 o'clock, then you'll be able to see which one is the new or old version.
You should then be able to see the distinctive differences between them and see that the old version is much nicer looking..
BUT, as I haven´t seen the \\"older\\" version in person, I really wouldn´t know if it really does look better in reality or has the same plastic look as the newer version, but based on all the great reviews (and photos) of the old version, my guess is that the old version really does look better.
Please feel free to comment on this if you happens to have both the old and new one and could provide a comparison.

Invicta should also have named their model different after the changes so that it's possible to find out about the differences before one buy it..
Most websites and sellers presents the old version photos of it, unfortunately.

So reviews of recent date saying like \\"it looks even better in person\\" and so on, I just don´t get.. Rolex lookalike? Are you joking? Yes, the OLDER version could probably pass (again, based on photos I´ve seen, and where it was compared next to a Rolex), but absolutely NOT this new one..

I rated it 2 star on .co.uk but I have changed my mind now and therefor gives it only 1 as my first reaction was that I thought it was fake.
But I would probably have loved itif it had met my expectations.

product_title: Casio Men's A178WA-1A Illuminator Watch
review_headline: Can't Beat This Watch for the Price
review_body:
Amazon's price is practically a giveaway for this fine Casio watch.
I've had it for over a month and it keeps very accurate time.
It's light and comfortable with a stainless steel band that's easy to adjust to fit.
Please be aware that Amazon's description of the band is wrong: It's not the \\"fold over clasp\\" but is the kind you must latch with a small clip.

Note that this watch has a year setting (2000--2099) so that it will \\"know\\" that 2012 is a leap year and will show February 29. Also, when you program the month and date, the watch automatically shows the day because it knows the day from the year, month, and date you entered.

Numerals are large and easy to see: day, month, and date are plainly visible above larger numbers showing the time. There's also a dual time setting for another time zone, and you can switch to 24 hour time with the touch of a button.

This watch is intuitive to set unlike some digital watches. I barely looked at the instructions because it was so easy to set the Casio. This watch has a 10 year battery which is nice except that I have no idea when the watch was manufactured. The design dates back to the year 2000, so if it was in a warehouse for a decade, the battery might die long before 10 years from now. Would be nice to find out when my watch was made.

Amazon's $14.02 price is amazingly low because it would cost $10 to replace the battery in my old Timex. So for 4 bucks more than a battery replacement, I bought a new watch that's better than the Timex anyway.

If you want an accurate, fully functional, easy to read, comfortable, good looking watch on the cheap, you won't do better than this!

product_title: Invicta Men's 0470 Pro Diver Collection Ocean Ghost Silver Meteorite Dial Gunmetal Ion-Plated Stainless Watch
review_headline: Fantastic watch for the astronomy or sciences buff
review_body:
This is the second Invicta watch I've owned, and I'm very impressed with it. It is a larger watch (46mm case diameter, 15mm thick) and fairly heavy (my previous day-to-day watch being the [[ASIN:B0007OER0S Citizen Men's JR3060-59F Eco-Drive Titanium Skyhawk Chronograph Watch]], currently unavailable) but quite manageable compared to the [[ASIN:B00556FGEO Invicta Men's 1439 Russian Diver Rose Dial Black Rubber Watch]].

Opening the box, it's well packaged in a bright yellow gift box, with a small microfiber cloth for cleaning. The watch makes a striking statement, with a gun metal grey case and band, and a bright silver meteorite dial. The meteorite dial is etched to show the Widmanstätten pattern characteristic of octahedrite iron meteorites and some pallasites, and with my watch the dial is a flawless disc of meteorite. The significance of this pattern is that it proves the extra-terrestrial origin of the material used to make the dial. Additionally, since the pattern is due to nickel-iron crystals in the meteorite, the dial is naturally rust-resistant.

In theory, this is a dive watch. While it has several characteristics that would be useful in a dive watch (large face, water resistant to 200M, rotating bezel, luminous dials), I couldn't recommend using it as such. It would be far too difficult to read at depth, and there are better watches on the market for that purpose. However, as a day to day watch, it has striking good looks and having a piece of space rock on your wrist is a good conversation item. The price is very good for a watch with a meteorite dial (compare to any of the Rolex watches with a meteorite dial, such as [[ASIN:B003V26H1U Rolex Mens White Gold President Meteorite Dial]]), and as noted a flawless slice of meteorite the size of a large watch dial is unusual.

Regarding other reviews that on \\"numerous rough edges along the casing and band,\\" I would point out that my watch was well made with fine quality, and had no such rough edges. Based on other Invicta watches I've had/handled, good quality seems to be the norm for this company.

Bottom line: Very good day-to-day watch for those interested in sciences (astronomy, metallurgy, geology, etc), or just wanting an unusual or exceptional timepiece. Not recommended for actual diving.. Based on other Invicta watches I've had/handled, good quality seems to be the norm for this company. Bottom line: Very good day-to-day watch for those interested in sciences (astronomy, metallurgy, geology, etc), or just wanting an unusual or exceptional timepiece. Not recommended for actual diving.
