product_title: Timex Men's T41101 Expedition Metal Field Analog-Digital Sandblasted Bracelet Watch
review_headline: Best of Everything for the price
review_body: I've owned my T41101 Expedition going on 5 or 6 years and it is still ticking, however it is time to replace it due to terrorist attacks.  We were going through the airport check point and I set my watch on a ledge about 5' from the tile floor to put my shoes & belt back on and I bumped it off.  It landed directly on the crown and it must have damaged some of the LCD in the digital part.  They still show but some don't appear anymore.  Everything still works, and there is no visible damage, they just don't all light up which makes it very hard to read.  I has been dropped several times without breaking, it hit just right this time.  That being said, I am going to buy the exact same watch.  I had 2 other dual analog/digital expeditions, but I prefer the metal bands to the leather which after a while stretches, tears, smells, and needs replaced frequently, at least in my case.  This watch is tough, unique (I have still never seen anyone else with it in public), and looks good.  It is nice enough to wear on the job and for fun after work.  As far as dressing up for board meetings, weddings, etc I will still wear my eco drive (but I don't want to beat my eco drive up).  It is good enough for swimming, but I don't know if I would trust it diving even with the 50m (164') WR rating.  I'll stick to my dive watch for that.  For work & everyday use, this Expedition can't be beat.  The finish has lasted well (of course there is wear and areas that it are shiny now, but you will have that with any watch short of tungsten or the new wear resistant >$300 watches.  I have not been gentle with it.  I work as a Physical Therapist in a hospital & Outpatient so I am constantly washing my hands and using hand sanitizer, bleach wipes, alcohol wipes, wipes that kill anything and seem to dissolve my skin lol, I swim in pools, the ocean etc, none of which has affected the finish (metal is easy to disinfect and looks better than rubber).  I wear it during outdoor sports & activities, aswell as military training (the burnished metal is also nice making it less reflective).  The Unique finish is nice enough to wear to work & out after work plus it tough enough to take punishment  The band is still going strong, some reviewers say it is light and flimsy, it is lighter than my Dive Watch (thank goodness for that!) but it has not broken or shown signs of failing.  It fits well and moves with my wrist so that it doesn't pinch or put pressure on the back of my hand when I flex my wrist. The small locking clasp did get loose after a few years and it did fly off of my wrist playing deck hockey landing on asphalt without damaging it.  I used a hammer and a small punch in the indented areas to tighten the small clasp up and it's as good as new.  I honestly can't remember how many links had to be taken out but I don't remember it seeming small when I got it, like some people have commented.  I like how the band lets the watch lay flat, or if you fold the band in on itself, it props the face of the watch about 60 degrees letting you use it more like a clock at your desk, night stand, etc especially when traveling.  The watch itself is smaller than a lot of the high end massive watches, which is nice for everyday use and fits easily under cuffs or gloves.  The buttons and Crown are smaller and rarely get pushed or pulled out accidentally.  The crown also doesn't dig into the back of your wrist like the larger ones on dive watches and other big watches.  I love the look of the Analog and the functions of the digital watch that they blended nicely.  The numbers are large and glow for a decent amount of time though you always have the Indiglo.  Some people commented on the second hand not lining up with all of the lines, but mine hits most of them... It's more than good enough to measure Heart & Respiratory Rates.  It keeps great time, both Analog and Digital, I haven't noticed any loss of time on either.  The second hand does make a louder ticking sound than myother watches but unless you sleep with it on and keep your wrist close to your ear it won't bother you.  The crystal face of the watch is amazing, I finally did scratch it moving into our new house, but it took carrying a couch and the face of my watch scraping against the metal strike plate. I don't think anything would have saved it, but the scratch is small and not noticeable.  It would be nice to have the crystal a little recessed, but it holds up very well.  I just changed the battery a 2nd time a month ago (right before it got dropped of course) so they last about 3 years.  The Back of the watch is easy enough to get off but a pain to put back on without the proper tools, some other reviews give good directions & warnings, but I just take it to Walmart & they do it for the price of the battery :).  It sounds like the watch breaks when it finally snaps in.  Functions: The directions are terrible, only use them to know what your watch does, not how to do it.  There are some annoying things like you can only go forward & have to cycle through (can't go backwards) if you miss your number.  Push all 4 buttons at the same time and it resets the watch.  Mine never went crazy like some people's have but I did try it to see if it would fix my digital display.  Otherwise you only have 3 buttons that work like most other watches.  If Timex wants to pay me I will fix their English Instructions for them, they do need to pay someone to do it! :)  Indiglo: Awesome, it's the reason I buy Timex watches, nothing else compares.  The darker face of the watch and the light numbers give it a cool look with the Indiglo on.  It can be on only when you push the button, or if you hold the button in for ~3 sec it will stay on 3-4 seconds, Hold it again & it will light up only when pushing the button.  There seems to be a flaw in this model for some reason there is a very tiny edge that doesn't light up right above where it says Indiglo, by the 11 that didn't get the indidiglo paint.  Thought it was just mine, but guess not.  It doesn't interfere with anything but in the dark it's not a perfect circle.  I'll live.  2 Time Zones: Nice for the military and for vacationing, makes it easy to sync the analog when changing time zones & for calling home (I do wish T2 would be replaced by the day of the week)  Alarm: Easy to set up, turn on or off, & loud enough to wake me up, though I usually rely on a small travel alarm clock, but it works in a pinch  Chime: would be nice if it didn't make all the buttons beep when pushed and still beep on the hour, I usually leave it off.  Chrono: Works like a charm and it is nice for timing anything, and it has split times.  It is nice you can use it together with the timer so I can time 2 patients at the same time if they are receiving different treatments, I don't have to walk over and look at their timers.  Timer: it would be nice to have a reverse button so you don't have to cycle through all the numbers.  It resets easily but you get used to it.  It works well & you can use it with Chrono.  Can you get a better watch?  Of course, but no watch less than $50 will touch it.  I'm buying a replacement for mine so I can use the digital features, but I will still use my current for play.  I will see if the quality is the same when it arrives.  EDIT:  Read the above for my First watch of this type that I got years ago.  It seems quality has went down hill a little bit on this one.  After about 3-4 months of wearing it daily, the analog function would stop working.  Pulling the crown, resetting the time and pushing it it would fix it, but this started occurring 1-2 times/month and eventually the analog portion stopped working all together.  It was not the battery as the digital function and indiglo continue to work.  I tried replacing the battery still does not work.  I Still Love the watch, but it's not worth sending in for repairs.  I will not be buying this watch again.  The new dual function ones have the nylon fabricbands which don't work well working in a hospital where frequent hand washings are necessary or if other things happen to get on the band i'm not sure it is possible to sanitize it.

product_title: Charles-Hubert, Paris Open Face Mechanical Pocket Watch
review_body:
I purchased a Charles-Hubert, Paris pocket watch (model number 3756) for my father almost a year ago today. It was one of the last things I did with my father before he past away so I've been very careful with this watch. I know that I'm well beyond any return possibility, but I felt you should know about one of your products.

Three times now, the stem has pulled completely out from the watch! I've had it serviced by a very reputable watch repairman each time. He tells me there is a screw/nut system that holds the stem in place and that he can only tighten it so far. It seems that, with time, the nut loosens thus allowing the stem to pull out completely when setting the time. Quite frustrating for such a new watch, I must say.

After this third time (with extremely limited use as I didn't want to damage it) I'm inclined to give up and scrap the watch. I don't know if this is a design flaw or just this particular watch, but it makes me extremely leery of purchasing another watch from this manufacturer. It's also very saddening to me as the watch was a pleasant reminder of my father that I could carry in my pocket and use as a time piece.

product_title: Invicta Men's 1552 Specialty Collection Interchangeable Watch Set
review_body:
I already reviewed the [[ASIN:B005FN09QW Invicta Men's 1553 Specialty Collection Interchangeable Watch Set]], and this is basically the same watch except that the watch case and band hardware is silver instead of gold.

It does a yeoman's job. It's not especially high-end or anything, but for everyday casual wear, it's fine. The face is large and very sharp-looking, and the bands are comfortable and of reasonable quality... nothing special, just nylon, which is suitable for casual wear. I personally haven't used any of the other colored bands, but that's personal preference. The color selection is pretty good, and the colors are understated and not flashy.

It keeps good time, from what I can tell; I haven't had to adjust it for accuracy. Setting the time is simple; the date takes a little more doing- kind of cumbersome, but that's not a big deal.

It's water-resistant to 165 feet, so I've gone swimming with it a few times and have showered with it as well with no concerns or adverse effects. The band dries quickly, and the finish doesn't dull. I should also note that it isn't a magnet for scratches, which is great for me because I'm hard on watches. It's been banged and dropped a few times, but it still looks good with no noticeable marks.

This is a nice buy at the (lowered) price. You won't wear it to a wedding or anything, but for everyday, casuel wear and light sports or outdoor excursions, it does the job and looks pretty good doing it.

review_body:

product_title: Haurex Italy Men's 8A340UN1 Yacht Black Dial Watch
review_body: This watch was suppose to be a gift for my dad on Father's day while I was deployed in Afghanistan.  When I purchased it, I thought it would be a nice watch for him.  They actually sent a \\"new watch\\" that not only had a dead battery, but it was broken!!!!  Since discovering it was broken, it has been nothing but a headache trying to get resolved.    When my dad received the gift, everything looked alright but the watch wasn't working.  So, he took it to a jewelers to try to get it look at and they let him know that the battery was dead.  Upon replacing the battery, they tried to set the time and the crown was broken.  How do you sell and ship a broken product???  So, after the jeweler replaced the battery and set the time, come to find out there were no warranty papers to get the watch serviced through the manufacture warranty.  One would think that when an item is sold with a warranty, the proper information would be included pertaining to that warranty for the product.  Not in this case.  Upon receiving the broken watch, still deployed in Afghanistan, I have since returned it and still nothing.  The item is sold out and some \\"excuse\\" from the customer service.  I just want a watch that works for my dad 's gift.  Even if something is outside the \\"return\\" period, who sells, or ships a broken watch???  To top it off, I'm halfway around the world trying to get an issue resolved, one would think it may take a little bit to receive the product in order to return it.  I will never purchase a product like this from here again, and spread the word of the this TERRIBLE experience.  Dad, I'm sorry, and yes still working to get this figured out.  I may just end up swallowing the cost for this mistake.

product_title: TAG Heuer Men's WAT2011.BA0951 Link Silver Dial Watch
review_body:
I spent much too much time researching this watch. I should have bought much sooner.

There are several negative leaning reviews of Tag watches on Amazon that influenced me to hold off but in the end, I have not experienced any of the problems mentioned. This watch keeps great perfect and it looks elegant. I didn't want a watch crowded full of bells and whistles, even the full display date on this one is a little much for me. This watch is perfect.

review_headline: 'IIII' vs 'IV' being used for the Roman #4,
review_body:
I was questioning the 'IIII' for the #4 instead of it being 'IV', and some interesting articles, this being one of them: Alan Heldman, alt.horology:
Yes, all of those theories have been mentioned. But the one not mentioned in the last post is the one that strikes me (four times) as the most likely: Classicists who have studied old Roman inscription of marble monuments etc. say that IIII was very often, perhaps predominantly, the form that was used in classical times. In a book picturing hundreds of tower clock dials, I found that about 95+% of them were in the IIII form. Interestingly, though, the most famous tower clock in the world, Big Ben, uses the IV form. There is also a hypothesis that the first clocks to use the IV form were clocks which had the rare feature of \\"Roman Striking.\\" This used two bells, a higher pitch bell representing a one and a lower pitch bell representing a five. Thus four o'clock would be struck by one stroke of the small bell followed by one stroke of the big bell; six would be struck by one stroke of the big bell followed by one stroke of the small bell. This is a very efficient system, but died out almost entirely in the early 18th c..
So I guess it's not miss numbered, but I can't say that that makes this a good or bad time piece. It does look very nice, I'm purchasing it for my guy, I'll keep you posted. I'm giving it 5stars for now for its accuracy and description, ill review it again when I receive the watch, I'm excited!

With that being said, this watch has good features, but here is where the problem lies...

There is only ONE jeweler or watch repairman IN THE WORLD that is certified to work on your Luminox (that is ANY Luminox) and that is Saltzmans Watches of Rhode Island. This is due to the fact that Luminox watches use tritium. What this means to you is that the sky is the limit when it comes to cost of repairs (competition is a good thing). Also, Saltzman will not provide an over-the-phone estimate, so if your watch has problems your choices are a) trash the watch or b) send your watch to Saltzman having no idea how much it will cost you to repair and wait. Trying to get any information from Saltzman over the phone seems to insult them and they are pretty rude. They won't even tell you what the average cost is for a standard service like replacing a battery or mineral crystal. To me that seems sketchy in itself. If they are the only jeweler to repair Luminox watches they should have it down to a science as to how much it costs to replace standard items. But they refuse to offer a quote over the phone, so you have no choice but to wait until you have sent it in, and they have charged you just to look at it. Only then they will give you a quote.

In the 3 years I have owned the watch the mineral crystal has shattered due to impact twice. The impacts were moderate at worst (wrist hitting a concrete wall while walking at normal pace and wrist hitting metal racking while retrieving items from the shelf). product_title: Aviator Tough Solar Watch
review_headline: Charming mechanical toy with a sense of humor
review_body:
Casio must be a unique place to work. They have a huge following and have pioneered certain features - such as radio synching - which are the biggest advances in watch technology in decades. But to really understand Casio watches - why people collect them and why there is something of a Casio cult - you have to look beyond functionality. Casio is culturally very Japanese, a land obsessed with playfulness, fantasy, fashion, and toys for grownups. There is a direct link from these large, bulky, exaggerated-macho watches to transformer toys, Tonka trucks, anime and manga comic books. To appreciate a watch like this GW3000, one must take delight not only in knowing what time it is, but in watching the intricate dials dance around, forward and backward, when one changes modes; a watch with a sense of humor. The sixty five page micromanual is not just a practical guidebook, it's a puzzle to be solved under a magnifying glass. This is a company which issues dozens of G-Shock versions, including a Bathing Ape watch, a pure white digital, and a Mud-Man. Endless variations. Casio is all about fun. If all you want to know is what time it is - use your cell phone.

The GW3000 model has a large analog dial and a nest of subdials, all with analog hands. No digital displays. I ordered the version with orange numerals and then I went on eBay and bought a bright orange resin band to go with it, replacing the black band. Look great together and I get a lot of compliments; my Holloween watch. Functional? Yes; I live in Western New England and it does pick up the Colorado radio signal fairly reliably and captures time to the second (although Citizen is said to be developing technology to get the time from GPS satellites, which should work even better). Solar power? Sure, I just leave it in the window all day. Is it perfect? No: the watch could use a lamp, and there is no way to tell the last time it synched. And speaking of the Holloween colors, it's as big as a pumpkin pie - not ideal if you have skinny wrists. But watching all the hands spin around in a totally unnecessary but highly entertaining jig? Priceless. Casio is all about mechano-fun. Love this watch. Five stars.- not ideal if you have skinny wrists. But watching all the hands spin around in a totally unnecessary but highly entertaining jig? Priceless. Casio is all about mechano-fun. Love this watch. Five stars.

product_title: Luminox Men's 3007 Original Navy SEAL Dive Watch
review_headline: Keeps on Tickin and Takin a Lickin
review_body: I have had this watch now for about three years and it is still seemingly bulletproof. I have, however, had to replace the band because it started to rip and would not remain on my wrist. The ruberized band itself lasted about 2 years which is good considering the a salesman for luminox said they normally only last a year. And in those two years, I barely took this thing off; not in the shower, pool, gym, or for work around the house; this watch is a quality time peice. The nylon band may last longer, but velcro does not work well if wet and in cold conditions; the velcro becomes useless. The rubber band is also very comfortable. The housing and transparent shield will, inevitably, get scuffed up, but I have really abused this watch at times. Never do these scuffs mess with the ability to read the watch.  It is really nice to have the day of the month as well, but this does not illuminate. But, this watch lights up so bright at night you can actually use it to read something if you really had to in pitch darkness. I have walked down a dark hallway at my house and this watch gave off a green aura that lit the way for me to see. It is also going to be a great watch for divers if it is not taken below 200 meters, which is a long way anyway. The rotating bezel allows you to set your time for oxygen or to time yourself at the gym like I do. The 60 second mark on the rotating bezel is also illuminated by tritium to find it easily. It has a lot of versatility for a simple design.  Luminox uses swiss quartz and the face has 12 and 24 hour time markings, adhereing to its military roots. The blackened stainless steel caseback has the Navy SEAL emblem laser etched, along with Swiss Made, adding to the coolness factor of the watch. However, I wish the little screws used to hold the caseback in place were also blackened as they do rust from the corrosive sweat you give off. My other issue with the watch is the second hands dont quite match up with the tick makes on the face. This, to me, is very trivial but it may bother some people. This watch is very easy to change to time and date if needed with the pinwheel on the side. Over the 3 years I have used it, it has never fell behind or sped up time, it always keeps accurate time.   Also, this is a super lightweight and comfortable watch you will forget you have on you unil you need it. I used to frequently wear my father's Omega Seamaster (James Bond Watch) and the thing was just too heavy and it would cut into my hand. My Fossil watch does the same thing. This watch won't pull the hair out of your arms or cause discomfort in heavy use.  This is my favorite watch and is the best I have ever owned. For the money, you get a great timepiece that will last a very long time. I highly recommend this watch to people like me who tend to unintentionally abuse things. A watch is an invaluable item to have on you and this is my watch of choice.

product_title: Citizen Watches Mens AT4008-51E Perpetual Chrono A-T Watch
review_body:
I love this watch. I have had a Citizen Blue Angel for years. That is a good watch too, but it was getting old. The numbers on the circular slide rule were pretty beat up, the crystal was scratched (already replaced once). I liked the Blue Angel for the multiple time zones, but I like the new AT4008 watch even better. Here's why:

1. The crystal is saphire. That means this is going to last for years without scratches.
2. The Time Zones work even BETTER than the Blue Angel. The Blue Angel watch required me to set the daylight Savings time for every zone. This watch has a receiver that adjusts the time every night at 2 AM and sets the daylight savings time automatically. I love that feature alone. It is easy to pick the US time zone, and if you are in China or somewhere that is not covered by the 5 preset time zones, you can adjust for that as well. The manual is easy to read and covers everything.
3. The Tachymeter works! At least one of the other Citizen's I was considering had a tachymeter on the dial, but it was non functional! This one works. The Chronometer is also pretty easy to use and is well explained in the manual.
4. This watch looks GREAT! I love the black dial, stainless band, and white letters on the dial and the tachymeter. This is a very handsome watch. It is just the right size for my wrist. and very easy to read.
5. The band has both single and half width links to make it easy to adjust. I spent $10 at Fred Meyer to have them adjust the band for me. It was worth it.

I looked for over 2 years to find a watch to replace my Blue Angel, and this is it. I also shopped around and didn't find any better price than Amazon. The final thing that got me to order this was Amazon's policy to accept it back for any reason at no charge. How can you go wrong?

product_title: Luminox Land Field Day Date 1820 Men's Black Leather Strap Watch A.1828
review_headline: Great Looking Pilot/Military Style Watch But Quality is Hit or Miss
review_body:
My requirements for a watch haven't changed since I bought my first \\"nice\\" watch back in 2010. The goal here is a nice-looking, classy analog watch that can stand up to the the torture I put watches through, while continuing to remain reliable and attractive. The watch should also be simple and easy to read in both the light and dark. I started with a Seiko Kinetic Dive Watch, and that proved to fit my needs perfectly, but I've since decided to supplement it with a pilot/military style watch. Just as most people who buy a couple hundred dollar dive watch really wish it was a Rolex Submariner (though ironically, this wasn't the case with me and the Seiko Kinetic), when I settled on the Luminox 1828 Field Watch, in the back of my head I was wishing I could afford Ball's Engineer Master II Arabic (If you're comfortable dropping a grand or 2 on a watch check out Ball. Just my 2 cents, but Ball may be the coolest watch company on the planet, and they're actually an American watch company, though like most watchmakers they buy their movement eubaches from ETA). Anyway, back to this thing: It looks awesome in person: handsome, distinct, rugged looking and masculine, yet reasonably understated (aside from the classic field watch style, I love the Luminox logo in enamel under the 12 o'clock marker, and the enamel Arabic Numerals). It even looks great at night with the green tritium lights offset by the orange 12 o'clock marker. Believe it or not, the more conventionally illuminated Seikos are a bit easier to read at night, but this one is still legible. Aside from the great looks and great (tritium) lume, the other major plus from my standpoint is the 48 month battery. Judging from the other reviews Luminox quality control is kind of hit-or-miss. I basically landed on this brand because they appeared to make watches for divers, and real dive watches are specifically built and tested to withstand constant abuse. While this appears to have most of the features of a \\"real\\" dive watch (screw down crown, screw in case back, large stainless steel case, heavy duty spring bars, thick sapphire crystal, 200m depth rating), Luminox does not actually submit their watches for testing (such watches have the word \\"Diver's\\" printed in front of the water resistant rating). Most of the satisfied reviewers appear to put their watches through fairly hazardous (for a watch) physical activities though, so between that and the features that imply a watch built to take abuse, I bit. The problem is, I've never found a really effective way to judge whether a watch that seems to be built to take a beating actually will if its an unknown brand. After reading a lot more reviews of other Luminox and Mondaine (parent company of Luminox), there were way too many reports of watches that simply broke for me to feel comfortable. I sold my Luminox on Ebay for about half what I paid and bought the Hamilton Khaki Pilot instead. While my Hamilton has a charm of its own, I still think the Luminox looked cooler, but the Hamilton is a better made product from a far more reputable company (its part of the evil SWATCH empire). In practice, the Hamilton also held up just fine while I put it through basically the same daily wear as my beloved Seiko Kinetic Divers. For all I know the Luminox MIGHT still be holding up just fine, or it might have broken. Hopefully not, hopefully the person I sold it to is still enjoying it. Anyway, the only specific out of the box issues I actually experienced were with the band (which even though it appeared to be of high quality turned out to REALLY not like water. Sure it was leather but so's the band on my Hamilton that replaced this watch), and the lugs that held the band were sharp, angular, and pointy and really dug into my wrist. I didn't put that in my review earlier because at first I assumed the watch was digging into my wrist because the band was new and stiff, but as I broke the band in, the watch did not become more comfortable, the issue was the shape of the lugs. My Hamilton (with an equally stiff band out of the box) never had this issue, nor do my Seiko Divers (which weigh twice as much, by the way, but have nice rounded lugs). Anyway, ultimately I had to cut my rating to two stars because even though my purchase didn't actually burn me, I cannot rate a product this expensive and potentially unreliable highly. Ok, $300 won't exactly get you a Rolex, but still a LOT of people who buy these are left with a busted watch after less than a year and to me that's simply unacceptable. Finally, here are 2 things I've learned about picking out a good watch both from this experience, and my subsequent reading:
1, The first warning bell should sound if your \\"Swiss made\\" watch uses a movement from an outside supplier like Ronda (the supplier of movements for all Invictas and most if not all Mondaine and Luminox watches) as opposed to ETA. It's not that Ronda is a bad company, they're not. Rather its that they aren't a monolithic semi-monopoly with a zillion in-house brands to sell to like ETA, so they don't get to be as picky about their customers. SWATCH brands, and third parties they WILL sell to (who range from fairly inexpensive boutique makers like Marcello C to VERY high end brands like Breitling and even IWC) are consistently a safe bet. A watch with a Ronda movement MIGHT be a quality product on par with one containing an ETA movement or it might be used in a piece of junk like an Invicta. So remember, \\"Swiss\\" watch doesn't always mean what you might think it means, and while there's nothing necessarily wrong with a company that buys its movement from a third party like Ronda, you have to look a bit more carefully to make sure you're getting a good product. I cost myself a few bucks in learning that lesson. Hopefully if you read my review you won't make the same mistake.

2, Brands I am comfortable recommending in place of Luminox include Hamilton (obviously), Tissot (Just as well made imo and even cheaper, the only reason why I didn't buy the slightly cheaper black faced Tissot PRS 200 instead of the Luminox in the first place is because it just didn't have quite the military/pilot/field look I wanted). If you want something a little more modern and sportier like the classic Luminox \\"dive watch\\" the company likes to pretend is issued by the Navy SEALS then I'd also say a small American brand called Reactor is worth a look. Unlike Mondaine/Luminox their products are actually made for strenuous use, and therefore they actually take pains to stand behind their products. Seiko makes some nice analog sporting watches as well and if I had unlimited funds I'd own several, however they can be tough to find and noticealby more expensive than Tissot or Reactor.

product_title: Casio Men's A178WA-1A Illuminator Watch
review_headline: Great looks, cheap, retro-cool, multiple functions, A178 vs A168
review_body:
If you're looking at A178, you must've looked at A168. Both are cool, funky watches. What might have looked as a total geek or poor-man's watch in the 80s is now hipster cool (for better or worse). Kudos to Casio to continuing to produce these 80s styles, still in 2012! Don't ever stop!

There's also the gold version which I personally favor (it's funkier IMO) but the silver one is half the cost. Amazon price is around $12-$14, which has got to be a bargain!! You may have also considered A168. You can't go wrong with either but here's a comparison:
- A178 is a tad bigger overall so it feels more substantial. A168 sometimes feels a bit small for men, A178 feels like the perfect in-between size for both men and women.
- Band is identical
- A178's display and numbers are bigger
- The look of A178, while retro, would match formal wear (suits) better. A168's face screams retro-80s more and with all the colorful labels (ElectroLuminescence, Illuminator), it might almost look comical with formal wear.
- Has dual time, A168 does not. This is excellent if you travel a lot.
- A178 has corner lit, greenish-yellow bulb light which lights up for 2 seconds on butten press; A168 has whole-screen bright blue backlight and only stays lit while you have the button pressed. The corner light is plenty bright though A168's blue backlight looks cooler IMO.
- A178's stopwatch is better as it let's you count up to 10hrs (9:59:59) before flipping over to zero. A168 is fairly limited b/c it's stopwatch can count only up to 59:59 (1hr).
- A168 has 3 side buttons, A178 has 4, one on each corner. This gives a more balanced look.

At the end of the day, you can't go wrong with this watch. At this price, it's a no-brainer. And I have both A168 and A178 BTW. I switch them out depending on mood. If you have the funds, just get both! :) Reminder: the watch is "WR" (Water Resist) - meaning you CAN get it wet but I wouldn't go swimming with it.

[Update 8/11/2013] I've recently put a nylon watch strap ("Nato" strap) on it and it looks great! Of all the retro-styled Casio watches I have, I think the silver A178 is probably the easiest to pair up with a NATO strap in terms of looks. The square face and square LCD readout gives it really nice balance. FYI - 18mm strap and spring bars. Note: there's so little space under the spring bars, you'll have to place the strap first, then put the spring bars in place and it's a tight fit. So unfortunately, you don't have the easy swapability of the straps b/c of the little clearance.ing with it.

product_title: Casio Men's W213D-1AVCF Basic Silver-Tone Bracelet Digital Watch
review_headline: An excellent light weight inexpensive watch
review_body:
I recently purchased the W213 and I thought I'd review it and pass along a few things I learned.

First off, I'm very satisfied with the watch. I chose the 213 for a combination of reasons: a) Large LCD digital display, b) very light weight, c) metal band and body, d) more than one alarm function, e) 10 year battery and f) made by Casio. In all of these things I am completely satisfied and can heartily recommend the watch for anyone seeking this combination of features. Having written a rewview of the W752, I can tell you that it's EVEN lighter, thinner (a plus to me, as I was always banging the 752's face into things when in a hurry) and easier to read. The face of the watch is very crisp and large and the numbers and display are extremely easy to read. The metal watch and band are masculine looking, though not bulky. Surpassing the 752, there are 5 alarm functions, one of which features a snooze option. I would still prefer a blue back light to the side mounted white LED, but that's a matter of personal preference and I couldn't find a watch with blue back light and 10 year battery and the side mounted white LED works just fine. For a watch that costs around $20, having a 10 year battery is a great benefit, since they charge around $15 locally to replace watch batteries in water resistant watches. Why buy a new watch battery at $15 every couple of years when you can buy one watch for around $20 and have it last 10 years.

So ... I'm very happy with my new watch and can recommend it to anyone seeking this combination of features. As much as I loved and do love the 752, the thick body design seemed to seek out things to smack into just a bit too often, and the crystal has gotten VERY scratched up. That will be my \\"heavy work\\" watch, while the 213 will become my everyday watch.

As before, there are a few things I learned in shopping for this watch that I thought I'd pass along.

1) BATTERY AND E.L. BACKLIGHT - To the best of my knowledge, Casio still does not yet offer a 10 year battery on any watch featuring blue electroluminescent back lighting. I'm assuming it draws too much power to last 10 years. If I'm wrong about that, do let me know.

2) CRACKING PLASTIC BANDS / RESIN BANDS - During past research on this topic, I learned quite a bit about plastic/resin watch bands. I used to love to purchase Casio watches with plastic bodies and bands, but stopped the practice when it became clear I couldn't keep the bands in tact for more than about 18 months. They always cracked and split long before the watch itself died. This was a consistent problem I faced with at least half a dozen such watches. I never knew why they split so badly, but they always did. Well, in the instruction booklet for 752, they happened to mention that IF you get a plastic (or, as they call it, resin) band for the watch, don't allow it to stay exposed to water or perspiration for long periods of time as it WILL lead to cracking and splitting. I was STUNNED. As a person who perspires freely and lives in a humid climate, this is virtually impossible for me to do any time I'm active for long periods of time. According to the instructions, I should remove the watch if I'm going to be perspiring for long periods of time and dry the watch off when the band does get wet. WHY on earth any company would continue to use a material for wrist bands that their own instruction manuals admit will crack and split with prolonged exposure to water and / or perspiration is beyond me. Anyone out there buying plastic band watches and working in a swimming pool? You might want to go ALL metal. AS far as I know, this must be true for all or most plastic banded watches in the world, as more than just my Casio's have met this fate in the past. I long ago switched to all metal watches and I suggest the industry find a new material that doesn't scream \\"We want you to buy a new watch every year or two\\". But that's just me. Or is it?

3) 10 YEAR BATTERIES AND WATER RESISTANCE - One thing that drew me to this watch was it's 10 year battery. As I said before, it never sat well with me to have to drop $15 to have a 2 dollar battery replaced just because the watch requires special handling to preserve it's water seal. But when I read the instructions for this watch, I was very surprised to find that even though it comes with a 10 year battery ... if you want to preserve the water resistant features, you have to have the water seal replaced every 2 to 3 years. They also suggest now (213) that you not bathe in soapy water while wearing the watch, as that also reduces the life of the seals. Now, this doesn't matter to me personally, as I don't bathe or swim with my watch on, but ... what exactly is the point of making a 10 year battery for a water resistant watch if you have to bring it to someone to replace the seal every 2 to 3 years? I made the 10 year battery a part of my selection process to avoid having to pay someone $15 every 2 to 3 years to open my water resistant watch ... only to find that if water resistance WAS important to me, I'd have to do this anyway. I don't really see the advantage here. So, if water resistance AND a 10 year battery are important to you, you might want to rethink your decision making. If, like me, the water resistance doesn't matter, then feel free to enjoy your 10 year battery as I plan to.

4) SIZING THE METAL WATCH BAND - While I found the manual that came with my Casio 752 very informative, it said absolutely nothing about HOW to adjust the size of the metal band with which it is equipped. Neither does the manual for the 213. I assume this is because the 752 and 213 bodies are available with many different bands, which a quick browse on Amazon confirms. The process isn't all that difficult, but there area few things you'll need to know and to have handy to re-size the band. The band itself comes in a size that was about 2 links too large for my medium/large sized wrist. There are two possible downsizing solutions offered: A) Move the mounting pin on the main outer clasp so that the pin rests closer to the push button release and/or B) remove one or more links.

On the 213, there are only 2 sets of holes the mounting pin can rest in. I moved the mounting pin from the position furthest from the push button release to the one closest to it. That cut the \\"too big\\" factor by only a tiny bit. I'd guess this is about a 1/2 link adjustment. I realized I would also have to remove a link or two. Here's how to do both:

MOVING THE CLASP MOUNTING PIN

The clasp mounting pin sits between pairs of small holes in the main clasp (2 pairs to choose from). Use a small metal object (fine point metal pencil tip, a thick pin, thumb tack point, tiny tipped screwdriver for glasses) and carefully push one end of the pin inward and to one side. This will remove the end of the pin from it's hole, allowing the pin to be wiggled free from between its current pair of holes. BE CAREFUL ... there is a spring inside this mounting pin and if you're not careful, once it's out of it's mounting holes, it may want to ROCKET away from you. Once the pin is free, move the pin to one of the pairs of mounting holes you think will work best for your wrist size and place one end into one of the holes. Next, slide the other end of the mounting pin along the inside of the clasp until the other end of the pin pops into the opposing whole of your choosing. The spring inside the pin will allow the free end to compress as you slide it closer to the hole and will then push the end into the hole when you reach it.

REMOVING LINKS

If the band is still too big after moving the mounting pin as far as you can, now it's time to remove a link or two. If you're going to remove links, decide first from which side it will make the most sense to remove the link or links. If you take them front he wrong side,you might find the watch fits perfectly, but sits crooked on your arm (faces too much toward or away from you). That's what I did the first time. The watch fit fine, but it sat funny on my arm.

To determine on which side it will make the most sense to remove links, put the watch on your wrist and close the clasp and center the clasp on the underside of your arm and check to see where the watch body now sits on your wrist. If it sits more to one side or the other, be sure to remove a link or links that will leave the watch face directly opposite the clasp as much as possible. For example, if, when you put the watch on, the body already sits directly across from the clasp and you need to remove two links, be sure to remove one from each side, or the watch will sit crooked on your arm.

NOTE - BEFORE REMOVING LINKS, I FOUND IT MADE THE WHOLE PROCESS EASIER WHEN I FIRST UNCOUPLED THE MAIN CLASP, MAKING ACCESS TO THE INSIDE OF THE BAND MUCH EASIER.

This band comes with a fairly easy to use system for removing (or adding) links. Several links on either side of the clasp feature a hole on the back surface (the side that lays against your skin) into which a very small screwdriver can be inserted. (If you don't have them already, I'd suggest spending a dollar or two on either a glasses repair screwdriver or one of those super small sets of screw drivers you can find in most grocery, drug, electronics and mass merchandizing stores as well as any home improvement center.) Use the smallest diameter screwdriver you can find and insert it into the whole on inside of the link you wish to remove and push very firmly and very carefully in the direction indicated by the arrow that's stamped into the back of the link. (Don't push toward the arrow, push in the same direction indicated by the arrow). If you don't have much hand or arm strength, you may need to have someone else do this for you. By pushing repeatedly and firmly in the direction of the arrow, you'll eventually push the connector piece out one side off the link. Keep pushing until the connector piece extends far enough beyond the end of the link so that you can grab it with your fingers (or, more likely, a pair of needle nose pliers) and remove it (about 1/16 to 1/8\\"). On the model 213, I found removing it required pliers. The two links joined by the connector piece you just removed are now free of each other. To free the link you want to remove, take out the 2nd connector piece attached to the other side of that link and it will come free of the band.

NOTE - If you want to remove two links that are adjacent to each other, you need only remove the connector pieces at either end of the two links, not the one that joins those two together.

Once you've removed the link or links you desire, put the final connector pin back in to join the two loose pieces of the band. To do this, just slide the two links together until they line up properly (until the place where they come together looks just like the links that are still attached to each other) and then slide the small end of the connector piece into the opening on the end of the link. Push it as far inward as you can with your fingers. This should leave about 1/16 to 1/8\\" of the connector sticking out. If MORE than that is sticking out, keep working with the connector and the two pieces it connects with your fingers until you can slide it in further. Trying to POUND it in with tools when it sticks out much further than 1/16\\" may bend the pin.

When the pin is as far in as you can manually advance it, take the watch band and turn it on it's side so the connector piece points up. Take the blade of a small metal screw driver and place it against the part of the connector piece that still extends out of the link. Use a hammer to firmly but gently tap the back end of the metal screw driver lightly a few times until the connector piece is fully back in place. I found only a few light taps worked fine.

I removed 1 link from either side of the 213 band and it fits perfectly. Thus far, after a week of use, I'm totally delighted with this super light weight, very handy watch.r away from you). product_title: Accutron Men's 26E02 Val d'Isere Diamond Chronograph Watch
review_body: I bought this watch through Amazon for my husband for a special birthday gift, and it's absolutely lovely without being gaudy or excessively showy.  (He has decided, however, to wear it only for special occasions.)  Still, it is simply stunning and lovely - even on this compact macho guy.  This is good since he is the type that would not wish to wear a watch he considered feminine looking. Also, it is not a 'huge piece,' but a rather compact display.  The diamonds are clearly sparkling and profuse, but their cut is flat-topped, so it's a bit more subtle. And the band is gorgeous with a more polished stainless steel look.  At this stage, the only drawback seems to be that it lacks the mini-adjuster at the latch point on the band back - the one which permits a pin to be moved back and forth 1-2 millimeters for each of 2-4 holes.  This means, in hubby's case, it feels too lose or too tight.  So he says. If you, on the other hand, can live with link-removal differences, and are not a huge man, this may be your diamond watch.

product_title: Bulova Women's 96R39 Diamond Watch
review_body: It is beautiful , comfortable and big enough to easily tell time!  I am completely happy with this watch!  After having a small face watch and having to strain to tell the time, I wanted a large easy to see face, but also wanted it pretty and feminine.  This reasonably priced watch fit my needs perfectly!

product_title: Fossil Men's FS4483 Sport Black Diamond-Accented Dial Watch
review_body: Product as described, arrived in 3 days! Was a gift for a friend and he loved it. Great dress watch!

product_title: Citizen Men's BL8000-03A Eco-Drive Calibre 8700 Sport Watch
review_body: i've had this watch for 6 years now, but with the stainless steel band. i've got to say it has kept perfect time and date and i can always depend on this watch. i've had other watches for looks and etc, but for perfect time keeping, especially while traveling, this is my go to watch. when i go to a different time zone and use the local time function, the date will automatically adjust which is really nice. i can just get off the plane, turn one dial and know exactly what time and date it is locally.     the thing's built like a tank. i've dropped it and taken falls with the watch. it has scratches but functionally it's been perfect. if not for the stupid daylight saving time i would have never needed to adjust time on this watch.     i still get a lot of people asking me about this watch, and i'm always glad to tell them how inexpensive it is and tell them to look into getting one.     a downside of the watch is i've been wanting a new watch, but this citizen just won't die and keeps going, so i can't justify buying a new watch =(

product_title: Akribos XXIV Men's AK406SS Bravura Davinci Mechanical Stainless Steel Watch with Black Leather Band
review_body: I described most of it in the pictures I uploaded, but I'm glad I took a leap of faith with this watch. It's awesome. I'm a college student, and I gotta say, if I had an excuse to dress up everyday, I would be wearing this watch. Everything is very simple and elegant. I have a Sturhling automatic (Stuhrling Original Men's 182.33161 Special Reserve 'Millenia' Skeleton Automatic Watch), and like the Akribos, it's awesome, but the internal parts a little obstructed by the brand name framed around the watch face. This watch not only does have a brand name on it (it's inscribed on the rim on the back of the watch and on the band clasp) it doesn't (obviously) even have numbers on its watch face. This allows you to really appreciate the internal workings of the watch. Literally everything is open for you to see (along with those around you). Because it's mechanical, it also isn't as thick as the automatic ones you can buy, and it also really adds a retro-oldschool style that everyone can appreciate.     Cons:  The major problem (as cited on multiple reviews) is that the watch appears to randomly stop and the only way to get it working again is to flick it or tip it or whatever. It also seems to stop exactly at 9:15 and 10 sec. This is because the hour hand is placed too low in the watch so it gets caught on the second hand. This was sooo disappointing. Don't they realize they could sell many more of these watches if they could just fix that ONE and only one problem? I managed to fix it so now it works just as well as my other watches, but it really is an unfortunate defect.     Regardless. It's a beautiful watch in every way. It's classy but not flashy, and everybody who's seen it has asked to look at it (\\"Oh wow, THAT WATCH IS SOOO COOL!\\"). I would recommend that people really look into this watch. Online pics and reviews can only get you so far, but I hope this review offers a little more substance for others to use.

product_title: Adidas Men's ADH2036 White Toronto Analog Watch
review_body: This watch is OK.  It is really thick, so if you couldnt tell, the watch is BIG.  Secondly, the material though comfortable doesnt stay white long.. it gets dirty VERY easily.

product_title: XOXO Women's XO114 White Enamel and Rhinestone Accent Bracelet Watch
review_body: I wanted an inexpensive watch that looked good and this watch was perfect. I saw on a few reviews that the clasp can be loose and indeed it was when I received my watch but I put a small piece of adhesive vinyl over where the clasp shuts to make it slightly thicker for the clasp to grip and that worked like a charm. I also had to remove a link to make it fit my wrist better.  The ring around the face does chip easily so be warned. I accidentally dropped the watch and a tiny bit of white paint chipped off but it's not too noticeable. I'll just have to be more careful  The day & date dials are just for decoration but I had read that on previous reviews and wasn't too bothered by it. Really for the price you can't expect all the bells and whistles!    All in all I am in love with this watch, it's so pretty and really shows off my summer tan!

review_body: It's a spiffy little watch for less than $24, with more modes and functions than you can shake a stick at!  What's not to like?

review_headline: Great looking watch! Perfect for any avid watch-wearer!
review_body:

Lumination had to last (tritium if possible).  Made to take hits, drops, mud, sand, water.  Screw down crown  Large enough face, so I can read easily.  Glass had to be scratch resistance (sapphire if possible).    Options  Date/day wheel if possible.  Stainless steel or Titanium (no plastic body).  NATO strap or equivalent.  Auto powered    After a couple months of research on AMAZON, watch type messageboards, it came down to the Traser Commander Titanium P6506    I have had it for a couple weeks and I have no complaints yet.  I have washed my car and truck, gone off-roading, did some yard work and it has gotten wet, hit the side of my truck, gotten dusty.  And so far no issues.  The tritium is bright enough to view at night with no straining.  It is not super bright that you may see in advertisements.    My only grip is the strap's end, it just hangs out there.  Looks unfinished...  With the NATO strap the end is stickup up over the bezel.  It is hardly long enough to tuck it back under one of the metal loops.  I have posted some pics so you will see what i mean.    Overall - I am very pleased with the purchase of this watch and expect to have it last for a very long long time. The metal clasp has quite a bit of adjustment in it...maybe Invicta wanted to make a watch for a number of different wrist sizes.  I also like my clasps to sit directly in the middle of my wrist and because of the odd links and where they were placed on this watch, my clasp sits slightly off center of my wrist.  This may be a bit paranoia, just my preference.  Weight of the watch is not much more than the larger of the Invicata series.  You probably won't notice this too much.  So if you like the larger watch faces and don't mind the extra effort in resizing, this is a good timepiece and I would recommend it.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNE095P2 Stainless Steel Watch
review_headline: Military style watch that's a WINNER!
review_body:
As I've been getting older, my eyesight has gotten worse and I'm too vain to wear my reading glasses all the time. So I've been looking for a watch that meet these requirements:

1. I wanted a military-style watch with a plain black face which had white numbers (no dots or dashes for the hours). I didn't want a \\"busy\\" face or one with a chronograph since I can't read the small dials of a chronograph anyway. It also had to have W-I-D-E minute and hour arms to be easily readable without my reading glasses.

2. I have a skinny wrist (7.5\\"). I found lots of military-style watches that I liked, but most of them were 44mm. The current trend is to go for large watches, but a 44mm watch looked like a wall clock on my my wrist. I needed a watch that was no bigger than 40mm.

3. I wanted a watch that was no thicker than 11mm which makes it easier to wear under a long sleeve shirt. I also found thick watches (like diving watches) are too heavy and I kept banging into things with them.

4. It had to be water resistant to 100M since I'm always around water. I also found watches that are water resistant to 100M are better built and more durable.

5. It could NOT be powered by a replaceable battery. From my experience, the battery always fails when you're in a remote area without access to a new battery or the means to replace it. My ideal watch had to be an automatic or solar powered.

6 The watch had to less than US$150.

It took me awhile to find a watch that met all my requirements, but it was the Seiko SNE095P2 solar powered quartz watch. It might be too plain for most guys, especially the younger ones, but it met all my needs.

One of the first watches that I ever had was a Seiko when I was 10 years old so it felt good to get back to one after 45 years. I also felt confident that the Seiko quality wouldn't fail me. I almost considered a similar Citizen Eco-Drive Watch, but Seiko has been making solar watches for almost as long as Citizen. In a side-by-side comparison, I liked the look of the Seiko over the Citizen.

I did replace the green canvas band with a Zulu one-piece \\"James Bond\\" nylon watch band which I find much better looking and more comfortable to wear. If you decide to replace it with a Zulu watch band, be sure to get an original and not a knock-off from China. If you want more \\"bling\\", you could replace it with a metal bracelet, but I find metal bracelets too heavy.

Overall, I'm very pleased with my watch. It's very readable without me having to use my reading glasses although I can't read the weekday and day function. The minute and hour hands and the 12, 6, and 9 hours are luminescent after exposure to light for a couple of hours. It's also very accurate. After a couple of weeks, I haven't notice any loss or gain in time.

If you need a military-style watch and you have the same requirements that I have, I highly recommend that you consider this watch.

product_title: Invicta Men's 6035 Pro Diver Collection Automatic Stainless Steel Watch
review_headline: Screw Down Crown? I am not sure if it is or not...
review_body: Firstly, this watch was $[...] shipped so I can not complain about the price. I did, however, expect some higher product quality because the watch is supposedly for diving and is rated at 200 Meters. Here is the problem...I gave my 4 year old a bath and the next day my watch is all steamed up and it wont keep time. It is 15 minutes fast almost every hour and I realized that it is actually 10 days off since I bought it 60 days ago so I still wonder when did this problem really start bath time or factory? I didn't wear it in the first 45 days of ownership and it was off 10 days when I opened the box.    Here is another problem... I let it sit in the box until I had time to get the band sized and by the time I got it sized the warranty registration period was over. If you buy this watch, get it registered fast because if you don't in the first 30 days, they will not warranty the watch. Period. Unfortunately, now I have to throw mine away because the repairs are going to be more than the watch is worth.    Also, if you read the instructions, you will find that the crown is a \\"screw down crown\\" and that you will void your warranty if you pull the crown and set your watch. I expect a watch maker to send a watch with the time and date correct...don't you? This watch arrived way off time and date so I set it immediately without reading the instructions. I am a man after all and I do not need those stupid things, right? Now, I have never had a watch requiring a screw down crown and naively set my watch to the proper date and time and supposedly stripped the threads on the \\"screw down\\" crown. I never felt any resistance when I pulled the crown so I am not sure if it even is screw down but anyway the warranty that I should have registered for would be voided now anyhow.    Unfortunately, I am screwed either way you can lose in this scenario...I didn't register until 60 days and I set the date and time and voided the warranty.     Bottom line: This whole situation stinks. Invicta should make a better watch so the crown threads don't strip. If they did the proud new owner would be forced to read the directions and there would be no need to use the warranty. The fact that   Invicta is blaming me for destroying this watch and voiding my warranty tells you what kind of people we are dealing with...I will take this as a lesson learned and I will buy another brand next time.

product_title: Hamilton Men's H64515333 Khaki King Pilot Black Day Date Dial Watch
review_body: This is an incredible piece by Hamilton. Fully automatic, with a Day/Date complication, the watch is a chunky, masculine model with quite a lot to recommend it. The case is a little tank of solid stainless steel, with a screwed in display back through which you can observe the mostly undecorated, but still impressive movement. The rotor however is engraved with the word Hamilton and the jewel count. The crown is screw down, and given proper protection by the crown gaurds. The Day display is beautiful; a perfect balance between the size of lettering and the open window. Far less successful is the Date display, with perhaps too small a window located at six o'clock, but the overall look of the Day at the 12 position and the Date at the 6 position gives the dial a touch of class. Best of all, the lettering is white on a black background! The Dial itself is a little busy, with rather large arabic numerals at 9 and 3 o'clock, but this is a matter of taste. On the wrist, the dial stands out. The bezel is sturdy and well made, with adequate grip for turning and firm enough, though I have turned more buttery bezels. Water resistance is only 100M but seriously, how many people are really going to take their automatic diving watch past the shore at the beach or the \\"big boy\\" end of the pool? Frankly, this is not a major issue. With a stainless steel bracelet, the watch has a litte heft on the wrist but isn't oppressive. With this black rubber strap with contrast stitching, it's nearly unnoticeable; be careful though if you wear the watch close to the end of the wrist - the case is hard and has some sharp edges. The movement is unexpectedly very accurate at this price point, four to five seconds fast per week - that's within COSC specifications.    The only MAJOR problem with this watch is the lack of superluminova, except on the hands, which is totally inadequate. Hamilton seems not to care too much about lume. This might have been a perfect piece though, if only instead of arabic numerals, Hamilton had used other markers to accomodate more lume. Even a desk diver needs some glow.     Overall, this watch is fantastic value for money. Just fantastic, and really beautiful on the wrist. You will feel like you paid quite a lot more for it than you did. Highly recommended.

product_title: Timex Ironman 100-Lap Watch
review_headline: excellent watch, cant go wrong with this one
review_body: I bought the all black version of this watch, model T5J992. There is no difference aside from color between the watches, hence my review is applicable to this product too.    It's difficult to find a watch that meets all my criteria. This holds true of this watch. I wanted a watch under $50 - check; resin strap - check; large digits - check; easy to use - check; and scratch resistant face - not so much. So the watch is great at meeting most of my criteria, but I was disappointed at how easily the display window can scratch. I believe the display material is acrylic plastic. I noticed a fine scratch that shows up on close inspection after only a week. While the display window is protected a bit by being recessed, I can only imagine more scratches as time goes by.    The other annoying thing about this watch is the delay when entering any one of the modes such as Chrono, Alarm, Interval, or Timer. The watch takes about one second to get ready. So during this time, the watch only shows what mode you are entering with a blank display. What this means is that you can't immediately start your chrono timer beacuse of the delay. One second delay may seem short to some people, but I expect the mode to be instantly ready to use.    Aside from those weaknesses, the watch is really nice. It's very well designed with nice placement of buttons, small lettering, and highly legible display. I think this is one of the most attractive and elegant looking Ironman watches I've seen. The material quality aside from the plastic display window is relatively good. I like the fact that the display is recessed and protected by a hardened rubbery crown. This gives the watch decent protection against accidental bumps. Also the rubbery ridge is raised at the sides to protect the buttons from incidental contact. Fit and finish cannot be faulted for a watch in this price range. In other words it feels like a quality watch that is built to last and withstand daily wear and tear.    I like the allblack color scheme of this model. It makes it stand out less, and so can be used for many different daily activities or settings. The strap is comfortable and has the right amount of flexibility and thickness. The Flix feature is nice to have, although I generally don't activate it since I prefer to just press the Indiglo button. There is a night mode which allows the Indiglo display to light when pressing any button. This is useful when one wants to use various modes in the dark. To activate either Flix or night mode, one just needs to hold down the Indiglo button for three seconds. As for the readability of the Indiglo I like that it's bright and only lights the digits, not the entire watch face. This looks cooler and stylish to me than the older version of Indiglo.    I find that this watch has all the functions I need on a regular basis, and nothing I don't want. I love the ability to set five different alarms that you can program to go off daily, on certain days of the week, or weekends. Neat! I find that the volume of the alarm is adequate to wake me up in the morning. The chronograph holds 100 laps which is more than I will ever likely need. You are able to store multiple workouts until the memory is full. When recalling the workouts, it's simple to cycle through the laps, and the watch even calculates the best lap and average lap time for you.    One thing I find immensely useful with this watch is the onscreen instructions and clever user interface. You really don't need instructions.. in fact I just toss mine after reading it through once. The interface has words on the display next to the buttons to remind you which buttons you should press. The text blinks to remind you of the mode you are in. You can use the Stop or Start/Split button to cycle up or down, for example when setting up the time or when recalling laps in your workout.    Overall I am very pleased with this Timex Ironman 100 Lap Flix watch. I would buy it again, even considering the few weaknesses I mentioned.

review_body: Bought this watch 11 months ago. Up until about a month ago I have enjoyed this watch more than most watches I have owned. The only problem I had up to that time was a dislike of the watch band. It has one retaining loop to hold the band in place and frequently it will slide off and then the band is loose and sticks out.   The upside to this watch is that the time is always spot on correct. I work on an hourly schedule and must know the correct time. With this watch that was always possible.  My complaint and why I rate this watch with a 2 stars is that about a month ago or after 10 months of use water began to show up on the underside of the glass face. Since it was under warranty I mailed it back to CASIO 1st class for less than a $1.50. A few days ago I was informed that the watch would not be repaired under warranty and that they wanted $15.00 for repairs, about $6.00 for shipping and some sales tax as well. In the end they wanted more money to repair an under warranty watch then I originally paid for the watch 11 months ago at Amazon.    At this point I consider CASIO warranty to be worth little if anything. I will replace this watch but not with a CASIO.  If your going to wear a CASIO almost every day and subject it to constant use beware of the potential for a warranty that will not be honored.    http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001A5LKAS/ref=cm_cr_rev_prod_title

I've wanted a Monaco for some time, and was always torn between this model and the classic \\"Steve McQueen\\" blue  model with the two chronograph dials and crown at 9 o'clock (this is a traditional chrono with 3 inset dials and crown at 3 o'clock), and ultimately this one won out for that very reason.    I will warn about the unisex label of this watch in that this is a fairly large piece, and even men with small wrists might not find it comfortable to wear.    If you like the classic Monaco style and want a watch that matches a suit and tie as well as jeans and a leather jacket you could do a lot worse than this. product_title: Invicta Men's 1461 Vintage Collection Riveted Leather Strap Brown Dial Watch
review_body: Likes:      The watch band was very soft, didn't chafe against skin, and was flexible (not stiff) making this watch feel comfortable enough to wear for a long period of time.  The size and weight of the watch and face was fine; it didn't feel too heavy on the wrist.  It looks nice and being water proof is a big plus.  It is nice enough to wear with your suit, but not too fancy for jeans and a polo.  The band is well-made, well-stitched solid leather.  The box it came in was also very nice and I mention it only because the presentation of the watch in its box just echoed the quality of the product itself.    Also a plus is the two-stage time adjustment.  Pulling out the adjuster one click changes the date; two clicks changes the time. A lot of watches have this, but having another watch that doesn't makes this a good feature to my husband. Note that the watch changes the date when you've passed 12 twice, so be sure to change the date right after an automatic roll over or you risk being off half a day.    Dislikes:    The numbers are very big. It would be great for someone who is visually impaired. This is a style issue (maybe that's just not my husband's style) and will not be a negative for everyone.    It has no light, which is a con because you can't tell what time it is, except during the day or in good light.  So wearing the watch to a presentation given in the dark means you can't read your watch to know what time it is. This is a bigger issue than number size, because this makes the watch non-functional in certain circumstances.

review_body:
I have had many watches over my 77 year life Including watches that cost almost $4000. I am a former military pilot and even today I like accuracy in a watch. Wish there were watches like this during my 20 years in the Air Force.

In a word the watch is suburb for my use. I like the heft, the large numbers and the lighted dial. At first I did not think I would like the metal holes on the watch band. After some use, I think they are great and the band is a great band. I would not think of changing it. I do not have big arms or hands and the watch still looks good and is so easy to read. I set the watch by the atomic watch in Denver so I can with confidence say it keeps excellent time. This watch would be to large for most ladies unless you are the outdoor, rock climbing type of lady. It has the heft of a Rolex Navigator and is similar in size but keeps better time and you never have to wind it or put a battery in it. The second hand also stops when you pull out the crown so you can set the watch to the second if you are that time conscious. The crown does have to be wound backwards before you can pull up the crown to set the time. A good feature.

I did a lot of research before I purchased this watch. Money was no factor. I wanted certain things such as an analog face with day only. I also wanted a black strap and a black face. I originally was searching for a watch that updated itself with the atomic watch in Denver. I was not familiar with the Eco-Drive. After reading about it I decided I had found the exact watch I wanted at an excellent price. I rate this watch Five Stars. If you are looking for a dressy watch you may want to change band to a solid black leather band and it would look as good as my former Rolex, in my opinion. For most people you will not go wrong when you purchase this watch. I have always been big into computers, electronics, watches and even at my age am still into these things.

product_title: Seiko Men's SUN011 Velatura Kinetic GMT Blue Dial Stainless Steel Watch
review_body: I have been wearing this watch for a couple weeks now and am entirely satisfied with my choice.  I upgraded from a similar Seiko Series 5 after dealing with an issue with capacitor leakage common in the earlier Kinetic watches.  These issues have now been resolved through Seiko.  The self charging nature of the Seiko Kinetics is a very nice feature since there are no batteries to change -- ever.  Straight out the box, the watch already held about 1 month of charge (movement during shipping I suppose) and after a week of normal use (8+ hours a day) the watch is be good for a full six months if I was to set it aside.    The watch is solid and therefore heavy and may seem awkward to someone moving up from a smaller watch.  My previous Seiko had a 39mm bezel and there was a noticeable difference in weight and bulk between the two.  That said, this watch does not interfere with daily tasks unless you have to stick your arm into a tight space.  The latching mechanism is actually slimmer than on my Series 5, but feels much more solid in the catch.  Settings are simple and straight forward even if you have never had a watch with a GMT feature.  The included manual will answer any questions that may arise in six different languages.  And yea, the watch looks even better on your wrist than it does in the picture.    The only step that you will have to take on your own is having the watch sized.  I didn't do this work myself, but the local shop that I took it on was more than happy to show me the tiny screws and rods that hold the band together.  The shop carries higher end lines of Seikos (no spring drives in stock yet), but mentioned that this was one of the more difficult they had to work with.  That's not a bad thing if you want your band to stay intact over the years, but can add a few extra minutes to the resizing process.

product_title: Timex Men's T49201 Expedition E-Compass Titanium Leather Watch
review_body: I bought this watch for my own birthday present. It has worked out well and I'm very pleased. I wanted a compass with me all the time. I wouldn't rely on it for a long expedition, but it has proved more consistent than I expected. It is more affected by external metallic sources than my Silva compass, so you need to step away from buildings with rebar and cars before checking a reading.     My main complaint is that the contrast between the hands and the face is not strong enough. It has taken me a while to get used to distinguishing between the hands and the markings on the face. It usually takes more than a quick glance. This isn't a problem with the back light, which works fine.     No problems with the water resistance, and the strap has held up well to repeated dunkings while canoeing.    Overall, I'm very pleased.

product_title: Pere de Temps Men's 3027 Debut Patton Automatic Mechanical WatchStainless Steel with Exhibition Dial
review_body: This watch looks every bit as elegant as watches costing 5 times the price. The precision movement that this watch attempts to emulate is very close, but not quite up to par with more expensive watches. That is probably to be expected at this price point, as you're buying a watch that \\"looks\\" like a much more expensive timepiece. In addition, in spite of an automatic watch winder, this watch loses 2-6 minutes of time per day. Finally, the construction of the watch feels heavy and substantial; it has a large face, and the band is heavily padded. I have had mine for 7 months, and it has yet to \\"break-in\\" to my wrist. On the contrary, the fob loop has already broken, and cannot be repaired.    Unfortunately, this watch falls into timepiece purgatory:    If you want to purchase a large, heavy timepiece that looks like a much more expensive watch (from 3 feet away), then this would be one way to do that. You could, however, purchase the same concept for 1/5th of the price.    If you're looking for a well-crafted, long-lasting watch that your next generation will fight over, then you should definitely spend the extra money and buy a proven, reliable timepiece from a reputable dealer who is well versed in the nuances of great watchmakers.

review_body: [[VIDEOID:moZ47B5F7QULMY]]The most important function of a watch is time-telling, and this watch's mechanical functions are defective. review_body: Like others reviewing this item, I too am struck by the sheer beauty of this watch, so much so that I was tempted to keep it, even after discovering that the workmanship is extremely below par,. I just wanted to keep it! But at almost $200.00, common sense won out & I returned it. The Bezel would turn only under extreme pressure and would seize-up midway through the rotation... it should rotate only 1 direction but would rotate in either direction. The screw-downs didn't and I realized that the one controlling the month was placed too close to the lugs to turn. After comparing the photo to other photos from different sellers it became obvious that the batch being sold for 171.00 is defective. This was determined by noticing the placement of the push-button top left to the photo offered from HSN... you'll see the defect.. But I really love the design, so I will reorder from the alternate site listed on Amazon's item description and hope I get a good one.

product_title: 18mm MODENA Flat Italian Rubber Watch Band w/ Deployant / Deployment Buckle / Clasp
review_headline: The best band for the buck...
review_body: I've been an avid watch collector for the past 15 years, so I've experienced with every type of band and strap available.  I dislike leather and other \\"natural\\" bands - besides being ridiculously expensive $150 - $500 range...(come on, for a watch band???) they collect sweat like there's no tomorrow. Nasty, icky situation after you take the watch off - and they do smell! Now, I don't go and work out with my watches, I'm talking about regular wear, in \\"regular\\" weather (continental Europe, mid-West US) and after a year or two of wearing it.  Metal bands, sometimes they cause a bit of a rash (maybe is cheap construction laced with chemicals?! I do not know!)  So, rubber was the natural selection for me.  Super comfortable to wear, the clasp adds a touch of sophistication to it.  It is a snap to replace the original bands with this 18mm MODENA Flat Italian Rubber Watch Band, if you have the proper tools you can do it at home yourself in less than 2 minutes!  I replace the original band on my Baume & Mercier Capeland GMT Reveil - Today it was the 1st time I wore it (with the new band) people were asking me about the watch (& the band!) - Highly recommended!

Pull the metal knob at the end of the strap down with your thumb to retract the pins.  Place the strap into the watch end AT A RIGHT ANGLE (in other words, from the top not the side)  Release the metal knob.  The pins will snap into place.  This works much more easily than trying to push the strap in from the side.
