product_title: Timex Men's Watch T5E261
review_headline: Finally I can read the time!
review_body: I had a cheapo digital watch and although it always worked well, my eyes are getting worse with age, so I was having trouble reading the time, especially in lower light conditions. When I started shopping for watches, I was looking for something that had large digits and also that I could use as a stopwatch for my workouts. I figured if it was easy to read the time on a page full of watch pictures, that would be the one and this one caught my eye immediately. This is a very nice watch. The band is very comfortable and the digits are easy to read. It was also easy to figure out how to set the time even without the directions, which I read later. The only drawback seems to be the little bump of vinyl at the end of the strap where it goes thru the clasp. It's pretty tight getting it thru there, so it makes it a little more difficult to put it on in a hurry. That may where in with time. It may also be a safety catch should you accidentally pull open the velcro strap so you don't lose the watch. I don't think you'll be able to replace the band, also. It seems to be sewn into the watch body. I like the Flix feature. You have to activate it each day (for night time use) as it will turn off after 8 hours so you're not turning it on during the day I guess and wasting your battery. Just a quick flick of the wrist will illuminate the watch. It's hard to read, though, unless it's dark out or there isn't enough contrast. Looks like a great watch all in all.    Oh, and someone mentioned that they didn't like the little nub  or whatever at the end of the watch band that makes it hard to pass thru the band loop, but I figured out that when you take your watch off, if you just open it up to where it touches that bump, you can slide it off your wrist without passing it thru the loop. This makes it easier to put on the next time. Must be a little fail-safe if you happened to bump the velcro and loosen it while you're under water or something it won't come off your wrist and get lost.Another good point!

review_headline: Can't WAIT to show this baby OFF!!!!
review_body:
Well, I was not home when this watch arrived and my husband who had purchased it for me for x-mas was NOT saying good things to me over the phone. I was worried all the while I was out x-mas shopping!
He said the innitial presentation was HORRIBLE, the yellow box that it came in was FILTHY and he cleaned it right away with a disposable wipe.
Thank GOODNESS he called me back about an hour later and said that the watch had been steamed up from coming into the warm out of the cold and that things were looking UP.
When I got home they looked UP even MORE!!!!!! I think this watch is a GREAT VALUE for $100 bucks and a good amount of \\"bang for your buck!\\"
If you are looking for large diamonds in the bezel then this is NOT FOR YOU. If you want to stretch you $'s and rely on the way the diamonds are set for your bling factor then you'll be A-OK. The case is thick but I find that it lends itself to the look of a high end watch. I'm starting to collect watches and this is my 1st piece that was not purchased on a whim and was not something along the lines of Fossil or Kenneth Cole.
If you are starting to collect and want to take the 1st step into higher end watches I recommend this. I also recommend it if you already have a nice collection of higher end time pieces and want something for everyday use as you \\"beater\\" watch.
All in all I hope this starts me off on my way to bigger and better Invicta's, Bulova's and maybe even a Rolex for my 40th?!
My girlfriends will envy me, and if I saw this on one of their wrist's I'd assume it cost a good bit over $100. I'm still proud to say that one of my x-mas gifts from hubby was an Invicta diamond chrono watch.

I also found a jeweler that will remove links for $10 bucks. I have larger hands and wrists for a woman and will need atleast 2 links removed. Don't tell yourself you have large wrists and won't have to have links removed becauase you WILL.

My ding from 5 stars down to 4 was really about the care Amazon took in packaging this piece. The watch for the money in my opinion os 5 STARS!!!ging this piece. The watch for the money in my opinion os 5 STARS!!!

product_title: Citizen Men's BL5250-02L Titanium Eco-Drive Watch with Leather Band
review_body: I've been lusting after this watch for about a month and finally bought it - I couldn't be happier. I've read most of the reviews and will attempt not to repeat those in detail. So, here's my observations:  1) I wanted a watch with a brown leather band with a \\"rugged look\\" without being clunky. I saw this and thought it would work, but was a bit put off by the pictures on Amazon's site. When I finally got the watch, I was very pleasantly surprised that the actual watch looked much better in real life than the pictures on the site. Some reviewers say the watch and/or band was \\"shiny\\" and not to their liking. I find the leather band looks rich and the \\"chrome\\" look on the bezel enhanced the looks since it was much less \\"silvery\\" looking than a brushed silver finish would be. Amazing how tastes vary amongst people.  2)  I've made a kind of pact with myself that since I'm a \\"watch person\\" with over 20 in my collection, that I would no longer buy watches that require batteries, and would also strive to buy watches with a wireless timekeeping connection. Okay, so this watch doesn't have the wireless timekeeping connection, but it is solar powered. A big plus.  3) The perpetual calendar is great.  4) The watch (for the week that I've had it) is keeping time within seconds of the atomic clock in Boulder.  5) I like the tachymeter function for the few times I want to calibrate my car's speedometer and for those other times when I'm surreptitiously measuring manufacturing times in factories I visit in Asia.  Having said all that, there are a few nits:  1) The alarm is REALLY non-existent. Okay, I'm an older guy, but I can't really hear the alarm unless I'm specifically listening to it. And, it's a bear to set. Seiko owns the market on loud wrist watch alarms and also on luminous hands, numerals, etc.  2) The stop watch function is really rudimentary. Having to pull out the crown and rotate it to change to the stop watch mode is really cumbersome. Once you pull out the crown,rotate it, push it back in, and push the start/stop button you've probably missed what you wanted to time. And then, you only have a start-stop function - no lap function. And, to reset the stop watch, a long push on the start/stop button does it - totally counter-intuitive since normally if the top right button starts & stops the timing, the bottom right button resets it.  BOTTOM LINE: I like the watch for what I bought it for - it's probably one of the better looking watches I own - I would buy it again and recommend it to a friend.

product_title: Timex Men's Easy Reader Day-Date Expansion Band Watch
review_headline: It's OK if you have a small wrist
review_body: I had purchased a T20461 from Walmart for my uncle recently and I liked it so well, that I decided to buy the T20031 and T20471 for myself from Amazon.  These are supposed to be the same watch with the same style expansion band; the only difference is the color of the metal and/or dial face.  The fit of the T20461 was perfect for my wrist, and required no adjustment.  However, the fit of the T20031 and T20471 was much tighter and not all that comfortable.  I decided to count the links in the watches, and found that the T20461 from Walmart comes with 2 more links than the T20031 and T20471 from Amazon.  It seems that the bean counters at Timex have figured they can shave a few pennies from the cost by reducing the number of links in their watch bands.  I did notice that the packaging and plastic holder of the watch from Walmart is different than that from Amazon.  Obviously, the watches are from different manufacturing batches.  Whether the Amazon series is older or newer than the Walmart series is a mystery.  However, I can vouch for the fact that the Amazon series being delivered at this time are shy two links in the band.  So unless you have small, girly wrists, you might want to pass on this series of expansion wrist watches.  Other than this issue, the T20031 is a pretty nice watch.

review_headline: Stuhrling watches are Chinese and made in Hong Kong
review_body:
There is a great deal of confusion among buyers and potential buyers about Stuhrling watches and a bevy of similar brands. Considering that the descriptions for these watches go on and on about their Swiss heritage, it's quite understandable that so many people are confused.

Here's the skinny:

The Stuhrling brand is just one of dozens of so called watch brands that are either made in China or Hong Kong. These companies are very secretive about where their watches are actually made, but this one seems to be made in Hong Kong. I can also name: Rousseau, Louis Bolle and Parnis. There are many more types of Chinese watches with Swiss sounding names.

You must have noticed that ad copy -

\\"With dedication to the heritage of Swiss watchmaking...\\"

Yada yada.

So if you like the watch and it's worth $140 to you, okay. But please don't let yourself be misled. A company that sells watches in the $2,000 to $5,000 range is not going to suddenly slash their prices by 90 percent.

The technology for making mechanical watches goes all the way back to John Harrison, the inventor of the first sea clock. John finished his famous H4 watch in 1761. I know copyrights for songs expire after 75 years. I don't know the limit for watches, but I've never read about one watch company suing another for copyright infringement, and the copyrights can't go back all that far. Compared to modern watches, mechanical watches use fairly simple technology with gears and a spring. But if an accurate watch was your highest concern, you would buy a quartz watch with a battery or a digital watch.

Even the companies that make the very expensive watches use the same or very similar features. For example, the power reserve indicator (It shows how many hours worth of energy the main spring has stored.) is common on many watches, expensive ones and more affordable watches.

And just look at the name! Sturhling, I could tell just from the name that it's Chinese. (I studied Mandarin Chinese for 4 semesters and I've known many Chinese friends. So I've gotten used to their culture.) I have a hard drive case that reads - Metal Gear Box - on the side. Just from that, I could tell some Chinese person thought of the name. Open commerce has only been in China since the mid 1980s. Chinese people write names and advertising copy that seem sophisticated to them, but look sophomoric to most Americans.

But I object to:

1 - They're misleading you by pretending that Stuhrling is a Swiss watch company. I suggest you compare Stuhrling watches with Steinhausen watches. And honestly, if this were a Swiss watch company, it would be spelled Sterling, as in pound sterling or sterling silver. (Sterling comes from the old English word storling, which meant star, and by virtue of stars on the old English silver pennies, it came to mean quality.) If you're even a little familiar with Chinese culture, this is not that tough to sort out, folks.

2 - You can find Chinese copies of any more expensive brand and many particular watches. The Chinese government makes no effort to stop that.

On the other hand, I read an article that said the cheap copies probably help the genuine brand. Ironic, don't you think? That's because the cheap copies increase interest in the genuine watches. When people can afford to buy the real thing, they do.

That's from an article I read about cheap copies of expensive watches. It's just something to add to the discussion and the article did not include any figures so I wouldn't give it too much weight.

product_title: Casio Men's G7700-1 G-Shock Trainer Multi-Function Shock Resistant Watch
review_headline: Move over Ironman, Casio's got a trainer too!
review_body:
I'd been looking for a watch that would give me functions like the Timex Ironman series of chronographs, but with the toughness and superior build quality of a Casio G-Shock. Problem is, there aren't too many G Shocks that have functions that are suited for this. Sure, most have chronographs and timers but they are basic.

Enter the G7700 (and the sister G7710 with negative display and gold trim). This is a very unusual G Shock. It boasts 29 world time zones, a dual time mode, four alarms, two countdown timers that run intervals with each other (perfect for interval training), and a stopwatch accurate to 1/1000th of a second with 99 laps.

The interval timers are terrific and will repeat up to 5 times (though I wish you could set them for more). This makes it perfect for interval training. When one finishes, the alarm will go off, the other will start, and red and green LED's will flash alternately for ten seconds. This is invaluable for me. While the alarm isn't that loud, the LED's are bright when flashing (I run at night usually) so I can tell when the next one is starting even while listening to music through earphones.

The stopwatch also has a unique feature, a \\"countdown\\" till start, where the display will animate a 5...4...3...2...1...Start type countdown, with the LED's going from Red to Green at the start, sort of like race track christmas tree lights. Cool beans. I'll never use that part of the stopwatch but it's still cool.

The display is unusual in that the main Home time can display the year, or days past in the year with how many left to go, as well as day and week number. I like this feature. The watch has three 'lines' of display with the top two noticeably smaller. If I had one complaint, it would be that these two top smaller displays are slightly harder to glance at while running, but this is minor.

Backlight is standard bluish-green on the face, however the backlight time isn't adjustable. It lasts about 1.5 secs and will not stay on if you keep the \\"G\\" light button pressed. Display contrast is adjustable which is something I've not noticed on many G's. This Casio module is impressive. Hopefully they use this more often, rather than keep on cranking out the same old modules in different cases each year.and will not stay on if you keep the \\"G\\" light button pressed. We warrant the good working of this watch but must lay down that the damage caused by unsuitable treatment must not blame the watch. Excluded from this guarantee are: rupture of axe, glass, broken spring and damage caused by water...\\"   This is what I expect from a Chinese watch made several years ago, not the Swiss , many of whom, speak excellent English. Makes me wonder if this brand has been out-sourced.

product_title: Orient #CEM60002W Men's Duty Day/Date 50M Self Winding Automatic Watch
review_headline: Beautiful watch, outstanding quality, great vendor!
review_body: I purchased this because my Invicta sub was starting to take a beating and I wanted another automatic to put in rotation.  I was pricing Seiko's for two weeks and just couldn't decide on a model.  I wanted something with a silver or white face.  I was aware of Orients reputation as a great quality automatic watch and I was especially impressed that they still use their own in-house movement design.  I happened upon this watch accidentally and fell in love with it's appearance.  The silver and black face were equally handsome but the silver face was the one for me.  The vendor shipped from California and I had it on the east coast in 3 days AND I was ordering over the weekend.  Big kudos to Just Calculators for fantastic standard shipping.  The watch was brand new and flawless.  I took it out of the box, shook it gently to get the movement going, set the day/date/time and away we went.  The links on this bracelet have a unique design that was much easier to size myself than the standard pin type arrangement on most cheaper watches.  Bottom line, this is a beautiful automatic watch that is a STEAL for 60 bucks.  Quality wise, it beats my Invicta 8926 OB hands down.  The bracelet was flawless, the crystal was so clear as to be invisible (my Invicta actually looks stained in direct sunlight) and it keeps damn good time.  So far it hasn't lost a second.  I have it set to my computer and it's dead nuts after 48 hours.    It's a keeper and I'm seriously thinking about replacing my Invicta with the Orient Sub.

review_body: My fiance and I were in the Mall of Asia (Manila) and as usual I stopped by the store here that sells Omega, Rolex and other fine timepieces. NO MORE KINETIC drives for me as they stop after not being worn for a short time! I am estatic about the purchase and had never really considered Citizen seriously before. product_title: G-Shock GA100A-7A Classic Series Designer Watches - White
review_headline: Best looking watch I've ever owned.
review_body: After a lifetime of black or metal scuba and combat style watches I decided to give this model a try.    This is hands down the nicest looking watch I've ever owned, very classy.    First time I wore it to the gym, I could tell it was noticed and it's been complemented several times during day wear.    I was worried that white would look girlish... this thing looks as girlish as an M1 Abrams battle tank camouflaged white for the winter snow.    The blue numbering and hands look great on the white background and are soothing on the eyes.    The wide double-holed band adds to it's muscularity.    I'm a big guy with a large wrist and am only two notches to the end of the strap, so if you have a monster wrist you may be disappointed.    On the other hand, my petite girlfriend tried it on an it looked amazing on her and the band was could be adjusted to fit her her perfectly, so I'm ordering one for her also.     I've also got white skin since I'm not a big fan of sun exposure and it still stands out, if you have a darker complexion this watch will really pop.    And for such a big watch, it's very light.    One note of caution, for what I've read long sleeve darkly dyed cotton shirts will stain this watch as well as if you rub it against blue jeans.    The finish is glossy, not matte so normal dirt wipes right off.    The time keeping is very accurate and the other functions like stopwatch, alarm and countdown time, etc. are a bonus.    I've owned several of Casio watches and have never had one that wasn't accurate.    As a gift or for yourself even if you're a girl this watch will not disappoint.

product_title: Invicta Women's 5377 Angel Diamond-Accented Stainless Steel Watch
review_body: Being a watch addict and having many 'fancy' and 'high-end' watches, this watch is by far my favorite watch!!! At first, I was skeptical because the other customer pictures make it look so huge on their wrists...but it doesn't look as huge on me, and my wrist isnt large, or small. They must have tiny wrists.     It is super versatile, I wear it to work in the professional setting, out for a night on the town, and embarrasingly Ive worn it to the gym to work out. But it looks wonderful in any setting...and its also durable in these settings too. I always made sure my watches were water resistant when I was younger because I NEVER took it off, but as I got older, and started purchasing more expensive watches, I realized I should do more to take care of them, unfortunately I sometimes still forget to remove the watch when bathing and/or washing dishes...which is OK!! Ive never had any issue with water getting into the face, or damaging it in any way. Invicta is famous for their diving watches, so I wouldnt expect anything less from them. The face must be a mineral glass, and not quartz because it resists scratching of everyday use. Although with mineral glass, if it does get scratched, or cracked it has to be sent to the manufacturer to be fixed (I had a mishap with a Dolce watch, it dropped on the concrete and severely shattered the mineral crystal, yet the face crystal remained intact, sort of like a busted window that isnt broken to peices. You dont have to be extra careful because this watch is VERY durable, just know it takes a lot to damage it, and if you do, it has to be sent off to fix.     The hands and time markers also glow in the dark, which is awesome if lighting is low and you need to see the time. The square style is not very traditional and it makes this watch very fashionable (I purchased the round faced one, and its much smaller and not as fashionable, It looks like a regular, boring watch compared to this one).     The diamonds are microscopic, and really do not add 'bling' if that is what you are looking for.     This would be a wonderful gift for a woman who's looking for an larger, durable, versatile, elegant, yet up to date styled watch without a lot of glitz. Definitely an A++++ in my opinion.

review_body:
The T-Touch has been in my must have list of watches for years now. I finally pulled the trigger and bought one for myself and I must say it is an excellent watch. Definitely a must have for any watch collector.

The first time I took it out of the box it had that ho-hum effect on me. This is because I am not really a big fan of titanium watches. I just find the dark dull color of titanium doesn't have that wow factor compared to shiny stainless. But with the thickness and the size of this watch it makes sense to go with titanium. The diameter at 43mm is not so large but I was surprised on how thick this watch is. This is something to look out for, you may not be able to wear this under your dress shirt sleeve without having to pull the sleeve over it everytime you look at the time. Anyhow like I said unboxing it was a bit anti-climactic for me. However once I got to use the features I was completely wowed. I own my fair share of Pathfinders and GShocks and none of them can compare to the looks of this watch. It's truly amazing that at this price point how they can fit all that stuff and make it an ana-digi watch at the same time. I am very happy with this purchase. The only con I can say about the watch is the lack of solar power or rechargeable power. I think that if they made the carbon dial into a solar panel or make the batter rechargeable like those MTM watches it would be awesome. But other than it's a great timepiece. It does so much more than my other so much more expensive watches.

If you're a techie or watch collector or both you gotta have this.

product_title: Timex Women's T5K175 Ironman Traditional 10-Lap Blue Resin Strap Watch
review_body: I bought this particular model for my daughter, who borrowed my full size mens Ironman once and fell in love with it. This one is a little more compact, a plus for either gender I think. It also has a slightly less fashionable band than the regular Ironman Womans model, making it cheaper. (There are so many models bearing the \\"Ironman\\" moniker  that \\"regular\\" is probably meaningless. Wish I could be more helpful, but it would seem that overwhelming us with choices is part of Timex's marketing strategy.) Since she's in the habit of loosing watches I didn't want to pay more than I had to, and this model gave us the functionality we both love at a reduced price.    I'm a long time runner and probably a little more obsessed than some with timing my runs. I like the latest Ironman functionality better than previous watches (various Casios including G-shock, Timex Expedition, Older Ironmans). I particularly like the button layout (start/lap button easy to hit, stop and indiglo buttons hard to hit accidentally, accidental resets virtually impossible) and I've gotten so used to using my 50-lap chrono to track my split times that I hate being without it. This ones says 100-lap in the description, but my daughters says \\"10-lap\\" on the watch itself (look closely at the picture and you can see this). I tested and it actually remembers 30 laps (go figure). The big difference, however, as that while I can record multiple workouts on mine, with the date of each, hers only remembers the last workout, and once you reset the chrono your data is gone forever. Personally I would hate that. This watch also lacks the Dual interval timer that I use for reminding me when to \\"eat\\" (gels) on long runs, and has only one alarm. Mine has three.

product_title: Uzi Men's Uzi-001-N The Protector Tritium H3 Black Nylon Strap Watch
review_headline: Flimsy piece of rubbish- don't waste your time!
review_body:
I'll keep the review brief because there isn't a whole lot that needs to be said about this watch. Just do yourself a favor and do NOT buy one!

At first glance it looks like an OK buy for the modest price being asked with its supposedly \\"rugged\\" construction, Tritium lume, 200m water resistance, screw down crown, Swiss quartz movement etc. but beware, this watch is a piece of junk.

I've had TWO of these watches and in both cases, the second hand has simply fallen off and now slides around the inside the watch face, actually jamming the hour or minute hands, preventing them from rotating properly. This experience is not unique to me either, I've read on the internet of other people who have the exact same thing happen to their Uzi Protector. Also, the Tritium lume on this watch is VERY dim and is nothing like the Luminox/ Traser illumination system.

There is obviously some design/ manufacturing flaw with this watch so just do yourself a favor and don't bother with it.

Junk and a generous 1 star rating.

The watch does feel solid and i love the slim profile for a shock watch. Ive had shock watches in the past and they are usually uncomfortable bulky. Now for the issue. For some god awful reason Casio made the adjust button flat as opposed to all the other buttons which stick out. Im not sure if this is Casio thing or a independent feature for this model series. All i know is Timex and other brands i've seen dont generally do this. So in order to press the button down you need either a y poi object like a pen cap or paper clip. The problem with this is the adjust button is probably the most used button on the watch as it controls all the multi fuctions such as setting the alarm and timer. If you are like me and use these functions reguarly this is a major downfall and very frustrating. To conclude this review, if you are looking for a cool looking watch and rarely use multi functions then this is for you, however if you're like me and use the multi functions reguarly either steer clear from this watch or be prepared to always keep a paper clip in your pocket to operate it. This issue has frustrated me so much that I'm already back in the market for a new watch a week after my purchase of this item.

product_title: Casio Women's LCF30-1B Tough Solar Ana-Digi Sport Watch
review_headline: Solar cell doesn't last long enough
review_body:
It's a big watch for what is typically associated with women, but I'm an outdoorsy-type and find the size to be just right since it's still smaller than the typical men's sports watch. The second day I had this watch it informed me, by turning off at a rather inopportune moment, that it was low on power. In winter, sunlight for charging is a commodity, so now I simply take the watch off and let it charge under the bathroom lights while I'm showering in the morning. Since I've been doing this, no battery failure has occurred. The directions say that about 5 minutes of direct sunlight will charge the watch for a day, and that seems about right to me. I'm sure powering the watch will be a non-issue come summer.

UPDATE: After having the watch for a few weeks now, it has shut down 3 or 4 times due to low cell power.

Cons: There are too many unnecessary functions for time-zones, etc. I just want a single display that gives both the digital time and date in one window without fuss. This watch is either or. Unless you're accustomed to changing time zones on a daily basis, two functions will probably mean nothing to you: \\"DT\\" and \\"HS.\\" Another unnecessary function is the alarm. While it's certainly thoughtful, I can't imagine a time or a place now where alarms aren't taken care of by cell phones. If you are somewhere where a cell phone won't work, an alarm is probably not your first concern. I'd rather have some sort of lap counter, for running.

UPDATE: The glass face is also prone to scratching -- it sits \\"high\\" on the watch, with no protective raised cover around it (as in most other sports watches. This watch now has more face scratches on it than other watches that I've had for years.

Pros: The stopwatch is better than my Timex Ironman in that you don't need to hold down a button to reset -- just tap. Additionally, the watch lights up when it's dark and you turn it toward you, and the hands glow bright green after a nice light-charge. Solar power. Analog and digital at once: the analog could be useful for assessing compass directions (which you can't do with a digital-only piece), and the digital is always useful if you want to be exact.and digital at once: the analog could be useful for assessing compass directions (which you can't do with a digital-only piece), and the digital is always useful if you want to be exact.

product_title: Bulova Men's 98B131 Marine Star Black Dial Bracelet Watch
review_headline: Solid and attractive watch at a great price!
review_body: I found this watch after starting a search for a fairly inexpensive diving watch that was somewhat reminiscent of a Submariner but not one of the numerous homages and clones.  I was hesitant about purchasing this timepiece because I'm typically not a fan of polished links on the bracelet and I thought that the wave pattern on the dial was too prominent.  I'm really glad that I decided to get it, it the dial is understated, and the wave pattern is a lot more subtle than in the Amazon images.  The placement of the date window between the 4 and 5 o'clock markers is unique and another characteristic of this watch that helps to set it apart.  The band is solid and the polished links are a nice contrast to the brushed ones,  and link removal is easy using the [[ASIN:B00598QKMA SE Adjustable Watch Band Link Pin Remover w/ 3 Tips JT63056]] or any of the other similar ones available.        It has a pretty low profile compared to some of the other coin edge diving watches, but it has nice heft and is very comfortable.  The watch has some weight but is very balanced on the wrist and doesn't feel heavy after extended wearing.  It fits my 7.5\\" wrist very well, that's always a concern when buying a watch online, but you will be pleased with the diameter and case thickness if your wrist is similarly sized.  The lume on the watch seems to be decent.  I havent had it long enough to comment much on this aspect, but it has done well outside and in a dark bedroom.  I set the watch against an atomic G-Shock and the Bulova seems to be very accurate.    Don't hesitate to buy this watch if you are on the fence, it's a great value and really looks amazing on the wrist.

The luminosity of it lights up brighter than any other Wenger I have, and it's my favorite dial design. I went with this model (steel band) specifically because I wanted the utmost durability since I wear it to work, as well as a long-lasting band. (The stainless steel band looks just like a Rolex also). And it's water resistant to 200m (660 ft), how could you beat that for this great price?

In conclusion, it's the one watch that literally makes me smile every time I go to put it on every morning, and I feel proud to glance at it (trying not to stare!) to check the time after a hard day's work. Perfect watch, 5/5. I'm a longtime Wenger and Victorinox watch customer, and this is the best one I have. I only buy Swiss-made (or any other European) watches.

product_title: Swatch Men's SVCK4032G Stainless Steel Analog Watch with Gold-Tone Dial
review_headline: Super styling, solid and still GLITZY
review_body: After pining for this watch online, I physically went to a Swatch dealer and tried it on. Yes, it is a big watch--a boyfriend watch--in the style of those Michael Kors produces. (A boyfriend watch is designed to look as though your boyfriend took it off in a moment of eternal devotion and gave it to you to wear!)What I had wanted was a Michael Kors watch in white but after a lot of research into watch band material (ceramic breaks, acrylic takes on other colours and stains, so does silicon etc.) I decided not to invest that kind of money and risk disappointment. Because this Swatch is intended as a unisex watch, it is automatically way too large for a woman's wrist so assume it will need to be sized by someone who knows what they are doing--make sure they give you back the unused links to save in case you need them as replacements in future. The sales people at the Swatch kiosque I visited told me this is the hottest selling watch Swatch produces. It also comes in a slightly more expensive ROSE GOLD--though why this is more I cannot fathom--along with the regularly priced gold, red, gray, black,silver, brown and white. What I think makes this watch so cool is that there is opaque plastic surrounding the watch case--joining it to the band. The plastic lightens the effect of what could otherwise be perceived as a bulky, heavy-looking piece of jewelry. Instead, the plastic becomes a design element that makes the watch look modern. The catch works really well -- it secures the watch to your arm; so well that you may need help the first time getting out of it. All in all, I am very satisfied with this purchase and would recommend the full blooded product to men and women alike. The online price advertised by Amazon is better than the price offered at the Swatch boutique I visited in person. Just remember, if you are female, it is likely that you will need to have the watch sized when it arrives.

product_title: Orient Men's 2ER00002D Automatic Diver Stainless Steel Watch
review_body: I haven't enjoyed a watch this much in years.    If you are reading this review then you have probably studied up on this watch and its contemporaries.  I cannot speak much for the other watches, such as the Invicta model that this 2ER from Orient is often compared to.  But having read the reviews of this watch and the others in its class, I felt confident enough to pull the trigger for the Orient... and so far I have not been at all disappointed by my decision.    I think these watches would be flying off the shelves if there were better pictures available (at least on Amazon).  I think the Orient website has some pics, but a few more here wouldn't hurt business as this is one stunning instrument!    I will admit that the Orient kept irregular time the first couple of days out of the box.  I couldn't really tell if it was running fast or slow.  This may be due more to my not having wound it enough(?), however, over the past week or so I have noticed that it routinely runs 7-8 seconds fast per day when compared to my computer's clock.  This is acceptable to me but if it ever bugs me enough I suppose I can take it to the jeweler and have them slow it down a bit.  All in all, Rolex Submariner style and accuracy for a tiny fraction of the cost.      I love that Orient builds all of their automatic movements in-house.  Many of the high-end makes don't even do that anymore.  It may just be me but it gives this watch some status and bragging rights of its own :)    Did I mention the looks??? Very nice!    Okay, so many of you have read the other comments stating that this model sufferes from an uncomfortable band and poor illumination.  First, the band: It looks great and is actually comfortable to me.  It doesn't snag my arm hair or cut into me as some of the other fellows have indicated.  From that standpoint, I find it fits the bill just fine.  However, my only beef with the band is that the clasping mechanism feels extremely tight and not very substantial.  I've triedto \\"break in\\" the clasping functions but it still feels tight.  Maybe a drop of oil in the right place will do the trick... maybe a little more use and time will work this out.  At any rate, not a really big deal as I hardly ever want to take the watch off anyway, hahaha.  And for the illumination, I feel that it is adequate for me.  Once my head hits the pillow I am done so I cannot say I have really needed to read the watch much in the dark (but for the record: the one time when I did, I could).    I hope this helps you in your quest for the ultimate in inexpensive automatic timepieces.

product_title: Casio GW500A-1V G-Shock Atomic Solar Watch
review_headline: The Best Digital Watch I've Owned!
review_body: I've had many digital watches over the years because I like the alarms and timers.  I got tired of the dial window on my cheap models scratching because they were made of plastic.    I did some research and learned to avoid the cheap ones made of acrylic (plastic).  I started looking for models made of tougher glass which is easy to do here at amazon.  If you click on a watch for the description and scroll down until you see the blue \\"Product Description\\" on the left will be a link that reads \\"Dial window material type\\"   if you click on it reads:    The covering of the watch dial. Acrylic, mineral, and sapphire are the three types of crystals commonly used in watches. Acrylic crystal is an inexpensive plastic that allows shallow scratches to be buffed out. Mineral crystal is composed of several elements that are heat-treated to create an unusual hardness that helps resist scratches. Sapphire is the most expensive and durable crystal, approximately three times harder than mineral crystals and 20 times harder than acrylic crystals.     I was unable to find any made of sapphire and figured it very $$$ so I went with one made with a mineral dial window and am very happy. Its recessed and feels like glass and I'm not worried about it scratching.  The band is also made of very durable but comfortable material.    Here is the list of features:      * Quality Japanese-quartz movement      * Tough Solar Power; shock Resistant; auto EL backlight with Afterglow; 4 daily alarms and 1 Snooze Alarm      * Chronograph measures up to 110 seconds      * Time recorder; memory capacity: 30 records (each record contains month, day, hour, minutes, seconds); hourly time signal      * Water-resistant to 660 feet (200 M)    I often use count down timers with my watch but this particular model replaced the count down timer with a time recorder?  I have no use for this but guess it may be useful for some to record the exact moment 30 times?  Also if they deem this odd feature necessary on this model why not leave the much more popular count down timer?    That being said, it still has multiple alarms which I use and also has the optional hourly beep.    I like the look/style, the slight red with the stainless is a nice/unique look and worth the trade of the countdown timer.    Don't forget the solar power, atomic time keeping and the optional (I like it) auto back light which turns the back light on when you turn your wrist to check the time in the dark, nice!    I hope this was helpful (at least you know there is not a  countdown timer)  I'm considering buying a 2nd one of these as a backup, I like it so much!    Chet

product_title: Seiko Men's SNZG54 Sports Two-Tone Automatic World Time Watch
review_headline: Seiko Men's SNZG54 Two-Tone Automatic World Time Sports Watch
review_body: I have always wanted this watch. I searched all around the internet (eBay, Buy.com, Amazon, etc.) and specialty watch shops all over Los Angeles and Amazon offered the best deal at $117 and free shipping (I paid less because I used my Amazon Visa points).    The case is made of handsome stainless steel with gold tones. The silver dial makes it very easy to read the time and I like the bilingual (English and Spanish) day indicator. Furthermore, being in the airline industry and having friends all over the world, the world time bezel comes in handy when I need to check the time in the other side of the planet. The fact that it is automatic is a big plus, eliminating the need for annual battery changes. The total look is an elegant two-tone wristwatch with the necessary functions at the right price tag.    Seiko has always produced fine timepieces at affordable prices. Among the many Japanese watchmakers, I would put Seiko and Citizen at the top of the list. Of course, they are no match to the Swiss watches, but at $100 or so, how can you go wrong?    My only gripe about this watch is the small size of the dial. I wish Seiko had/has/will have a similar watch with a larger face. My wrist is not that big at all, but I like large watches -- they exude more masculinity.    Overall, the Seiko SNZG54 is definitely worth the money. For would-be buyers, I suggest that you search for the best deals around. I would say max should be $120-125. Some sellers slash their prices and some websites offer discounts. Of course, the lower the price, the better.

product_title: Baume & Mercier Men's 8670 Riviera XL Watch
review_headline: Simple yet beautiful, elegant and distinct
review_body: I spent a lot of time looking at watches, trying to find the right watch for me, something I liked, something my wife approved of, and something I could afford! The Baume & Mercier 8670 fits the bill; it is simple yet beautiful, elegant and distinct, unique but not too radical. It is dressy enough to wear to work, yet rugged and sporty enough to wear while sailing. While shopping for watches I spotted one that I thought was breathtaking. When I asked to see it, the salesperson explained to me it is a used watch, so the price is well under half of a new one. The cost? $27,000! The brand? Patek Philippe! Slightly out of my price range! But I think one of the reasons I like the 8670 is it has several features of that watch, the large bold roman numerals, and the crescent moon hand, which really stands out among watches. The watch is a nice size, big but not huge, comfortable to wear all day. The watch looks much better in person than in pictures, the center of the band is a brushed finish while the outer links are polished. The 12 sided shape (dodecagon) adds distinction close up but from a distance looks almost round. The screw down winder is nice and solid. If you've never owned a mechanical automatic watch, don't expect quartz accuracy of five seconds a month, they are typically more like five seconds a day! I found mine runs fast, so on the first of the month, when I set the date, I set the time one minute slow, so by the end of the month I am one minute fast. Not quartz accuracy, but plus and minus 1 minute is perfectly acceptable, even for an engineer! Bear in mid there are two very similar models, the 8670 and the MAO8670, one has a white face with silver hands and the other has a silver face with black hands. I preferred the contrast of the black hands with the silver face; the face is nearly white and looks really good in fluorescent light. And Baume & Mercier is owned by the Cartier Group...

review_body: The Omega Seamaster 2221.80 is my first big brand watch, so my I shant be able to do any comparisons with other timepieces in this class. I am, however, truly happy with this watch. It is stylish, sturdy, and, most importantly: it feels good. It is stylish enough to wear at formal events yet sporty enough to go with normal everyday attire. I have not owned it for long enough to tell you that it will provide fault-free service for a lifetime, but it seems nigh on unbreakable. If you need a little more light, there is a big snooze bar on the top, which when pressed, brightly illuminates the clock face. The clock is also very quiet, just as advertised. product_title: Casio Men's PAW1300T-7V "Pathfinder" Resin Watch
review_headline: Not the best choice for an altimeter
review_body: I received this watch as gift to replace an Avocet Vertech that finally died after 10+ years of hard use (cracked case).  Let me preface this review by stating that my primary need for this watch is for outdoor recreational pursuits, not as an everyday watch.  I much prefer a classic analog watch for every day use; this is kind of too techno-geeky for my taste.  As an everyday watch it's fine; as an outdoors tool I find it to a bit lacking.    The altimeter is good with some nice tracking functions.  I am wondering if it will prove to be as accurate as my Vertech (the chip in the Vertech is temperature compensated during calibration).  Digital compass is nice for general use or a quick check of direction but not good enough for navigation; I would still carry my trusty Silva Ranger.   The rest of the stuff on here is nice but to me it is just \\"fluff\\".  Atomic time keeping is great but to be honest, plus or minus a second or two really doesn't matter much to me.  The light feature is very nice, something my Vertech didn't have.  Solar power is nice, but replacing a battery every couple of years is no big deal to me.  The titanium band is a big negative for me.  Good for looks but not practical for use.  Being a bracelet, once it is adjusted to your wrist that is the only place it will go.  It will never fit on the outside of a shell or glove where I need it in winter when climbing and skiing. And in warmer weather I would rather not have a metal bracelet type band on my arm when having fun outdoors.  I checked with Casio about replacing this with a resin or nylon band....  Forget it, can't be done.  You have to order special parts to attach to the watch head along with special pins and Casio seems very reluctant to do this (one of the reasons I received this as a gift was it was advertised as \\"multi-band\\" and the gift giver thought it referred to the watch band).  Lastly, the functions on this watch are not very intuitive; this watch has an instruction manual that is153 pages long.  That's at least 100 pages more than I want to read to learn how to use a watch.  When I am cold, tired and hungry I want something that is easy to use, not have to look at a cheat sheet to figure out which buttons I need to press..    So for the bottom line....  I would return this if it were an option.  If your primary need is for an outdoors friendly watch that is easy to use, I'd give this a 3.  There are better choices out there for less money.  If you are into the latest tech stuff and are looking for something to impress your friends, then I would give it a 5.  I ended up giving it a 4.  Also this would be a good watch for a world traveler.  That being said it will never replace a dress watch or a nice casual sport watch in the looks department.  This watch is going to end up in my top drawer most of the time but will see occasional use when I travel.

product_title: Timex Expedition E-Compass Mens Watch T49531
review_body: Funny story, I tried to find this watch at local retailers.  At one point I walked into a very upscale Nasr Brothers Jewelers.  The kind of place where you find Rolex, Breitling, Omega, TAG Heuer, Cartier, Moldova.  The owner quickly comes up to me, and exuberantly says, \\"Hello boss!  What can I do for you?\\".  I said I was looking for a Timex, and he quite sympathetically replies,\\"I'm sorry, we don't carry Timex.\\" True story.    After shopping around online, I found that Amazon had, by far, the best price.    Anyhow, about the watch.  Overall I'm satisfied with this watch.  First of all, it has kept perfect time.  Six weeks ago, when it arrived in the mail, I set it to Universal Coordinated Time, and it has not lost one second.  Also, when you press the crown to activate the INDIGLO, the backlight remains illuminated for 4 seconds after release.  Another pro that I've noticed is that the phosphorescent hands are very bright and remain so for quite a long time.    The compass is a little odd.  It does not appear to be super accurate, but I suppose if you were lost in the woods it's close enough to steer you in the right direction.  The rotating bezel is cool, but rather useless.  And the two function buttons both activate the compass.  I mean, you've got two buttons, two features would've been nice.  Perhaps a stop watch or something.  The instructions on how to calibrate the compass were clear enough, I thought.  It asks you to set the watch of a flat surface, press the button to start the calibration, and then slowly rotate the watch too full revolutions in one direction, taking at least 15 seconds per revolution.  That's all fine and dandy, but I find it's easier to simply hold to watch level on your wrist and spin yourself around a couple of times.  I mean, as long as there's no one watching.    These little things aside, I like this watch.  It's big, and it looks cool.  I like the deep blue color of the face, and the shiny chrome around the numbers.  Size was the main thing.  I'm a student pilot, and pilots need big watches.  You can't have a tiny little watch that just tells time.  It needs to be like a wall clock that you wear on your wrist.    Not bad for the $78.70 I paid for it.  But as soon as I'm looking to pay at the very least $300 for a watch, I'm going back to Nasr Brothers.

review_body: I am a road cyclist.  It is helpful to know a few things about a given ride: the distance, the speeds, and the total cumulative ascent.  The total cumulative ascent (TCA) is the summation of the hill climbs for that day.  For example, a ride of 100 miles on the flat is a whole lot easier than one of 10,000 feet TCA.  I had a Casio watch which readily gave the TCA in 1998, unfortunately it was lost in Italy.  I called Casio prior to purchase of a new one and was told that the Casio Pathfinder PAG40B would do the job.  The watch does graph the altitude.  However, after hours of trying to obtain the TCA using the instruction manual and a phone call to Casio it would appear it cannot be done.  It is a shame; it is a good watch otherwise.

product_title: Fossil Bluetooth Mens Watch FX6001
review_headline: Works great, functional, enough geek cachet to impress most anyone (or make them mock you)
review_body: I've had the FX6001 for about seven months now, and I actually love it. It was a bit of a heartbreak when I realized it wouldn't work with my Nokia Symbian Series60 phone, (see discussion board) but the phone was old, and I wanted a new one anyway. I purchased the Sony Ericsson k800i (which I adore) and it worked perfectly.    Now check this: For the longest time, I thought that once it got out of sync (hard out of sync, more than 20 minutes away), it was a trip through the Bluetooth menu, and re-connecting/pairing both devices manually. I've discovered (and perhaps missed it in the documentation) that you don't have to do that at all. If you set the device to \\"always allow/authorized\\" on your phone, all you need to do is press the upper right button (which normally shows the time/date/checks connection status) two times, and voila, repaired.     Since I discovered that, the ease-of-use has gone up, and the annoyance factor at using its primary features has dropped dramatically.    I've turned off the out-of-range/depaired notifier because I cross my arms a lot and it sometimes loses sync and would buzz me (or if I was walking, occasionally), but as I mention above, it's able to resync automagically within 20 minutes, or by pressing the button anytime.     The caller id shows the name as you have it stored in your phone, or the raw number if you don't have it stored. You can send it straight to voicemail, after an initial \\"quiet\\" click, which is nice too. The battery easily lasts 9-10 days, and I don't mind tossing the charger on it when I notice the battery getting low--I just plug it into my computer's USB port and all's well.     I personally enjoy the style of the watch a great deal. I don't think it's nearly as cheap looking as others say, and I like that it's a fully-black, metal band. (Though the underside has some wear-off, from my desk, etc, but that's only noticeable to me.) The build quality is definitely high, and the glass face has held up to more thana few smacks into the stucco wall outside my house.    The display is easy to read and very cool, and when I was at Bloghaus at CES this year, it was a popular device to show everyone. I really enjoy the minimalistic approach, and that it serves its one function well. I'm really not a \\"smartphone\\" kind of guy, nor a \\"smartwatch\\" person, so I like it for what it is.    Reading the content of a text message might be a nice add-on, but I think it'd be cumbersome and slow, and you might as well grab your phone for anything of length. The buzz when you get a text is simple enough, and I actually like the fact that it will keep buzzing you if you fall out of sync and resync if you've failed to check the message. (It doesn't buzz for voicemail indicators, though, or multimedia messages.)    It should be noted that my USB-wall adapter doesn't work, and I've always needed to charge mine through USB. I was really very upset when I opened it and could *not* get it to charge, but I decided to try the straight USB approach, which thankfully works like a charm. Again, battery life really isn't an issue at all--the Bluetooth will last an optimistic week, and the watch has enough power to make it another week for time-keeping.     Overall a great watch that actually got me to buy a Sony Ericsson phone--something that's an absolute joy to use, I'll add. Definitely worth the buy, and much cheaper than when I bought it. (I preordered mine, and probably received one of the very first production units, since I was calling to bother them to ship!)

product_title: Pulsar Men's PF3223 Alarm Chronograph Watch
review_body: This Pulsar Chronograph timepiece looks great and is high quality. You should know it is made by Seiko. Similar Seiko Chronographs watches cost 3 times as much. The accuracy and workmanship are top notch.    The subdial indicators are easy to read against the white subdial background. This is a nice contrast to the main navy blue dial.    But...the stainless steel watch band with the small links initially seems a bit flimsy. However, the band is actually very strong and won't pinch your wrist if the band is sized appropriately. I was able to adjust the links myself without taking to jeweler. If I can do it...you can do it.    The alarm is very soft and may not wake you up from a sound sleep. Note: The alarm can only be set 12 hours ahead due to the functionality. I would rate the watch 5 stars if it wasn't for this.    You may also want to consider the Pulsar PF3093 Chronograph. This is essentially the same watch with a thicker stainless steel band. It is rated at 200M instead of 100M. The price is the same on Amazon but has a higher retail price.    This watch is a great value. You won't go wrong in purchasing this one.

review_headline: Poorly Made Watch!  Stopped working after two months!
review_body: I purchased this watch in early December because it was a good price, looked nice and had decent reviews.  Not even two months later, the watch stopped working.  It just died and the gears stopped moving.  I wear the watch every day and am constantly moving around the office, so I know it was not a charge issue.      The very first indicator of poor craftsmanship was when I noticed the watch was about a minute fast per day.  So, when it got to around 15 minutes ahead of time, I decided to wind it back to the real time, only to find that pulling out the knob slightly and twisting it would not wind the hands.  Finally, the entire pin came out of the watch and there was no real force used.  I've owned several watches and am very careful with them.  This should not have happened.  Now, Amazon wants me to contact customer service to try to get this resolved.  I can only wait to see what mess this will turn into.

product_title: Seiko Men's SNA617 Alarm Chronograph Watch
review_body: This is a solid, heavy watch. The movement is very accurate (and precise, if you are fussy about the distinction), although the alarm setting can be +/- one minute. The alarm is easy to set and emits a pleasant pinging, audible indoors but barely registers on a city street. The main disadvantage is that the crown does not screw down; after a month of wearing the watch, I bumped into a doorway and tore the crown off and had to send it for repair under the warranty (speedy service and turn-around). Before this, I wore a TagHeuer and find this watch better in legibility (esp. at night, with a bright glow even at at dawn),precision, and security of the clasp. The uni-directional ratcheting bezel broke on my Tag even after several repairs and is basically unreliable; on the Seiko, it is firm (but the polished finish on the edge makes it slippery to turn). Some of the black markers on the bezel have chipped off, which seems so improbably cheap - I'm waiting for the rest to go so it will look uniform. Other reviews have noted the watchband as lightweight; the solid link band on my Tag is heavier (and costs $300 to replace!), but the pin that secures it to the watch is \\"the weakest link\\" and not any better than the Seiko. Basically, I love this watch and for the price, feel confident wearing it for whatever activity, all day, every day for years to come.

review_body: I'm trying to decide whether or not this purchase was worth it or not.  On one hand, I needed a good watch that tells time and is black in color.  On the other hand, I have to pay child support.  I chose the watch because the return on my investment outweighed every other factor.  It was a no-brainer.    Pros:  It tells time good.  It's black.  Cons:  None really.    I highly recommend this watch to anyone looking for a timepiece that is capable of telling time, and is black.  However, you must take into consideration other responsibilities such as mortgage payments and lawsuits.  If you have the money, go for it.  It tells awesome time.  And it's black!

product_title: Mens Skagen Collectors Limited Edition Watch H450LSLW
review_headline: Great watch, but what's it all about?
review_body: This is a very stylish watch that is typical \\"Skagen minimalist\\".  It's a good size, very thin of course, with clear hands on the face.  No luminous features - you cannot read this watch in the dark :-)    The edge of case is split and has a series of \\"studs\\" around the circumference.  It's actually a nice detail and is completely in-character with the rest of the design.  You can just about see the detail in some of the oblique shots.    The strap has a suede-look central band (you can make this out on the photos).  I suspect it won't be all that durable but who knows?  Straps are easy and cheap to replace anyway.    At $45 I think this watch was a real bargain and I'm extremely pleased with it.    So what about the downside?  Well given how inexpensive this watch was I was tempted to give it five stars.  But this particular example is advertised as a \\"Limited Edition, Hans Christian Andersen\\" watch.    Unfortunately Skagen gives no information on this - which I think is a strange omission for a \\"Limited Edition\\" design.  It would have been nice to have just a simple sheet of paper in the box to explain what the writing was, and why it had been chosen.  Is it an original draft of \\"The Little Mermaid\\", or just his shopping list?  Oddly I can't even find this information on the web.

review_headline: So long as you are willing to throw it away when the battery dies
review_body: I've owned this watch for about 2 years.  Today the battery finally died.  No problem, I thought.  The number for the battery is nicely etched on the back cover, easy to find and read.    Where the watch fails miserably is in re-attaching the back once you've replaced the battery.  Unless you want to go to a watch store and pay extra $$ to have it professionally replaced, or have the specialized equipment and knowledge to know how to put the cover back on, chances are you will either break the crystal front or the watch entirely or never get the back cover back on properly.  After trying to pressure it back on with my fingers, I went on the internet and found out it was almost impossible to do so in that way on these watches.  Some success by others was had with padded clamps.  I don't have those.  I will not be replacing this watch with another Timex.  I've always owned Timex (good price for decent quality) but this was the last for me.

product_title: Tech Swiss Double automatic watch winder with built in MULTI SETTING SMART IC TIMER by Tech Swiss
review_body: I have two automatic watches, and would sometimes forego even wearing one at all because I had let them both run down (which takes barely more than a day), and setting the time, date, day, etc. was too much hassle. This winder is exactly what I needed. As other users have said, it's very quiet, which is a big plus. It's not 100% silent, but it's pretty close.    Loading the watches was slightly awkward for me at first, but after awhile, it got much easier. Each of the two watch-holding modules for the watches has an adapter that pops on or off to accommodate the size of your watch. The modules are covered with black felt on the front and rear to protect the watches, and have a spring-loaded backpiece, so you can compress it, slide your watch over it, then release. Insertion and removal of the modules into the winder -- with or without the watches -- is very smooth and easy.    On the rear panel of the winder, you can select clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, or auto mode, which presumably either alternates the direction or randomizes it. I've not sat there and watched to figure it out. Additionally, there are four timer modes (wind time/rest time): 33 sec./12 min., 10 min./90 min., 30 min./3 hrs., and 1 hr./3 hrs.    The construction appears solid and sturdy, but not overly so. This will never be confused for a watch winder costing $250-300. Aesthetically, the only thing I really don't care for is the cheesy \\"Tech Swiss\\" on the front (at the bottom) in a very lame Times New Roman-style font. It really lends an air of cheapness to the winder that wouldn't have been there otherwise. Apart from that, the unit is quite nice-looking (matte black and gray/silver), the door is solid-feeling with a full-length pin hinge, the lenses appear to be glass or heavy clear plastic/acrylic, and it's very stable when in use. Fit and finish is good.    Pay attention to the dimensions noted: this is a fairly large unit, about a foot in height. It's not something that will easily blend into the background on your dresser. The adapter is 110v only, so this cannot be used in 220/240v countries without a voltage adapter. Overall, a fine product and well worth its $34 price tag. Recommended.

product_title: Torgoen Swiss Men's T06202 Pilot Computer E6B Dual Time Zone Stainless Steel Watch
review_body: This watch is very well made. It's no lightweight, even the band is hefty, at 22mm wide and 3mm thick. Anyone with a large wrist would be comfortable with it in my opinion, the band out of the box was very long, longer than most other watches. I needed to remove 5 links to fit it, as opposed to the usual 3. I have it adjusted down to 7.5\\", it fits perfectly and sits well on my wrist. And the links themselves aren't small, and they're solid, not stamped or folded steel. All of the metal has a finely brushed finish with the exception of the back, which is polished with an etched image of an aircraft and the Torgoen name. Timekeeping is very accurate. The GMT function took some tweaking to get set just right, but every other GMT/24hr watch I own required the same attention. The orange color of the face isn't as vivid as the pictures make it appear, it's more of a \\"orange creme\\" color, just a little paler than the average orange peel. It's easy to read, and has good visibility over a wide range of conditions. The crystal is very slightly domed, I don't believe enough to make it more likely to be damaged. The hands, indexes and numbers are well illuminated, I've had it last as much as six hours. I'm very satisfied with the watch. I've spent much more on other watches and not been as happy, and will be buying more Torgoen in the future.

From rubber keys to a membrane to keys that glow in the dark to the current sleek hard plastic, it has been an evolutionary movement that progresses forward, sideways, maybe a little backward, but always going somewhere. I like this version. Instead of the previous paradigm of scrolling through the functions until you find the one you like, this model takes you from any mode to a homepage, where you can go to any other mode. review_headline: I gave this as a gift to my mother
review_body: My mother recently lost most of her vision in an accident.  It's amazing how the simple things she used to be able to do now cause her so much frustration. The watch I picked out is, by design, fairly comparable to others she used to wear - she can see enough to tell if the design is OK - she just can't read the dial, so that was important.  It is quite simple to use, which is good for a woman in her late 70's, and the volume is loud enough so that in most circumstances, she doesn't have any difficulty hearing the voice.    I can't stress how much the watch itself has made her life better - the independence she lost in the accident is, partially, regained.    Anyway, for the money, this watch is well worth what I paid, and I'm sure my mother would agree.

product_title: Skagen Women's 107SSSBD Stainless Steel Mesh Watch
review_body: I collect wristwatches and among them my wife and I have a number of Skagen watches. They always have leading edge styling which I really like and they are reasonably priced. I have found that they work well and for the most part I have been happy with them. I have found three negatives though. First, although the watches work well the company's quality control is not everything it should be. On quite a few of my Skagen watches the second hand does not line up properly with the second and minute marks on the watch face. So every time the second hand ticks it is between the marks, not on them. If you watch this for a minute it can be quite irritating. I have not had this problem with any of my other watch brands. The next thing is that my watch repair person tells me that Skagen has always been difficult to work with in getting parts to fix their watches and that recently the company has quit selling parts to repair shops entirely. Now you must send the watch to Skagen if you need to have it repaired. The reason this came up is that I wanted to get a new crystal for one of my Skagen watches and even to do something simple like this I had to send it to the factory. The last thing is that although Skagen stresses \\"Denmark\\" on its watches and in its advertising they don't make a point of telling you that most of the watches are actually made in China.    However, dispite these little problems they have good style and value for the money. I knew these things when I bought this watch and bought it anyway.

review_headline: Lovley Watch, hellish clasp, reasonable trader
review_body: The item is very nice indeed, classic style, simple and attractive.  The watch was very much cheaper from the US than buying the same model in the UK even accounting for postage.  Unfortunatley on arrival the watch did not work, a call to the seller led to them asking me to return the watch or else accept $10.00 to have the battery changed.  $10.00 would not have covered the cost of walking into a jewellers here and since postage back to the US was about £30.00, I engaged in further discussion the seller who agreed to pay teh postage for the watch to be retured.  This led to a tour of DHL's hopelessly ill informed depots, no fault of the supplier.  A replace was sent very quickly and worked beautifully, the only oddity is that the original instructions and those of the replacement were in Spanish, however instructions in English are available via the Skagen web site.  The remaining issue now is the duty for which I have been invoiced twice, once for the original watch and once for the replacement, this issue remains to be resolved with DHL.   I am very pleased with the watch, it is elegant and neat and works as it should, my only niggle is the clasp which is fiddley and difficult to secure and prone to catching on clothing and releasing as a result.  All in all a satisfactory transaction and and a very pleasing watch.

review_body: This is the same review as the ladies' version since I bought both watches as a gift set.  A great buy. The watch is indeed very, very slim. The colors are just as depicted in the Amazon picture. Invicta packaging is a huge bonus. Highly recommended.

product_title: Philip Men's 8253141115 Watch
review_headline: Beautiful watch - Looks classy and expensive

product_title: Bulova Women's 96T29 Leather Watch
review_headline: Perfect watch for me - but probably not for everyone.
review_body: This is a gorgeous, classy watch - it's versatile enough to wear with almost anything, and it's dressy without being ostentatious. At $55, it's a great deal, too.     A lot of women's watches are just too big and look funny on me, since I am rather small-boned and thin. This watch is pretty little, so it looks great on me. If you have large wrists, or if you can't see very well and want a larger watch so you can tell time more easily, this might not be the best choice for you. But for smaller women who have a hard time finding nice watches that don't make them look like they're playing dress-up out of mom's jewelry box, you can't go wrong with this one.

review_body: My wife tried this watch on and disliked it, because it was too thick. I also ordered a Baby G (white) and it is thinner and looks nice on me. My wife didn't try out any of the features of this watch, because she didn't like the way it looked.

product_title: Seiko Men's SGF719 Dress Stainless Steel Watch
review_body:
I'm just out of college and working and wanted to get a watch that I felt was professional but good for everyday use (buying multiple watches while paying off student loans isn't practical). I like the classic look that doesn't seem dated. I'm not into all the bells and whistles, just something that looks good and tells time. Also I was happy with the size of the watchface, full but not overbearing, because I am a runner, not a baseball player, hence smaller wrists. I feel comfortable wearing this to work, out on a date, or at formal events. I'd still use a digital for working out or strenuous outdoor activities, but this is good anywhere else.

Good weight, tasteful look, great watch. If you want a quality watch without breaking the bank, I highly recommend this one.

review_body: I have this watch too and fund it very funny, if you take the time then it is easy to know how late it is, I find all those watches very funny.

review_body: Solid little watch,   I liked the older black on black style as it was more understated.  BAND NOT REPLACEABLE.   It's a soft plastic and they become brittle and fail in about a year. product_title: SE 88 Watch Wrench, Adjustable In Box
review_headline: Works. Hard to adjust. Arrived needing lubricant.
review_body:
I had to laugh when I received this. It was all by itself in the box with a couple of packing plastic bubbles that only took up 1/3 of the box. The strange thing was the rattling inside as I was carrying it in! See the picture with the box cover under the bottom of of the box? That is how it arrived! No one bothered to put the cover on the box. The tool and 9 of the twelve bits were just rolling around in the box under the flaps, wherever. The tool box was undamaged (fortunately so were the tool and bits).
So I could not turn the adjusting screws for either the top or the bottom until I sprayed on some WD40. Then everything worked fine. With enough fussing to get the top pins at the right width and the bottom snug, I got the watch open, replaced the battery, and closed the watch. So it worked well for me.

product_title: Croton Women's CA201046SSMP Silver-Tone White Dial Watch
review_body: The watch is very nice looking.  I am pleased with everything except for two issues - 1)if you do not wear the watch for more than a day it stops and you have to reset it every time - such a pain, and 2) setting the date and day of the week is not easy to do - the watch does not come with any detailed instructions and it took my husband a few hours to figure it out.

product_title: Casio Men's VA510A-1AV Waveceptor Atomic Solar Watch
review_body: This is a fantastic watch. First, I think it looks more stylish than in the product photo on this page. It's also very lightweight. I looked at a few of the other Casio solar atomic watches and they all seemed to be too geeky (with the big digital numbers) or too big/heavy (G-shock and/or stainless steel), so this one is, in the immortal words of Goldilocks, just right. I don't know if I'll ever use the additional functions (alarm, stopwatch, etc) but it's nice to know they're available. To top it all off, it was only $79.99 from Amazon, and I like it better than some of the more-expensive Citizen Eco-Drive ones I was also looking at.

product_title: Tissot Men's T33758861 T-Touch Titanium Watch
review_headline: weak band, lousy compass, no backlight, fails too much
review_body: I bought 2 T-Touch watches, one for my husband and one for myself. They are wonderful pieces, with very cool functions, if they worked, like someone said in another comment.  My husband´s has failed twice already, once the compass ceased working and now it stopped altogether. Obviously it does not resist water not even to wash your hands which is absurd for this type of watch.  Mine has worked fine (but with minimum use) but the rubber strap (worth $115 to replace) just snapped off the watch and you could see the very thin rubber it had to hold itself on to the watch. The absence of such a simple thing as a backlight bothers me a lot, in the dark the watch is useless!  Definitely too expensive for the quality.  Not worth the Tissot name (I have other impeccable Tissot watches).

product_title: Invicta Men's 9210 Pro Diver Collection Automatic Watch
review_body:
December 27, 2008
Invicta take quite a beating in the reviews sometimes and I have played my part as they make a vast selection of watches, some of which are incredibly ugly or impractical. This one is beautiful though. It's one of those watches where the balance is just right. The band is good quality, it keeps good time (I have had it a week and it is still settling, so perhaps off by 30 sec. a day).
The bezel is not matte as in the photo, but shiny, so it compliments the center of the band. Apart from Invicta being inscribed on every single piece of the thing (side, the winder, the back, the face, the clasp and the inside of every single link... come on Invicta, you copy the Rolex Yacht Master and then defile it by putting your name on it 16 times) it's an understated watch. Great with jeans and great with a suit.

So I got the understated beauty of an eight thousand dollar watch for $65. I love it. You will too.

July 21, 2010
The date does not line up in the date window under the magnifier anymore, which is annoying and makes the date really difficult to read. Apart from that the watch is still in one piece and keeping decent time.

product_title: Timex T2M515 Mens Automatic Chronograph Black Leather Strap Watch
review_body: To answer the first comment this watch like all inexpensive automatic watches, is subject to being damaged by over winding.  I have owned this watch for about 1 week and have noticed after winding the watch manually to the 30 hour mark, then wearing it for about 6 hours, the power meter went to the 40 hour mark. I then took the watch off and gave the auto winder a rest for a few hours.  This action may have saved the prior commentors watch.  A watch with over wind protection will cost over $600.00.  All automatics including expensive ones have the following characteristics.  Do not set the date between 9:00 PM and 2:00 AM.  Do not expose the watch to high magnetic fields.   Overall this watch is thus far performing well.  The reason for not giving it four stars is that is about 50 seconds fast per day a compared to the WWV time standard.

review_body: After purchasing this watch as a replacement for one of my other watch's I kept it in a drawer for a few months before my other watch died. However after my first watch of 3 years died (a walmart special) I put this one into use. After 11 days I noticed it was broken. Apparently while I was washing my hands the button to set the analog watch fell off and water made it into the watch. For 100 m water resistance it didn't last a simple hand washing let alone anything at depth. Very upset especially after hearing Timex's logo for years. My first and last Timex I will ever buy.

product_title: Star Wars: Clone Wars Boys WD6664957AMC Digital Watch
review_body: Apparently, Amazon makes you rate an item with at least one star, which is why I went that high with this useless piece of junk. Yes, it only costs a few dollars, but my son waitied for it to arrive as if it were the hope diamond. We reverently took it out of the box, opened it, took out the instructions to set the time . . . and discovered that they are apparently for an entirely different model of watch altogether. The pictures and text refer to setting the time for a watch that has 2 buttons on the side; this watch has one and all it does when you push it is switch back and forth between the incorrect time and incorrect month/day. So, setting the correct time is impossible. My son took the crushing blow well, realizing that his longed-for Star Wars watch is a useless piece of junk. Whatever you do, click away from this screen right now and do not waste even a dollar on this item. Spend more and get a watch that tells time. That is what I am now going to do.

product_title: Casio Men's GW810-1V G-Shock Solar Atomic Digital Watch
review_headline: Great watch.... except one missing feature
review_body: I think this watch is great. I own the previous version of this watch. It is still running after 4 years of scuba diving, Playing in the woods & rain, working in my wood shop or doing yard work and on my workouts. The one feature the old version does not have is the count down timer. This model does. In fact the new model has most of the features the old one does and then some.     This version of the watch appears to have better power savings. In the winter long sleeves and shorter daylight required the old watch sit in the windows sill every couple of days. The new one has not faded yet and 22 Dec is only a week away!    The missing feature? No day of week! Yes there is a date, but no day... a little thing I know, but I lose track!    I like the watch otherwise.  It syncs with WWV every night.  The back light is bright.  The stop wactc and count down timer a very convenient.  The five alarms are very handy.  Alarm number 1 can be set up as a snooze alarm.  I would buy it again... just got to learn to keep track of the day!
